533519|2026-09.headline: L&T Finance posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹975 Cr (up 33% YoY) with credit cost easing to 2.46% and RoA at 2.60%.
533519|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record consolidated PAT of ₹975 Cr, up 33% YoY, with consolidated book at ₹1,36,635 Cr (up 28% YoY) and RoA of 2.60%. Credit cost moderated 8 bps QoQ to 2.46%, and NIMs plus fees held at 10.48%, aided by a 25 bps fall in weighted average cost of borrowing. Rural disbursements were deliberately tempered on monsoon-related risk, while Personal Loans stalled sequentially on partner-level Cyclops migrations. Management also flagged the draft IRDAI commission consultation as a potential revenue headwind, which it said it has not yet quantified.

financial_highlights.change: up 33% YoY; ₹902 Cr in Q1 FY27
up 28% YoY; ₹1,29,634 Cr in Q1 FY27
up 19 bps YoY vs 2.41% after macro-prudential provision utilisation; 2.48% in Q1 FY27
up 223 bps vs 11.31% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Rural Business Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹6,356 Cr (up 1% YoY); book ₹33,465 Cr (up 22% YoY). Collection efficiency 99.7%-99.8%. Drought-declared-area book about ₹1,033 Cr, or 3.3% of the ₹31,500 Cr rural group loan and business loan book.

segments.name: Farmer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,643 Cr (down 1% YoY); book ₹17,397 Cr (up 9% YoY).

segments.name: Two-Wheelers
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹3,170 Cr (up 26% YoY); book ₹16,158 Cr (up 24% YoY). 92% of disbursements in prime segment; Cyclops 90+ DPD about 1.2%. September 0 DPD collection dip attributed to a self-cure experiment, with October back near 99%.

segments.name: Personal Loans
segments.commentary: Record disbursements ₹4,233 Cr (up 45% YoY); book ₹18,664 Cr (up 72% YoY). Sequentially flattish due to partner-by-partner Cyclops migration; monthly run rate now ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, targeting ₹1,700-1,800 Cr.

segments.name: Mortgage (HL/LAP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹2,926 Cr (up 8% YoY); book ₹32,846 Cr (up 20% YoY). Launched Aarambh economical housing loans (₹20-50 lakh tickets). Management says LAP delinquency is about 10% of industry delinquency on its index.

segments.name: SME Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹1,820 Cr (up 24% YoY); book ₹495 Cr (up 27% YoY). About 80% of portfolio covered under CGTMSE.

segments.name: Gold Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements ₹3,237 Cr (up 229% YoY); closing book ₹5,043 Cr (up 242% YoY). 502 active branches after 172 added in H1 FY27; about 110 branches above ₹15 Cr AUM.

guidance_outlook: Credit cost to reach 2%-2.2% corridor by Q4 FY27.
RoA to exit Q4 FY27 at 2.8%-3.0%; Lakshya 2031 RoA target 3.0%-3.2% for FY31.
RoE target 16%-18% by FY31.
NIMs + fees to stay around the middle of the 10%-10.5% corridor for next couple of quarters.
Cost of funds: management expects 2-3 more repo hikes at most (December, February); base cost of borrowing now 6.95%; incremental borrowing yields up 30-50 bps.
Gold loan branches to reach about 800 by end-2026 and about 2,000 in the long run; Gold AUM target ₹40,000-45,000 Cr (14%-15% of AUM) by FY31.
Book CAGR of 20%+ over Lakshya period; Q3 FY27 expected to show strong momentum with rural disbursements rising from festive season.
Investor Digital Day on 15 December 2026; full Hercules agentic cross-sell engine by early December 2026.
capex_capacity: Sampoorna multi-product branches at 151, of which 33 integrated with Gold Loan business.
Plans for 500 Gold branches and 200 Micro LAP branches; branches reach breakeven in about 6 months.
Opex to stay elevated for at least a couple more years due to branch rollouts, but offset by Cyclops and bot-led collection efficiencies.

Payments platform: UPI stack live in closed user group testing; agentic commerce stack with Pine Labs to be unveiled at RAISE 2026; Prepaid Issuer licence applied for, PPI products targeted for FY28 subject to RBI approval.
demand_pricing: Rural demand muted; management attributes flat rural disbursements to both risk guardrails and weak customer demand after below-normal monsoon (87% of LPA). Kharif sowing down 1.0% YoY at 101% of normal acreage.
Personal Loan sequential disbursement flat due to Cyclops implementation; large partnerships now 40% of PL originations and expected to rise.
Yields: management says risk-based pricing has recovered 70-75 bps of the 75-100 bps yield loss from Cyclops migration in Two-Wheelers, and expects yields to hold up.
Management said the mix shift away from Microfinance (grew ~5% when market de-grew) and towards Micro LAP, PL, Gold, and SME should keep yields up.
Cost of funds: CPs rose from about 5% to 8% of mix; PSL share fell from 26% to about 23%; PTCs about 5% at cheap rates; base cost now 6.95%, first time below 7%.
Fee and other income dipped QoQ because about ₹4,000 Cr of excess Q1 liquidity earned lower income; normal range is 180-185 bps, and liquidity was 20-22 bps lower this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will the repo rate hike be passed through, and what repricing exposure exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the ~₹25,000 Cr variable-rate home loan book reprices. Asset and liability fixed/floating mix is matched; management expects NIMs + fees to stay mid-corridor of 10%-10.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did portfolio cost of borrowing fall 25 bps when only incremental borrowings are at lower rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management replaced high-cost WCDLs and term loans that were drawn during Q1 excess liquidity (about ₹4,000 Cr); average liquidity fell to ₹9,500-10,000 Cr. CP tenors were extended to 6-12 months and PTC and sub-debt were raised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI commission consultation a risk to the 3% RoA target, and what offsets exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact is not quantified and the draft is under discussion; SRO FIDC is engaging the regulator for a glide path. Offsets cited include cross-sell via Hercules, PPI and payments fee income, and a one-to-one retail insurance channel accelerating in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the exposure to drought-affected states and rural underwriting changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought-declared-area book is about ₹1,033 Cr (3.3% of ₹31,500 Cr rural group and business loan book). Guardrails tightened in those districts; no visible risk build-up per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Two-Wheeler collection efficiency dip in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was an AI-based self-cure experiment (self-cure about 43%, targeting 50%-55%) that overshot; October recovered to about 99%, and it is not structural.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Personal Loan run rate and outlook after the sequential flattening?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly run rate is ₹1,400-1,500 Cr, with interim target of ₹1,700-1,800 Cr; onboarding a new partner now takes 3-4 months versus 2 months earlier, and one large partner remains to migrate.

qa_highlights.question: Is there gold loan stress such as GS2 formation or bullet-loan delinquency?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are business as usual; about 15 months in, no loss episode; auctions recovered over 140% of dues. Early delinquency seen only in recent bullet-loan cohorts, per RBI LTV norms effective 1 April.

risks_watch: Monsoon and drought exposure in Karnataka, Maharashtra, AP, Telangana; rabi outcome and rural cash flows.
Further repo hikes (2-3 expected) and incremental borrowing costs 30-50 bps higher; sustainability of 6.95% base cost.
Final IRDAI insurance commission framework and resulting RoA/fee impact; management has not quantified it.
Credit cost must fall from 2.46% to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27; Personal Loan and Two-Wheeler collection efficiency after the September dip.
Gold loan book growth on new branches and early bullet-loan delinquencies on post-1 April cohorts.
Rural disbursement pickup in Q3 after guardrail tightening.
key_quotes: We would like to reiterate that we are confident of achieving our guided credit cost corridor of 2%-2.2% by Q4FY27.
As the framework is still a draft consultation paper, it would be premature to quantify the final impact.
I'm being very, very candid on the call. We don't want to overreact to that because it is currently under discussion.
It is born out of an experiment and it is nothing structural.
So, for us, LAP remains our least concern.
533519|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on franchise, asset quality and the Lakshya 2031 trajectory, repeatedly reiterating credit cost, RoA and cost-of-funds targets. Cautious and evasive on the IRDAI commission impact (declined to quantify, "don't want to overreact") and on the full-year cost-of-funds path, and candid about the Cyclops-driven Personal Loan slowdown and the September Two-Wheeler collection experiment.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIMs + fees at 10.48% sits in the upper half of the 10%-10.5% corridor, and management guides it to stay around the middle, while RoA must rise from 2.60% to 2.8%-3.0% exit Q4 FY27; base cost of borrowing 6.95% but 2-3 more repo hikes could add 30-50 bps to incremental borrowing.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Book at ₹1,36,635 Cr (up 28% YoY) with 20%+ book CAGR guided through Lakshya, PL run rate ₹1,400-1,500 Cr/month targeting ₹1,700-1,800 Cr, and rural disbursements expected to rise from the festive season, though rural disbursements were flat at ₹6,356 Cr (up 1% YoY).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding guidance (credit cost 2%-2.2%, RoA 2.8%-3.0% by Q4 FY27) rather than raising it, with the IRDAI commission impact unquantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost must fall from 2.46% to 2%-2.2% by Q4 FY27 and PL collections and Two-Wheeler efficiency after the September dip are unproven, and the IRDAI commission framework is unquantified.

rows.why: Risk-based pricing has recovered 70-75 bps of the 75-100 bps Two-Wheeler yield loss from Cyclops, and management expects opex to stay elevated for a couple of years offset by Cyclops and bot efficiencies.

rows.why: Base cost of borrowing is 6.95% (first time below 7%), but management expects 2-3 more repo hikes, with incremental borrowing yields up 30-50 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on credit cost, RoA and the Lakshya 2031 trajectory and on the franchise, but cautious and evasive on the IRDAI commission impact and the full-year cost-of-funds path; analysts pressed on the IRDAI impact and the Personal Loan and Two-Wheeler collection dip.

533520|2026-03.headline: Indiabulls FY26 PAT of INR346 crores; Q4 FY26 PAT INR195 crores (INR194.26 crores per correction) led by first real estate revenue recognition.
533520|2026-03.overview: Indiabulls Ltd (formerly Yaari Digital) resumed earnings calls after a long gap, reporting FY26 revenue of about INR879 crores and PAT of INR346 crores, with Q4 FY26 revenue of INR417 crores and PAT of INR195 crores. Management said Q4 was the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the books and that the group has exited digital lending and e-commerce after merging 17 group entities. The company now runs two verticals, real estate and financial services, with real estate expected to deliver about 80% of group profit. Management guided real estate profits to at least double in FY27 and triple in FY28, though it declined quarterly guidance. The transcript carries annotations that correct several figures (FY26 revenue INR880.78 crores, Q4 revenue INR418.39 crores, Q4 PAT INR194.26 crores).

segments.name: Real Estate
segments.commentary: Expected to contribute nearly 80% of group profit; total GDV potential about INR21,000 crores plus and sellable area over 1.1 crore sq ft across Gurugram, Mumbai and Ludhiana. FY26 sales about 21.6 lakh sq ft; revenue recognised on percentage-completion basis, starting Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Financial Services - Broking
segments.commentary: Profitable, with about INR28 crores PBT in FY26 from the offline branch business. Online discount broking being built with a new team; 28,000 customers added in Q4 FY26; Algo platform launched.

segments.name: Financial Services - Asset Reconstruction (ARC)
segments.commentary: Fee-paying AUM INR622 crores and assets under allocation INR3,794 crores; about 2,200 collection staff on payroll. Management said the first year is absorbed by collections against acquisition cost, with profits from FY27.

segments.name: SMB investment (SpringCash, US)
segments.commentary: Treated as an investment, not a P&L business; stake acquired about 6 months earlier at a $30 million valuation, with about $100 million of disbursals reported by the company.

segments.name: NBFC (legacy Dhani book)
segments.commentary: Loan book about INR1,000 crores with zero debt; no fresh disbursements planned in FY26 or FY27; book is in run-off and expected to be collected as loans mature.

Management said it is difficult to give quarter-to-quarter guidance.
Around 40 lakh sq ft of launches planned in FY27 with GDV of INR6,000 plus crores; future pipeline of 42 lakh sq ft valued at INR11,900 plus crores.
Over the next 5 to 7 years, management said it could easily cross INR1,000-1,500 crores of PAT (CEO's view).

Indiabulls Tower Prabhadevi (Worli) expected to take 3-4 years to complete; capex about INR600 crores; annual rent about INR1,000 crores as stated, corrected to INR100-120 crores based on market rates.
GDV conversion into P&L expected over about seven years, with construction money flowing into the balance sheet by FY30-32.
capex_capacity: Indiabulls Tower, Prabhadevi (Mumbai): leased commercial asset, about 2.5 lakh sellable sq ft, construction started, capex about INR600 crores, rental income from year 4.
Upcoming launches of about 40 lakh sq ft in FY27 (GDV INR6,000 plus crores), plus future pipeline of 42 lakh sq ft (INR11,900 plus crores).
Key FY26 launches: Indiabulls Estate and Club Sector 104 (over 75% of phase 1 sold), Indiabulls Heights Sector 104 (nearly 100% sold within a week), Indiabulls Green Avenue (plotted, NCR).
Management said 20% of GDV is typically attributable to JV partners.
demand_pricing: Management said launched projects have appreciated about 15% from launch price and it sees no price downward revision.
About 80% recovery on all sold real estate units; buyers who miss payment windows have units cancelled.
Management said the online broking market is large and an entrant with good product and tech stack can grow; broking had 'suffered' during three years of restructuring.

qa_highlights.question: What litigations and contingent liabilities exist across the 17 subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 17 subsidiaries were shut down during the merger, have no litigations or financial liabilities, and that all legacy cases are resolved.

qa_highlights.question: How is revenue recognised for real estate, and what drives PAT growth from INR600-700 crores to INR1,200 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on percentage completion. Growth is driven by real estate, with about 40 lakh sq ft launching in FY27 and a further 1.1 crore sq ft in hand.

qa_highlights.question: Is the NBFC book's debt, cash position and NPA known?
qa_highlights.answer: NBFC and group have zero debt; cash and equivalents about INR750 crores; gross NPA about 1%, with legacy losses written off and assets sold to ARCs.

qa_highlights.question: Are PAT guidance figures PBT or PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PBT and PAT will be the same because of a tax shield of about INR3,000 crores in revenue inherited in the merger, until PBT reaches that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and timeline for the Worli/Prabhadevi commercial asset?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction has started; completion expected in 3-4 years; capex about INR600 crores; rental from year 4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDV inclusive of JV partner share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, GDV includes JV partners; their share is roughly 20%, per management. Conversion to balance sheet expected by about FY30-32.

qa_highlights.question: Why has broking not grown relative to new entrants, and what is the SpringCash valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed slow growth to three years of restructuring and said a new online discount broking team is being built. SpringCash was invested at a $30 million valuation about six months ago, and management expects further fundraises at higher valuations.

risks_watch: Real estate earnings depend on project launches, approvals and POC revenue recognition; receivables may build ahead of cash collection, per the analyst's question.
Management reiterated no quarterly guidance; FY27 2x and FY28 3x targets are untested.
Legacy NBFC book (about INR1,000 crores) has no fresh disbursement; recoverability and gross NPA of about 1% are management estimates.
Broking growth lagged peers; new online platform and products are still being launched, with the UPI and PPI licences expected in the current quarter.
Q4 PAT of INR195 crores in the transcript differs from the corrected INR194.26 crores; the INR143 crores profit figure is not reconciled in the call.
Tax shield: PBT equals PAT only until about INR3,000 crores of PBT, per management.

key_quotes: Real estate is the dominant earning driver and is expected to contribute nearly 80% of group profit.
Q4 FY26 marks the first quarter of real estate revenue recognition in the company's books.
Recognizing that profitability and preservation of capital is non -negotiable at Indiabulls, we exited these businesses.
So definitely we don't see any price downward revision happening.

533552|2026-03.headline: Rupa Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.3% to INR441.5 crore on 9% volume growth, while FY26 EBITDA fell 11.6% to INR115.3 crore.
533552|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6.3% YoY to INR441.5 crore, with volume up 9%, and EBITDA rose 19.8% to INR55 crore as margin expanded 150 bps to 12.5%, helped by Athleisure mix. For full-year FY26, revenue grew only 1.6% to INR1,259.1 crore while EBITDA and PAT declined 11.6% and 12.9%, with margins compressed. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% (largely volume-led) and EBITDA margin of 9-10%, and announced a 4-5% price hike in April with a further 2-3% possible in June-July. Management flagged intense price competition, crude-linked raw material costs, freight and FX pressures from the Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume grew 20% and value grew 25% YoY; management credited it as the main driver of the gross margin improvement.

segments.name: Channels (exports / modern trade incl. e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Exports were 3% and modern trade including e-commerce 5% of FY26 revenue; management says all channels, including GT, modern trade, exports and e-commerce, need equal focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-12%, split roughly equally between volume (4-5%) and value/price (4-5%).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 9-10%, versus 9.2% in FY26.
FY27 advertisement spend guided at 6-7% of revenue, versus about 4% in Q4 FY26.
Price hike of 4-5% taken in April 2026; a further 2-3% possible in June-July 2026 depending on market conditions.
Management targets profitability improvement of about 50 bps YoY each year over the next couple of years, alongside 10-12% growth.
Gross margin of about 28% in Q4 expected to be sustained with the initial price hike, per management.

Inventory split: raw material about 13%, finished goods about 54%, work in progress about 33%.
Brand and development spend of about INR70 crore in FY26: outdoor about 50%, television 10-12%, print about 12%, digital about 4%; the remaining share was not broken down.
Management said the company is shifting focus from primary to secondary (distributor-to-retailer) sales and will maintain optimum channel inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR60 crore outlay over two years for manufacturing-cum-warehousing facilities at Hosiery Park, Kolkata, West Bengal, to strengthen in-house capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Advertisement spend in Q4 and FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 advertisement spend was about 4% of revenue; FY27 guidance is 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the US-Iran war and Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no direct impact on the business, but flagged higher crude-linked raw material prices, higher shipping and freight costs, and FX volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Price hikes taken and planned?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4-5% price hike in April and possibly another 2-3% in June-July, depending on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher gross margin driven by product mix, with Athleisure growing strongly in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term roadmap given low historical growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 10-12% growth for the next couple of years, with profitability rising about 50 bps YoY, driven by secondary and retail focus and a new retail team.

risks_watch: Price competition: management says pricing remains intense and any further price hikes depend on market conditions and yarn/cotton prices.
Input cost and logistics: higher crude-linked raw material costs, freight costs from shipping disruption, and FX volatility from the Middle East situation.
Sustainability of the Q4 gross margin (about 28%) and 12.5% EBITDA margin, given that management attributes much of it to Athleisure mix and initial price hikes.
FY27 guidance of 10-12% growth requires about 4-5% volume growth, versus 1.6% revenue growth in FY26.
Advertisement spend rising to 6-7% of revenue in FY27 from about 4% in Q4, which could pressure margins against the 9-10% EBITDA guidance.
Brand spend breakdown incomplete (about 20% unaccounted) and promised separately; new sales team impact not yet proven.

533553|2026-03.headline: TD Power Systems FY26 standalone PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; FY27 revenue guided at INR24bn-plus, with a Turkey LD penalty dragging Q4 margins.
533553|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income rose 35% to INR17.37bn and PAT rose 42% to INR2.18bn; consolidated PAT rose 36% to INR2.36bn. Full-year order inflow was INR22.38bn (+51%), with exports at 79%, and the manufacturing order book stood at INR19.73bn at year-end. Q4 consolidated gross contribution margin fell about 3 points below the 33-34% historical average because of a one-off Turkey contract penalty after components shipped from India were delayed about 1.5 months. Management revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR2,400-plus crore and flagged a large-generator capacity expansion (rotors, machining up to about 200 MW) with details deferred about 2-3 months.

533573|2026-03.headline: Alembic Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% YoY to INR1,838 crore; FY27 guided to low double-digit consolidated top-line growth with Pivya launch drag of 100-150 bps.

Reported PAT was INR203 crore, helped by a one-time INR101 crore tax adjustment, after a INR24 crore exceptional item. R&D rose to INR209 crore (11% of revenue) on peptide development and higher filings. For FY26, revenue grew about 10%, EBITDA before R&D was INR1,846 crore (25% of revenue), and reported PAT grew 16% to INR675 crore. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit consolidated growth, with R&D of INR750-800 crore and capex of INR300-350 crore.

533573|2026-06.headline: Alembic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore; FY27 growth guidance raised to closer to mid-teens on US Generics.
533573|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR2,150 crore, with reported EBITDA up 21% to INR348 crore at a 16% margin. PAT rose 12% to INR173 crore, held back by a higher effective tax rate of about 22% after migrating to the new tax regime. US Generics growth was raised to mid-to-high teens for FY27 from low-to-mid teens, lifting overall company growth outlook to closer to mid-teens from low double digits. Management said the US branded business (Pivya and two smaller UTI-adjacent products) is a drag on margins in the ramp-up phase and is expected to break even around year-end.

segments.name: India Branded
segments.commentary: Grew 7%. Animal Health grew 24% (about 22% of India revenue); acute is about 37% of India revenue. Specialty is about 60% of total revenue; Gynae, Gastro and Ophthal growing in line with market.

segments.name: International Generics (ex-US, ROW)
segments.commentary: Grew 37%. Management guides ROW growth of about 15% in INR for the year; new JV in Saudi Arabia and Canada, new Latin American territories.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Grew 33% in volume-led growth. FY27 guidance was about 10% plus/minus; management now expects to finish above the ~10% level.

Ex-US business is B2B and subject to quarter-to-quarter supply variance; management reiterated 15% INR growth for year.

533581|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 10.1% YoY to INR1,717 crore and EBITDA fell 43% to INR131.5 crore, hit by LPG and truck disruptions and rupee depreciation.
533581|2026-03.overview: PG Electroplast's Q4 FY26 was hurt by an LPG shortage in March that cut RAC production at Supa, a truck shortage that deferred dispatches, and about 20% rupee depreciation against the dollar. Management estimated roughly INR420 crore of revenue loss in the quarter and a PBT impact of about INR120 crore. Full-year revenue rose to INR5,288 crore but PAT fell to INR193.6 crore from INR290.9 crore. Management said channel inventory has normalised after April and May sell-out, and guided FY27 to better-than-industry growth with EBITDA margin recovering towards 8%, while declining to give a numeric FY27 revenue or PAT number.

533581|2026-06.headline: PG Electroplast Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 35.2% YoY to INR2,034 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.7% amid commodity and rupee pressure.

The company reports a net cash position, and the compressor, refrigerator and washing machine capacity build-out is the main medium-term theme.

533581|2026-09.headline: PG Electroplast Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.5% YoY to Rs 934 crore, with EBITDA up 54.8% to Rs 69.14 crore at a 7.4% margin.

Gross contribution percentage fell YoY, which management attributed to pass-through pricing, a mix shift toward low-margin electronics and memory-driven price spikes, while per-unit margins were said to be stable. 533655|2026-03.headline: Triveni Turbine FY26 revenue rose 9% to ₹21.81 bn, a record; Q4 revenue hit ₹6.8 bn (+26%) but PAT fell 3% on a ₹157 mn exceptional charge.
533655|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as satisfactory despite geopolitical disruption, US tariff issues and the West Asia conflict, with H2 revenue growing over 125% year-on-year. Q4 posted record quarterly revenue of ₹6.8 bn, with exports at 60% of revenue, but margins compressed on a lower Aftermarket mix, a low-margin strategic NTPC battery-storage order and a mark-to-market loss on the rupee. Q4 order booking rose 19% to ₹7.54 bn, closing order book rose 8% to ₹20.54 bn, and the enquiry book was said to have nearly doubled, led by the US and India. Receivables ballooned to ₹6.39 bn (84 receivable days versus 49), which management expects to unwind, though FY27 is guided to be back-ended again.

533655|2026-06.headline: Triveni Turbine Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19.2% to ₹4.43 bn, but EBITDA margin fell to 18% from 25.8% on export deferrals and low-margin legacy orders.
533655|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 19.2% YoY to ₹4.43 bn, with domestic sales up 27.4% to ₹2.4 bn and exports up to ₹2.03 bn. EBITDA was ₹797 mn (18% margin vs 25.8%) and PBT was ₹697 mn (down 20.1%, 15.7% margin vs 23.5%). Management attributed the margin fall to a higher domestic mix, export deliveries deferred by freight costs rising 3-4x, a near-zero-margin NTPC CO2 energy storage project, and legacy orders priced before commodity inflation. Order booking rose 6.1% to ₹5.68 bn, led by exports and aftermarket, while domestic and product bookings declined.

533758|2026-03.headline: APL Apollo Q4 FY26: EBITDA per ton above INR5,500 on lower volumes, while management holds FY27 guidance of 15-20% volume and 20-25% EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 volume rose 9% YoY and EBITDA per ton ran above INR5,500, with FY26 ROCE at 37% and free cash flow of INR13 billion. Volumes softened from late February after the Middle East crisis, due to steel and gas shortages, labour shortages and channel destocking, and April was slow at about 2.5 lakh tons. Management prioritised margin over volume and said full-year absolute EBITDA targets are unchanged. Net cash rose to about INR1,510 crore by end-March, aided by inventory reduction and better creditor terms.

533758|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 volume fell ~20% QoQ to 745,000 tons, but EBITDA per ton held near INR5,500 and management reiterates 20% FY27 absolute EBITDA growth.
533758|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volume of 745,000 tons was below expectations, down roughly 20% QoQ, driven by the UAE disruption (about 25,000 tons lost QoQ), weak SG Premium volumes against secondary steel, an energy crisis hitting rust-proof pipes and roofing (25,000-30,000 tons), and destocking after steel prices rose. Management says July volumes were up about 20% MoM at over 300,000 tons, and it reiterated 15-20% volume growth and above 20% absolute EBITDA growth for FY27. Working capital days remain below zero and cash was about INR14 billion at June end versus INR15 billion in March 2026.

533758|2026-09.headline: APL Apollo Q2 FY27 volume hit 960,000 tons with EBITDA near Rs 6,000/ton; management guides FY27 EBITDA up 20%, with the 15% volume target conditional on Dubai and steel supply.
533758|2026-09.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter on volume, EBITDA and net profit, with volume of 960,000 tons despite UAE operations being disrupted, steel shortages in the domestic market and container disruption affecting exports. Growth came from the APL Apollo brand and roofing sheets, where pricing and EBITDA spreads improved, while low-margin SG Premium and export volumes were deliberately not pursued. Management guided FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis and said Q2 EBITDA per ton of about Rs 6,000 is sustainable. Working capital days were stated as zero, and cash rose 15% QoQ to Rs 16 billion. Several answers on Dubai, SG Premium and volume guidance were non-committal.

segments.commentary: Capacity cited at 7 lakh tons per year (about 175,000 tons per quarter); Q1 volume was about 135,000 tons and the target for the current quarter is 175,000 tons. Mix is 50% housing, 25% commercial/industrial and 25% other industrial; thickness 0.4-3.5 mm; no commission paid to third parties.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Low-margin product; management declined to give volume guidance due to steel shortage and low margin. Management said it can sell about 200,000 tons if steel prices fall and that absolute EBITDA would rise as volume increases.

segments.name: UAE (Dubai) operations
segments.commentary: Volume at about 40% of past levels; current run rate about 100,000 tons per year against about 300,000 tons capacity. Brownfield expansion to about 500,000 tons by March 2027, with EBITDA of Rs 8,000-10,000/ton expected on new mills. Management says no losses there.

segments.name: Defence, aerospace and specialised tubes
segments.commentary: New specialised tube mill can produce up to 250x250 mm with 16 mm thickness; samples sent to agencies, with results expected in 2-3 months. Development items for ISRO and DRDO are in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA growth of about 20% on an absolute basis by March 2027; management says it may beat this if UAE operations recover in H2. Management said absolute EBITDA should cross Rs 2,200 crore this year (one analyst cited Rs 2,200-2,300 crore; Shaleen Kumar's Rs 2,400 crore reference was given by management as possible if Dubai performed).

Apollo brand and roofing volume growth of about 15% for FY27 (about double-digit in H2); management also cited 15-20% YoY growth for these two segments. Company-wide volume guidance not committed due to Dubai and SG Premium uncertainty.
Q3 FY27 EBITDA per ton expected to be above Rs 6,000; October described as good and above guidance.

533941|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 63% YoY to Rs 78 crore and FY26 revenue reached Rs 255 crore (+58%), with PAT of Rs 19 crore.
533941|2026-03.overview: Thomas Scott reported Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 78 crore (+63% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 11 crore (14.14% margin) and PAT of Rs 6 crore (7.71% margin), its 10th consecutive quarter of revenue growth. For FY26, revenue was Rs 255 crore (+58%), EBITDA Rs 33 crore (13.1% margin, +105 bps) and PAT Rs 19 crore (+51%). Management said some own-brand sales shifted to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at 30-40% below retail, lowering reported revenue per unit while EBITDA margin was said to be neutral. Working capital, short-term borrowings and receivables drew the most scrutiny, with management attributing much of the stretch to a fire-related inventory loss and March-clustered sales.

qa_highlights.answer: Mainly an insurance claim receivable of about Rs 22 crore from last year's fire, plus Rs 6-8 crore of statutory and financial deposits, rent deposits and supplier advances.

qa_highlights.question: Are the new footwear and premium categories margin accretive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said they will be margin and ROCE accretive, focused on premium brands with higher MRP, and run on partner manufacturing with minimal capital investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why did own-brand revenue fall QoQ in Q4 and how will the revenue mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to outright wholesale sales to marketplace distributors at a lower price; it said the own brand still grows and that EBITDA margin is unchanged on those sales. It declined to give a mix forecast.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and what is the sustainable debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-to-equity was about 0.3-0.4, expected to fall to about 0.2 after insurance recovery; management said current working-capital limits are sufficient and sales are concentrated in the last month of each quarter (70-75%).

qa_highlights.question: Is operating cash flow expected to turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Not in the near term: management said positive operating cash flow requires growth at roughly the 23-25% ROCE rate, and the focus remains growth without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables trend and is there bad-debt risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said receivable days fell YoY, over 90% of receivables are under six months, and uncollectable amounts are provided immediately; an exceptional provision of about Rs 1.06-1.206 crore was booked in the quarter related to the insurance claim.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: In-house factories are at full capacity; captive job-work capacity is used for the balance, and Sholapur is the main site for periodic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How are the two fire incidents being handled and when will the insurance claim be received?
qa_highlights.answer: The first Gurgaon incident was minor; the second was major and is subject to insurance adjustment. Management gave no timeline for the claim, saying only that recovery is expected.

533941|2026-06.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
533941|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.

segments.commentary: Revenue close to INR 25 crore, up 34% YoY, driven by online-first approach, rapid launches and data-led merchandising. About 40% of brand revenue came via aggregator bulk orders booked at wholesale prices under marketplace channel.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

segments.name: Women's wear (newer category)
segments.commentary: Piloted for about two quarters; management says most revenue so far came from testing. Cited as a growth pillar at around 13% of Q1 revenue per analyst question, not disputed.

Management expects healthy margins and aims for consistent EBITDA margin improvement through the year, but may reinvest margin in growth; the 12-15% EBITDA margin range was cited by an analyst and not disputed.
Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.

Manufacturing footprint across Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.

Capex is consistent each quarter but described as modest; the main effort is workforce hiring, training and line efficiency.
Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.
Customer acquisition cost is about 4-6% of GMV, with the quarter at the higher end; no precise CAC or payback figure was given.
Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.
Management claims demand exceeds supply capability.
Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.

534091|2026-03.headline: MCX FY26 consolidated revenue more than doubled to INR2,302 crore and PAT crossed INR1,300 crore, with ADT up ~2.5x.

Management said growth was both structural and cyclical, but declined to comment on April and May participation and said not every quarter will be a big jump over the prior quarter. Cost lines (product licence fees, other expenses, SGF contribution, software support) rose faster than revenue in Q4, and management said the focus is on efficiency rather than spending less.

534139|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 order intake hit a record INR 915 crore (+0.5% YoY, double-digit QoQ) but EBIT fell to INR 32 crore on gross margin pressure and negative operating leverage.
534139|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly order booking of INR 915 crore, with sales growing about 5% YoY in a seasonally soft Q1 and an order backlog of about INR 2,100 crore entering Q2, up around 33%. EBIT was INR 32 crore, lower than last year, as commodity inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, transformer wire) and legacy fixed-price contracts compressed gross margin, while employee and other costs rose faster than sales. Management attributed the margin dip largely to Q1 operating leverage and FX-driven import costs, and said pricing actions are underway but will take time to flow through. No numerical guidance was given; management said the balance three quarters should be good.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA rise sharply while work and consultancy expenses fell from INR 3,412 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR 1,536 crore in Q1 FY27 (standalone)?

Further marketing fees are expected from Africa Avenue, Vinayak Mandir, Sarojini Nagar (7 GPRA) and 1% on Amrapali inventory sales of about INR 4,000-5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone and PMC revenue growth look slow, and what are the FY27-FY29 targets?

Standalone FY27 revenue INR 13,000-14,000 crore; FY28 about INR 21,000 crore; FY29 INR 24,000-25,000 crore. PAT guidance INR 1,100-1,200 crore FY27, INR 1,300-1,400 crore FY28, about INR 2,000 crore FY29 (consolidated).

qa_highlights.question: Is the Business Park tower purchase a cash drain, and what are the cash timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the first 10% instalment is paid; the rest is construction-linked over about two years. Management said cash will go out as CapEx and cited an auction price rise from a base of INR 39,100 to about INR 66,000 on the ground floor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CPSE REIT plan, timeline and investment needed?
qa_highlights.answer: NBCC approved an SPV in principle, subject to ministry and DIPAM approval, to hold three rentable assets totalling about 75,000 sq ft. No timeline was given; management said a national REIT will be launched only after a considerable portfolio (across CPSEs, est. INR 40,000-50,000 crore across five or six REITs) is assembled.

qa_highlights.question: Why have big awards (J&K, MAHAPREIT, Supertech) slipped, and is funding the constraint?

Seed money is being arranged by NBCC on some projects and by clients on others; a HUDCO MoU is in place. Management revised awards guidance to INR 20,000-25,000 crore this year from an earlier INR 30,000-32,000 crore.

534392|2026-03.headline: Vardhman Special Steels posted record FY26 profit of about INR122 crore on 225,000 tons volume; EBITDA/ton guidance raised to INR8,000-11,000.
534392|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with profit of about INR122 crore and sales volume of 225,000 tons, in line with budget. The Iran-US conflict pushed raw material prices up in Q4 and raised gas costs, but gas supply was not disrupted. Management raised FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance to INR8,000-11,000 from INR7,000-10,000 and set a 2-year target of INR9,000-12,000. The call centred on a reheating furnace commissioned in March, a solar plant, a new 210x210 section, a forging project, and a planned greenfield steel plant with capex of about INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Automotive special steels (existing plant)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 225,000 tons; FY27 sales target about 250,000-255,000 tons, with 250,000 tons to be used for modelling. Rolling capacity about 180,000 tons was supplemented by outsourced rolling; rolling capacity rises to 270,000 tons after the reheating furnace.

segments.name: Forging (ring gears, Aichi technology)
segments.commentary: Project budget INR475 crore, now expected to come in below that; about INR80 crore spent so far. First line targeted for Jan-Mar 2028 start, with ramp-up in FY29; plans for at least 3 lines.

segments.name: Greenfield steel plant
segments.commentary: Capacity 500,000-600,000 tons; commissioning targeted July 2029; land acquisition expected to close in May 2026. Ramp-up budgeted at 5-6 years to full utilisation.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance INR8,000-11,000; INR9,000-12,000 targeted in about 2 years, with management saying this could be a more confident range.
FY27 rolled volume target about 250,000-255,000 tons; for modelling, management asked analysts to use 250,000 tons, with a static 270,000-275,000 tons thereafter for the existing plant.

Melt shop currently under 300,000 tons licence; expansion to about 360,000 tons needs environmental clearance (50-50 chance, decision expected before March 2027); if approved, commissioning late CY27.
Price increases sought from Q1 FY27 to pass through higher scrap costs; discussions ongoing.
Government incentives expected at about INR12-13 crore in FY27, as the GST refund scheme ends Aug 2026 and electricity duty exemption runs to Aug 2029.
Equity infusion of about INR1,200 crore (INR385 crore already in, about INR800 crore to come), plus about INR1,200 crore debt; peak debt/equity below 0.75, comfort at 0.5.
capex_capacity: Reheating furnace commissioned March 2026, lifting rolling capacity to 270,000 tons; 9 crore units/year solar plant commissioned in Q4; new 210x210 section added to improve cast productivity and reduce rework.
Heat size raised from 37 tons to 40 tons; new NDT line and new peeling line in progress; Kocks Block commissioned.
Melt shop: plan to raise melting from 300,000 to about 360,000 tons, subject to environmental approval; equipment lead time 1-1.5 years.

Capex FY27 about INR100 crore (mostly land and development for the new plant, plus normal/replacement capex); FY27-28 expansion capex about INR700-800 crore, plus about INR100 crore for the existing plant and INR80-100 crore more if environmental approval comes.

Committed investment about INR2,600 crore through FY30: about INR2,000 crore for the steel plant and INR475 crore for forging; further specialised-alloy investments (ESR, VAR, VIM) still to be planned.
demand_pricing: Pricing works on spreads, not commodity prices; alloy steel prices rise less than commodity steel when scrap rises and fall less when scrap falls. Management said average selling price fell in FY26 versus FY25 despite higher volume.
Exports to be mainly indirect, via components from India to global OEs and EU FTA/CBAM benefits; direct export share to stay low. Luxury OEs such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz may give better prices.
Forging customer validation: Maruti Suzuki wants to see the factory running before validation; Aichi-linked approvals may be faster.
Management sees tool and die steel imports of about INR1,000 crore/year as an opportunity for future ingot-casting products.
Product mix expected to stay similar for the foreseeable future; a dip is likely when the new plant ramps up.

qa_highlights.question: What volume should be modelled for rolled products and is 250,000 tons sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said keep 250,000 tons for FY27 (target 255,000), with 270,000-275,000 tons from the following year and static at that level for existing plant modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA/ton be in the 8,500-11,000 range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed guidance of INR8,000-11,000 for this year, moving to INR9,000-12,000 in about 2 years; FY26 averaged above INR8,500.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of FY26 capex and how much will the forging project cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Kocks Block, reheating furnace, warehouses and land were the main items. Forging budget INR475 crore, spend so far about INR80 crore; expected to finish below budget, with more precise figures in about 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the expected FY27/FY28 capex and funding plans?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR100 crore; FY27-28 about INR700-800 crore for expansion. Debt/equity to stay below 0.75; about INR1,200 crore equity (INR385 crore in, Vardhman Group INR300-400 crore, Aichi, possible QIP) and about INR1,200 crore debt.

qa_highlights.question: What are government incentives and will the new plant get PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: No PLI for the new plant; it will be under the Punjab scheme. Incentives about INR12-13 crore in FY27 versus INR24 crore in FY26, as the GST refund ends Aug 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What ROCE is expected after the new plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes EBITDA on capital employed stays above 20% once plants reach full utilisation; below 20% it would not make sense to keep investing.

qa_highlights.question: What components will the forging plant make and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Ring gears for cars, using an Aichi process; one line initially versus Aichi's 9 lines. Management declined to give asset-level detail.

risks_watch: Environmental approval for the melt shop expansion to 360,000 tons is uncertain (management puts it at 50-50); Ludhiana is in a critically polluted zone.
Forging ramp-up depends on customer validation; Maruti Suzuki will validate only after seeing the factory operating; FY29 is the first year of meaningful forging volume.
Greenfield plant timeline (July 2029) and 5-6 year ramp-up carry execution and cost risk; capex figures are described as rough ballpark estimates.
Raw material and gas cost volatility from the Iran-US conflict; management flagged possible global recession and high oil prices as factors affecting the EBITDA range.
Dilution and funding: about INR800 crore equity still to come, including a possible QIP, and about INR1,200 crore debt to raise.
Expiry of the GST refund incentive in Aug 2026 lowers FY27 subsidy income to about INR12-13 crore.

534392|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
534392|2026-06.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.

Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

534392|2026-09.headline: Vardhman Special Steels Q2 FY27 PAT rose about 50% YoY on sales up 27%, with EBITDA per ton at the top of the INR9,000–12,000 guided range.
534392|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, with total sales up 27% YoY, revenue from operations up 39% and EBITDA and PAT each up about 50%. Strong automotive demand and tight supply after unscheduled shutdowns at a large competitor drove price increases over the last two quarters, and management said EBITDA per ton is currently at the high end of its range, partly due to inventory gains it called non-sustainable. The greenfield steel plant (INR2,000 crore cost, now expected to be higher), the forging plant and the brownfield expansion from 300,000 to 360,000 tons remain in progress, with the environmental approval still pending. Management also flagged a possible shift to 1:1 debt-equity, a rights issue in 2H CY27, and a possible dividend suspension for 3–4 years, to be decided at the April board meeting.

534425|2026-03.headline: Speciality Restaurants Q4 FY26 revenue up 13.65% YoY and PAT up 44.20%, with SSG of 2.25% for the quarter and 11.57% in April.
534425|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue growth of 13.65% YoY and PAT growth of 44.20%, helped by 2.25% same-store sales growth and gross margin expansion from 69.1% to 70.4%. Full-year SSG was 1.49%, and April SSG reached 11.57%, which management attributed to higher dine-in covers and refurbishments of older restaurants. Management guided to about 15% top-line growth in FY27 and about 15-16% EBITDA growth on revenue, with 32 new outlets planned. On the cost side, the company took a 4% price increase and moved 78% of its kitchens off LPG/PNG to induction, targeting 100% within 20 days.

segments.commentary: Walters AOV is about INR 700 and Sweet Bengal about INR 400 per cover. Plans include 15 new Walters (to 20 total) and 10 new Sweet Bengal outlets in FY27, with Sweet Bengal rebranding and FMCG packaging planned.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 SSG was 2.25% and full-year FY26 was 1.49%. Management said April SSG was 11.57%, driven by more dine-in covers, and blamed slow growth on unrenovated restaurants, with refurbishments now under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the restaurant-level economics for top brands?
qa_highlights.answer: For a 2,500-3,000 sq ft store, revenue is INR 8-9 crores a year with 22% restaurant EBITDA before rent. Rent is about 20-21% of revenue (revenue-share triggers at 17-18%), leaving about 15% post-rent EBITDA. Breakeven takes 4-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing LPG and fuel supply, and what does induction cost?
qa_highlights.answer: The company started the transition on 4 March and imported wok-based induction sets (around 300). It has 78% of the chain off fuel, targeting 100% in 20 days. Management said induction cost is the same or lower, with a 6% saving in a pilot restaurant from avoiding pilot-flame wastage.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on fewer brands, given that the bottom 8 brands contribute under 10% each?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed seven focus brands (Mainland China, Asia Kitchen, Haka, Gong, Siciliana, Walters, Sweet Bengal). Other brands are profitable and will not be shut, but no further expansion is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration, given the cash pile and the share price correction?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the question would be taken up by the Board and it was too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: How can FY26 cash flow (about INR 80 crores CFO less about INR 50 crores rent) reconcile with a 15% EBITDA margin claim?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the 15-16% figure is at restaurant level after rent. Cash-flow EBITDA is after corporate costs, which fell to about 4% of revenue from 6-7% as the company resumed expansion.

534600|2026-03.headline: JTL Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to INR693 crore on a record 1,23,262 MT quarterly volume; FY27 guided to about 30% volume growth.
534600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR693 crore (up 47.5% YoY, 47.2% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR58 crore and PAT of INR38 crore, and the company reported record quarterly and annual volumes. Management attributed the volume jump mainly to higher utilisation at the Mangaon facility and DFT structural steel pipes, with no channel-inventory gain. FY26 totals were revenue INR2,136 crore, EBITDA INR166 crore, PAT INR103 crore and volume 3,95,900 MT. Management guided to about 30% FY27 volume growth, while the 2 million tonne capacity target by FY27 was reiterated but the Aryan Bhatia question flagged that the earlier 6 lakh tonne FY27 guidance has effectively been reduced after capex delays.

segments.name: Mangaon facility (Maharashtra)

segments.name: DFT structural steel pipes
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q4 and exports; being empanelled with customers, and ACRS certification obtained for Australia, with US and Canada being explored.

segments.name: JTL Defence (formerly RCI Industries; copper, brass, phosphor bronze alloys)

ROCE expected to recover to about 25-30% in coming years as CWIP assets are capitalised; operating cash flow expected positive by FY28 (next financial year).
JTL Defence: 10-15% EBITDA margin targeted in coming quarters; defence capacity of 700-800 MT/month by FY29.
capex_capacity: Mangaon cold rolling complex (color-coated pipes, GT pipes) with 7 lakh tonne outlay; nearing completion, full running by end of H1 FY27.
Company capacity to rise from 1 million tonnes to 2 million tonnes; majority capex done, remaining about INR60-70 crore in H1 FY27.
All further capacity addition is at Maharashtra; no other facility additions planned.
Utilisation guidance not given for FY27 because new products keep starting at different rates; to be updated next quarter.
Capacity delays attributed to rains and complexity of the color-coated capex; the outlook timeline has slipped as a result.
demand_pricing: Management says market is on a good track after the November duty introduction led to price corrections, then price rises and stocking; a slowdown in the first week of the quarter due to state elections, followed by a pick-up.

Export margin is not superior to domestic; export premium is roughly INR6,000-8,000/ton at the general level, with the benefit being volume scale rather than margin.

qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA/ton expected at INR4,500-4,800 (10-15% growth); ROCE expected at 25-30% over the coming years as assets are capitalised.

There is no absolute inventory gain in this quarter.

534600|2026-06.headline: JTL Industries Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR722 crore with EBITDA INR59 crore (8.1% margin) and volumes up 17.8% YoY to 118,513 MT.
534600|2026-06.overview: JTL Industries reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA in Q1 FY27, with revenue of INR722 crore, EBITDA of INR59 crore and PAT of INR35 crore (4.9% margin). PAT absorbed INR2.8 crore of extra non-cash depreciation from the March 2026 revaluation at JTL Defence. Operational EBITDA per ton excluding other income was INR4,954, which management attributed to product mix and efficiency; it said JTL Defence added about INR200 per ton to consolidated figures. Management reiterated FY27 volume growth of at least 30%, with Mangaon capacity expansion of about 1 million tons targeted by end H1 and capex of about INR100 crore left to reach 2 million tons.

segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton about INR4,750 excluding JTL Defence; DFT structural pipes now running at 20,000-25,000 tons per quarter, roughly double the prior ~10,000 tons. Mangaon facility utilisation about 42%.

segments.name: JTL Defence (ex-RCI Industries & Technologies)
segments.commentary: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, with about 120 MT in the first month of Q2. Q1 EBITDA margin about 12%, versus about 20% in Q4 which included inventory gains. Management targets 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27 and INR150 crore top line this year.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential at peak utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.4 million tons at INR65,000-66,000/ton, roughly INR9,100 crore on the current capex cycle.

qa_highlights.question: JTL Defence guidance and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about 100 MT/month in Q1, about 120 MT in the first month of Q2; target 500 MT/month by Q4 FY27. Long-term margin 15%, with 10-15% expected over time.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Cycle down to about 75 days from 90; target 35-40 days by FY28, helped by dealer financing and a shift away from government receivables.

So, it's safe to say that 30% will be automobile and dealer network, 35% will be defense and the remaining will be mint factories.

534618|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 131.31% YoY to INR 1,102.40 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.76%, while FY26 order book stood at 2.83 GW peak.

Order inflow was flat-to-lower (about 2.3 GW vs 2.4 GW in FY25) and the order book fell from about 3.2 GW to 2.8 GW year on year. Management guided to a sustained EBITDA margin above 15%, with FY26 margin above 19.24%, and is self-funding a 54 MWp IPP fleet plus about 227 MWp under construction.

534748|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19.45% QoQ to INR 287.70 crore and EBITDA margin to 17.41%, with net profit at INR 12.37 crore.
534748|2026-03.overview: Total income for Q4 FY26 was INR 287.70 crore, up 19.45% QoQ from INR 240.86 crore. EBITDA rose 118.12% QoQ to INR 50.10 crore, with margin up 788 bps to 17.41%. Net profit was INR 12.37 crore versus INR 2.28 crore in Q3, with a 4.30% net margin. For FY26, total income was INR 1,066.42 crore, EBITDA INR 138.03 crore and net profit INR 26.99 crore. Management said it redeemed INR 43.19 crore of NCDs in one tranche and cut debt by nearly INR 68 crore over the last two quarters.

segments.name: TMT rebar / long products (Simhadri brand)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 rebar volume was 49,760 tonnes, up from about 39,000 t in Q3. Management said the average EBITDA per tonne was about INR 9,000-9,500 in the last quarter versus about INR 6,000 in earlier quarters, and about INR 6,800-7,000 on a yearly average.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Power segment revenue fell in FY26. Management attributed this to kiln refurbishments; it expects data-centre tie-ups and capacity expansion to improve consumption.

segments.name: Logistics (SEIL Logistics and Infra Company)
segments.commentary: A subsidiary formed to run a private freight terminal and logistics at Visakhapatnam, with railway sidings. MoUs with the Andhra Pradesh government cover about 150 acres adjacent to the existing land.

guidance_outlook: Management said Q4 FY26 is 'fine' but later years should be better; it expects steady margins while the market stays buoyant.
Management expects FY27 volumes to roughly double once the reheating furnace and capacity expansion come on stream from Q2 FY27, with capacity mostly doubled.
Sustainable EBITDA guidance given as about INR 7,000 per tonne on average volumes of 40,000-50,000 tonnes per quarter.

Finance cost is expected at about INR 12-13 crore per quarter, not below 10, after the new loan costs and trade finance charges fall away. Refinancing is targeted to bring the cost of debt to about 9%.

Existing capex (reheating furnace, furnace refurbishment, kiln work) is to be completed in FY27. New greenfield capex for the 1 million tonne green steel plant is about one year away, pending groundbreaking and the strategic investor's inputs.
Pledged shares are expected to be released once refinancing is complete and IMR funds are received.
capex_capacity: A reheating furnace is being installed, expected to start from Q2 FY27 and to add about 50,000 tonnes of new bar capacity. Management said it will raise rolling mill efficiency by 30-40%.
Billet and rebar capacities were raised by about 44-45% at the end of FY25. Utilisation is about 46-47% for rebar and 55-56% for billet, with a target of 70-75% in FY27.
Expansions already under way are expected to be operational by end-July 2026.
Land bank: about 400-450 acres existing; another 150 acres targeted for the logistics park and 150 acres for steel manufacturing. MoUs cover a 1 million tonne green steel plant.
Planned capex and debt paydown are to be funded from INR 300 crore of share warrant money from IMR Group and internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Management said the Indian steel outlook is strong, citing infrastructure, housing, railways, defence and import substitution. It also said Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam projects (Google AI hub, ArcelorMittal, Amaravati) are sources of demand, and that the company is an approved vendor for them.
April 2026 sales were described as 'great' and May as slightly weaker due to heatwave and the war situation. Management expects a June recovery.
Management said the company is largely insulated from the ongoing war, except for some diesel cost in transport. Coal, iron ore and scrap are sourced locally.
The company was re-empanelled under MES for TMT bar supplies to the Ministry of Defence.

qa_highlights.question: What does the company plan to fund its capacity growth and reduce its debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has MoUs with state governments for expansion and a 1 million tonne green steel plant. Project reports are pending, and the plan is to announce them once formalised.

qa_highlights.question: When is the balance payment expected from IMR on the share warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 300 crore warrant subscription is expected within about six months and will fund growth, including green steel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost trend, and why did it rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 finance cost was INR 7.50 crore, not INR 17 crore. The analyst then cited Q3 at INR 13 crore and Q4 at INR 17 crore; management attributed the difference to new loan processing costs and supplier trade finance. Term debt has fallen from about INR 350 crore to INR 250 crore, and current debt is about INR 270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What were rebar volumes and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 FY26 rebar sales were 49,760 tonnes. Management said FY27 capacity is expected to roughly double from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity utilisation and when will it reach 85-90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebar utilisation is about 46-47% and billet about 55-56%. Management expects 70-75% in FY27 after the reheating furnace is commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the company's shares 100% pledged, and will this change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is linked to past bank exposure. It expects the pledge to be released after refinancing, to a debt cost of about 9%, and once IMR funds are received.

Demand softness in May 2026 due to heatwave and war-related conditions.

534816|2026-03.headline: Indus Towers Q4 FY26: reported EBITDA INR 44.6bn (+1.6% YoY, 55.1% margin) and FY26 final dividend of INR 14/share distributing full-year FCF of INR 37.6bn.
534816|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 81bn (+4.8% YoY) and core rental revenue INR 53.1bn (+5.4% YoY), with co-locations up 5.6% YoY. Reported EBITDA was flat-to-up YoY but down 1% QoQ, held back by a Q4 one-time settlement hit to revenue, a Q3 positive one-off in other expenses, and higher seasonal maintenance spend. Full-year PAT fell 28.1% YoY to INR 71.4bn because FY25 carried a INR 51bn receivables write-back; normalised EBITDA and PAT grew 11.4% and 13%. The Board recommended a final dividend of INR 14/share, distributing the full FY26 free cash flow, with management guiding to a steady and progressive payout going forward.

financial_highlights.value: INR 11.1bn in Q4; INR 37.6bn in FY26

segments.name: Towers and co-locations (India)
segments.commentary: Q4 added 4,892 macro towers and 6,192 co-locations, taking the base to about 264,500 towers and 428,000 co-locations (+6.1% and +5.6% YoY). Tenancy ratio stable at 1.62; leaner-tower co-locations exceed 14,000, portfolio about 442,000 including leaner towers.

segments.name: Energy
segments.commentary: Energy revenue fell QoQ on cost optimisation and seasonal energy cost decline; energy margin -3.6% in Q4 vs -5.2% a year earlier. Solar access added at about 2,500 sites in Q4, taking the total to about 42,400; diesel consumption down about 7% YoY.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Operating licence secured in Zambia with on-ground execution starting; Uganda and Nigeria in final regulatory stages. Commercial frameworks and initial orders in place with the anchor customer; capex for Africa described as not significant initially.

segments.name: Non-tower / DAS / IBS
segments.commentary: Company says it reached leadership in IBS in Q4; DAS deployments picked up in metros, tunnels and highways. No figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Final dividend of INR 14/share recommended; management says the endeavour is steady and progressive distribution, with no minimum payout formula (dividend policy: FCF distributed at year-end, subject to working capital).
Management does not give forward numbers; says order book is healthy for the next few quarters with growth-oriented capex (about 70% of capex is growth, about 25% replacement/maintenance).
Full-year EBITDA margin said to be in line with the 55%-plus expectation.
Africa tower deployment expected to begin soon in Zambia, with ramp-up as approvals come through in Uganda and Nigeria.
capex_capacity: Q4 tower additions 4,892 and co-location additions 6,192; FY26 full-year additions about 15,200 towers and 22,500 co-locations.
Over 85% of sites digitally connected (fuel sensors, backhaul monitoring, smart meters, power equipment).
About 531,000 5G BTSs installed in the base; growth expected from loading on existing towers, with selective tower footprint expansion later.
Management flagged supply-side tightness in tower materials linked to LPG availability and West Asia conflict, affecting deployment timelines and costs.
demand_pricing: Core revenue growth muted by Q4 FY25 one-time reconciliation benefit (about 2.1pp of base) and a Q4 FY26 one-time settlement; management cited organic service revenue growth of about 5-5.5% YoY after adjusting for an Airtel tower acquisition.
Annual escalations of about 2.5% cited as a revenue driver.
Management said a major customer's contract expiries affect only a very small portion of the portfolio; some Jio tenancies have expired but are still operating, with minor churn.
Management expects tenancy ratio trend to change as second anchor customer ramps; cannot give a directional outlook.
Diesel-price pass-through is said to be billed on actuals with no lag; industrial (bulk) diesel price rise does not affect the company's retail diesel purchases.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about the FCF from last year's VI dues reversal, now that FY26 FCF is almost fully distributed, and what capex guidance applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Board evaluated FCF and desired debt levels and chose to distribute FY26 FCF; capex about 70% growth, 25% replacement, and no forward numbers given, with a healthy order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a formal dividend policy, and is there a minimum payout?
qa_highlights.answer: Policy is on the website: the Board considers distributing year-end FCF, subject to working capital and other conditions; no minimum payout amount is specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY25 cash not been released, given earlier comments about distributing it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board did not compartmentalise cash by year; it assessed full FCF and debt levels, with total distributions of about INR 37-38bn.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 maintenance spend a one-off or a structural reset as towers age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonality (clear-weather Q3/Q4 and pre-monsoon preparation) plus a deliberate tower-strengthening programme; said cost per tower has fallen over 3-4 years and the base is not reset.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the sequential EBITDA decline and per-tower drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 revenue hit by a one-time settlement; Q3 had a positive one-off in other expenses; network maintenance up 5.6% QoQ; full-year margin still on track at 55%-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Why are single-tenancy tower additions rising and what is the Vodafone rollout impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said co-location additions exceeded tower additions in Q3 and Q4; some towers move from other tower companies to Indus (net addition), so a direct split is not possible.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa operations start, and will NOC be local or in India?
qa_highlights.answer: First tower in Zambia expected very soon, well within six months; NOC location not yet decided.

qa_highlights.question: Do the Jio tower contract expiries lead to churn, and were renewals at the same terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Some expired tenancies still operate; very minor percentage churned; renewals continue on the same terms, with no incremental concessions mentioned in response.

534816|2026-06.headline: Indus Towers Q1 FY27 gross revenue rose 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn; EBITDA up 3.0% to INR 45.2 bn, margin 53.6%.
534816|2026-06.overview: Gross revenue grew 4.6% YoY to INR 84.3 bn, with core rental up 5.2% YoY to INR 53.7 bn on tower and colocation additions. Reported EBITDA rose 3.0% YoY to INR 45.2 bn, but margin fell 1.5 pp YoY to 53.6%; adjusting for a prior-year INR 0.9 bn write-back, EBITDA grew 5.2%. Energy margin was -4.6% (seasonal, plus past-period settlements), while diesel consumption fell 13% YoY. Management reiterated a firm order book for 3-4 quarters and began Africa rollouts guidance for next quarter, with economics still undisclosed. The CFO also announced his departure after five years.

535322|2026-03.headline: Repco Home Finance posted record FY26 disbursements of Rs.4,148 Crores (+26% YoY) and cut GNPA to 2.55%, while AUM growth of 9.6% to Rs.15,880 Crores lagged disbursements.
535322|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly (Rs.1,186 Crores) and annual (Rs.4,148 Crores) disbursements, with Q4 PAT of Rs.129.11 Crores versus Rs.108.77 Crores in Q3. Gross NPA fell from 3.26% in December 2025 to 2.55% in March 2026, and Stage 2 assets declined to about 7% from about 9.5% a year earlier. Loan book growth remained well below disbursement growth because of run-off, prepayments and balance transfers out. Management guided to Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement and Rs.18,000 Crores AUM for FY27, and a 75% total FY26 dividend.

segments.commentary: Home loans are 71% and non-housing loans 29% of the book, and salaried customers are 46% (Rs.7,410 Crores) against non-salaried 54% (Rs.8,470 Crores). Yields are 11.16% for HL, 13.44% for non-HL, 11.36% for salaried and 12.27% for non-salaried.

segments.commentary: GNPA on the new book is about 1% and Stage 2 is about 3.9%.
