Stage 2 assets expected to fall below 5% before end of FY27.
Spread target of about 3.2% to 3.25% for FY27, down from 3.34% previously reported.

demand_pricing: Balance transfers out (BT Out) average about Rs.30 to Rs.35 Crores per month, mainly to public sector banks, while BT In averages about Rs.45 to Rs.50 Crores per month, mainly from HFCs for self-employed borrowers. Management says net BT In is positive.

FY26 principal run-off was about Rs.2,670 Crores, comprising about Rs.700 Crores scheduled repayment and about Rs.2,000 Crores of prepayments, pre-closures and BT Out (including Rs.400 Crores of BT Out, Rs.256 Crores partial prepayment and Rs.1,675 Crores full closure).
Management is following risk-based pricing and has cut rates case by case to retain customers. Benchmark rates were cut 10 bps on 1 July 2025 and 10 bps on 1 February 2026.
Competitive market: management says spread and growth are in tension and it will sacrifice some spread to grow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.25,000 Crores AUM by FY28 aspiration still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Not on the original timeline. Management now targets about Rs.18,000 Crores by FY27 end and about Rs.25,000 Crores two years later, i.e. about one year behind. Inorganic buying is limited to Rs.25 to Rs.30 Crores this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AUM growth well below disbursement growth, and is the new book also running down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed vintage run-off, self-employed customers making bullet and part prepayments, and BT Out. An analyst's data point suggested about Rs.3,000 Crores of run-off on the post-FY22 book; management acknowledged part prepayments on the new book but said there were no major pre-closures there.

qa_highlights.question: Can per-branch productivity support Rs.5,000 Crores disbursement with current sales staff?
qa_highlights.answer: Average disbursement per branch is Rs.1.5 to Rs.2 Crores per month, which management says is achievable with one branch head and one sales manager plus processing support. It also acknowledged that adding salespeople is an option but is constrained by cost-to-income targets.

qa_highlights.question: Will Stage 2 fall below 5% and how?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to get Stage 2 below 5% by the end of FY27. Rs.300 Crores was rolled back in FY26 through a dedicated collection vertical, and a separate team now targets B0 to B1 flows.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated dividend payout continue?
qa_highlights.answer: The CEO said the higher payout is not a one-off and management wants to continue the trend. The FY27 interim/final split and quantum will be decided later.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the pricing and cost of funds trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell from 8.75% to 8.5% over the year, and the NHB refinance should cut it by 10 to 15 bps. Yield is about 11.9%, and spread is expected at about 3.2% to 3.25% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q-o-Q growth flat in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Karnataka e-Khata issue is fading, Andhra Pradesh had team realignment in Q4 with new leadership, and it expects growth from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan. It expects a much larger non-TN contribution from Q1 or Q2 FY27.

Profit affected by one-offs of about Rs.46 Crores in FY26 (Labour Code Rs.15 Crores, silver jubilee Rs.5 Crores, CSR uplift Rs.15 Crores, daily-balance interest method Rs.11.53 Crores), with CSR expected to fall back to 2% to 3%.
Quarterly disbursement run-rate of about Rs.1,000 Crores to be sustained in Q1 FY27 (management guidance).

Several answers were vague on specifics (CSR, FY27 dividend split, sales headcount), and management promised follow-up on the next call.

Net profit rose to Rs.114 Cr from Rs.108 Cr and NII to Rs.216 Cr from Rs.207 Cr, while GNPA was Rs.427 Cr (2.7%) versus Rs.405 Cr (2.6%) in the prior quarter. qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 disbursement affected by cheque issues, and is there a Q1 backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end disbursements of about Rs.35-40 Cr roll over each month as a normal cycle; June's figure carries the operational impact and any backlog will be made up in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are June and July run-rates back to normal, and is the Rs.1,200 Cr Q2 target credible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June was good, July was better and August is expected to exceed that, and the MD said he was confident of Rs.1,200 Cr, while declining to give exact figures citing price-sensitive policy.

qa_highlights.question: Have pricing or customer policies changed, and what is driving the higher runoff?
qa_highlights.answer: No major policy change; sourcing focus shifted and some rate concessions were given to retain customers. Higher BT-outs reflect competitors targeting the company's visibility from more aggressive marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality deterioration business as usual, and can recoveries outpace provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA uptick to transfers and promotions. Soft NPAs (April 2025-June 2026 slippages, about 1,000-1,100 cases, 40-45 per RVM) are targeted for at least 50% reduction, worth Rs.70-75 Cr, and chronic NPAs are being pursued via SARFAESI.

qa_highlights.question: How much spread compression and what does it do to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is 3.44% with cost of funds at 8.31%, and ROA around 2.9%. Spread may fall 10-12bps (maximum 10bps) next quarter, then stabilise.

535602|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 30% YoY to INR971.8 crore, while EBITDA grew 12% to INR112.9 crore at an 11.6% margin.
535602|2026-03.overview: Sharda Motor reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR971.8 crore (+30% YoY), gross profit of INR216.1 crore (+13%), and EBITDA of INR112.9 crore (+12%, 11.6% margin). For FY26, revenue reached INR3,396.8 crore (+20%), but gross profit grew only 8% to INR802.8 crore and EBITDA 6% to INR419.1 crore. Management attributed the gap between revenue and profit growth to catalyst price pass-through and a suspension business that stayed flat at about 9% of sales, and said new export and lightweighting orders would only show in growth once SOPs ramp. Analysts pressed hard on whether the core business lagged the industry, and management maintained that gross profit growth was in line with industry.

qa_highlights.answer: CAFE III is multi-fuel and technology-inclusive, so all powertrains except pure EVs still need emission systems. Management expects an INR4,000-10,000 per-vehicle content increase from the lightweighting portfolio, including torsion beams and subframes.

535602|2026-06.headline: Sharda Motor Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% to INR1,011.1 crores, but gross profit grew only 8% to INR203.9 crores and EBITDA 5% to INR103.2 crores.
535602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 34% YoY to INR1,011.1 crores, driven by pass-through catalyst sales and product mix, while gross profit grew 8% to INR203.9 crores. Management attributed the weak gross profit growth to a supplier fire at a key customer and one-time premium raw material and freight costs linked to the geopolitical situation in April and May, which it said stabilised in July. EBITDA was INR103.2 crores (10.2% margin, up 5%), and PAT was INR86.5 crores. Management said the lightweighting, export and emission order book is moving into SOPs, but gave no numerical guidance.

FY27 growth drivers cited: full-year benefit of lightweighting orders, ramp-up of additional lightweighting programmes, temperature-controlled tube adjacencies, North American export SOPs, and supportive domestic OEM volumes.

535693|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 50% to INR365 crore and PAT nearly doubled to INR59.61 crore, with an INR1,600 crore order book (4.46x FY26 revenue).

Management attributed the gain to Q2 and Q3 monsoon-quarter execution, where revenue reached INR180 crore versus INR70 crore a year earlier. Q4 standalone revenue was INR93.93 crore, PBT INR16.79 crore, PAT INR14.78 crore and EPS INR5.09. This was the company's first earnings call, and Q&A covered order book conversion, real estate plans, promoter pledge, and JV revenue sharing.

Average execution period for new bids is two to three years.

qa_highlights.answer: All road projects are EPC or item-rate; none are HAM. EPC margins range 13-20%, averaging about 15%, with niche works at 18-19% and general infrastructure at 11-13%.

qa_highlights.answer: Shares were pledged in 2014 when debt was higher; management is negotiating release with lenders and hopes to release it within one to two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book not show up in Q4 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 50% of the book was won in the last six months; EPC design, land and approvals take six to seven months before revenue recognition begins.

qa_highlights.answer: Current pipeline is about INR3,000 crore with results in 30-45 days; FY27 bidding is expected at INR7,000-8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included about INR4 crore of industrial plot sales that did not recur in FY26; real estate profit rose to INR16.70 crore from INR14.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be deployed to fund growth, and is there a debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to surety bonds plus bank guarantees, and JVs with partners, rather than a stated debt reduction target.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately 70% of order book revenue comes to BIL and 30% to JV partners, varying by project.

535693|2026-06.headline: Brahmaputra Infra Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.24% YoY to Rs 110.79 crore, with PAT up 9.57% to Rs 16.48 crore.
535693|2026-06.overview: Consolidated top line crossed Rs 110 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 20.24% YoY and 17.95% QoQ, driven by EPC activity. Consolidated EBITDA rose 13.08% YoY to Rs 25.15 crore, while PAT grew 9.57% YoY to Rs 16.48 crore. Management said Rs 429 crore of orders were booked in the quarter and the order book stands at about Rs 1,600 crore, with roughly 50% yet to start. Management also addressed cash conversion, pointing to Rs 165 crore of OCCPS repayments from June 2027 and arbitration recoveries of Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years.

segments.name: EPC

segments.commentary: Consolidated real estate revenue Rs 6.33 crore, up about 65% YoY from Rs 3.82 crore; real estate PBT Rs 5.40 crore. Management cites 85-90% margins for this segment.

Management expects no margin compression for FY28-FY29 and says growth will come from higher order inflow.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no stuck-up money or slow-moving WIP on post-2020 projects; debtors about Rs 15-20 crore with 45-90 day billing cycles. Pre-2020 legacy projects in arbitration: over Rs 100 crore monetised in five years, about Rs 150 crore still pending, with Rs 200-225 crore expected over two years including bank guarantee releases. OCCPS of Rs 165 crore repayment starts June 2027 and runs to 2034; management plans to swap OCCPS with arbitration awards.

535754|2026-03.headline: Ambuja Cements FY26: record 73.7 Mt volumes, but Q4 cost ~INR4,500/t; FY27 volume guided ~80 Mt and cost cut of INR250/t targeted.
535754|2026-03.overview: Ambuja's Q4 FY26 call (consolidating Orient Cement for 11 months and Penna from August 2025) showed record FY26 volumes of 73.7 Mt, up 16% YoY, with normalized FY26 EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (INR887/t, up 12%) and PAT of INR2,647 crore (up 17%). Management said Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above its earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, due to acquired-asset underperformance, freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management called the reset partial: FY28 capacity targets slip toward FY30, capex is cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore for FY27, and the company says cost peaked in Q4. Demand is expected to be soft and industry price hikes are small (about INR10/bag).

segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% in FY27. Rail link at Naliya is an add-on, not in base case; seven marine vessels ordered for delivery from next year.

segments.name: Penna Cement (acquired)
segments.commentary: Utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% in FY27. Breakdowns and deferred maintenance cited; Sanghi and Penna together hold 19 Mt capacity, with a 5-10% utilization uplift targeted.

segments.commentary: Management says Orient is running at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

Capacity to reach ~119 Mt by end FY27 after ~10 Mt of additions (commissioning Aug-Sep 2026 window); FY28 target capacity slips toward FY30; Maratha adds 4 Mt clinker; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) follow in about 24-28 months.
FY27 capex estimated at INR6,000-6,500 crore; project IRR hurdle of 18% stated.
Management did not give EBITDA/t guidance; said it is too early to estimate given volatility.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end after 10.7 Mt grinding and 7 Mt clinker added (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam, Jodhpur, Bhatapara).
Clinker capacity 69 Mt now, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).
About INR4,000 crore of capex already under execution (capacity, WHRS, fly ash transport); balance is debottlenecking and maintenance.

Management paused new projects until current ones are completed; engineering to be finalized over next 6 months.

April-May demand described as subdued and soft; management would be happy if industry recovers half of a price hike.
Q4 FY26 volume growth was muted (Orient-adjusted flat YoY per an analyst); packing bag shortages linked to West Asia conflict cost volume in March.
Premium cement gap versus base product INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium; price gap with the number-one player is INR5-10 in some districts.
Management expects FY27 demand to be soft due to inflation and weak monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 cost about INR4,500/t when management earlier pointed to an INR4,000 exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for the March exit; March averaged ~INR4,100 normalized, with INR250 escalation from West Asia. Causes cited: branding, repairs at acquired plants, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, and lower government incentives.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost reduction is assumed for FY27 after Q4 inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,500 is the peak; a INR250/t reduction gives ~INR4,250/t for FY27 on a full-year average, with Q1 FY27 flat at ~INR4,500.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,650/t cost target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned; INR500/t cumulative over two years is the committed minimum, with further runway to the earlier target.

qa_highlights.question: Why the reset in capacity and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said performance fell short of commitments, citing cost, wrong contractor choice, projects started without full engineering, and breakdowns at Penna and Sanghi; ~80% of the five KPIs relate to cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a target IRR for capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani stated a project IRR of 18%, all equity-funded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cause of high working capital and negative ACC operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinod Bahety said ACC has MSA receivables from Ambuja that will be settled via an ICD after shareholder approval; Ambuja's core working capital fell to 20 days from 30 days.

Pricing power in a soft demand environment; April-May trend described as subdued.

Non-core working capital, MSA receivables from ACC, and negative ACC operating cash flow, to be resolved via ICD.
Reduced government incentives after GST rate cuts and changed accrual policy.

535754|2026-06.headline: Ambuja Cements Q1 FY27: EBITDA up 331 bps to 16.7% and net cost down INR206/t to INR4,241/t, while total volumes fell (trade -2%, non-trade -21% YoY).
535754|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a value-over-volume quarter: trade share rose to 78% from 74%, and operating EBITDA reached INR1,589 crore on revenue of about INR9,500 crore. Net operating cost fell INR206/t sequentially to INR4,241/t, which management said absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia-related cost inflation. Volumes declined, with trade down 2% and non-trade down 21% YoY, and management attributed the quarter's weakness to diesel shortages, packing material issues and deliberate exits from low-margin South volumes. Management guided to 8% FY27 volume growth, citing July trade volumes up 8% YoY, and reiterated INR4,250/t full-year cost guidance.

segments.commentary: Trade volumes sustained with healthy margins; about 25% of volume mix.

Identified cost levers worth INR130-150/t: about INR35/t lead distance cut (15 km), INR30/t from raw material logistics and fly ash sourcing, INR50/t from energy (heat rate, power units, 75 MW new RE), and INR10-15/t other headroom.
Q2 FY27 net cost guided to be slightly better than June-quarter levels, after absorbing potential geopolitical cost rise of about INR100/t.
Capex FY27 about INR6,500 crore; Q1 spend about INR1,500-1,600 crore. FY28 capex similar at INR6,000-7,000 crore on a run-rate basis.
Installed capacity to reach 119 Mtpa by end-FY27 (adding about 10.2 Mt); 8-10 Mtpa of organic additions planned each year thereafter.
Long-term capacity utilisation target 70-75% on a value-focused basis; green power share to reach 60% by FY28 (48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis).

Kalamboli (Mumbai, 1 Mt) and Warisaliganj (Bihar, 2.4 Mt) expected in Q2 FY27 (Warisaliganj most likely September).
Maratha clinker line (4 Mt) now expected Q1 FY28; Mundra expected 18-24 months out (around 2029).
RE capacity 973-975 MW (of 1,122 MW target; about 150 MW remaining); WHRS 228 MW rising to about 376 MW.
Three coal blocks in focus; first expected to be operational in about 30 months. AFR (alternative fuel) substitution at about 7%, targeted at 10-15% in FY27.
Sanghi: about INR600 crore jetty expansion for clinker. Penna: INR100-150 crore for AFR and WHRS. About 3.5 Mt of old ACC capacity temporarily closed for around six months.
demand_pricing: Management says cement demand was stable across infrastructure, housing and construction; July trade volumes reportedly up 8% YoY.
Q1 headwinds: diesel availability, packing material shortages and logistics disruption in West and East. Logistics lead distance fell from 269 km to 249 km YoY, yet freight per tonne was flat.
NSP rose sequentially but fell YoY; management attributed the gap to Incoterm and channel-cost netting. Analyst comparison put Q1 NSP about INR100/t below UltraTech's reported NSP.

qa_highlights.answer: About 45 crore units sold in Q1; roughly 50% (about 20 crore units) expected to be consumed in Q2. Green power share is 34% on consumption basis, 48% on revenue-plus-consumption basis, targeted at 60% by FY28. Grid power costs INR7-8/unit versus the cost of captive green power, and sales are capped at around 10% of output.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 FY27 net cost rise given inventory buffers, and what is the full-year cost path?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 net cost expected to be broadly in line with or slightly better than the June quarter, after absorbing a potential geopolitical rise of about INR100/t. FY27 target INR4,250/t reiterated; FY28 target INR4,000/t or below. Clinker inventory about one month, coal about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade volumes still decline YoY, and how did the regions perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by diesel shortages, packing material issues and logistics disruption. North trade +2% YoY, West grew in trade and non-trade, East sustained, South cut about 1 Mt of low or negative EBITDA volume, Central degrew on blended-cement shift. Capacity utilisation 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Where did the INR206/t sequential cost reduction come from, and what was the gross saving after West Asia cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to fly ash sourcing, RE power price per unit, clinker factor down about 2-3%, marginal logistics gains (INR10/t), and fixed cost optimisation. Management said the INR206/t saving absorbed about INR110/t of West Asia cost, implying gross savings of about INR316/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NSP down about INR100/t versus UltraTech's reported NSP, and what are the Incoterm and netting effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NSP is netted for certain channel and Incoterm costs (ex-works terms), and that channel investment is being expensed against NSP. It did not quantify the gap and said NSP is market-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company keeping plants temporarily closed and treating non-trade differently at acquired assets?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3.5 Mt of old ACC and one acquired-company facility temporarily closed for around six months; management said these are not permanent closures. Karan Adani said non-trade volumes at acquired assets were largely at negative or marginal EBITDA, so the company is prioritising value over volume.

Execution risk on capacity: Kalamboli and Warisaliganj (Q2 FY27), Maratha clinker slipped to Q1 FY28, Mundra around 2029, and 8-10 Mtpa annual additions thereafter.

Reconciliation gap: management did not provide a breakdown of cement vs RMC vs power vs fly ash cost, and deferred several analyst requests (fly ash/power cumulative P&L, RMC margin drop to about 7%, fixed cost bridge) to offline follow-up.

Accounting items to monitor: O&M cost equalisation across quarters still under discussion with auditors; INR24 crore termination-related exceptional item (VRS in South); depreciation true-up after Sanghi and Penna merger.
Green power transition: grid connectivity for some cement plants expected in two to three quarters, and green power share target of 60% by FY28 depends on consumption rising from about 50% of sales.
key_quotes: Our strategy remains clear and consistent, creating sustainable value ahead of volume.
Net operating cost reduced to INR4,241 per metric ton, a reduction of INR 206 PMT from the previous quarter.
So the operating company, Ambuja has no debt.

Management flagged a weaker wedding calendar, a marginal March slowdown from geopolitical disruption, and 3-4% raw material inflation with 5-8% price increases under evaluation for H2.

535789|2026-03.headline: Sammaan Capital's IHC takeover closed 31 March 2026; all three domestic agencies upgraded within 50 days, lifting bonds ~100 bps and targeting FY27 PAT of INR1,400 crore.
535789|2026-03.overview: This was the first earnings call after IHC's strategic investment, with IHC's share allotment completed on 31 March 2026 and IHC holding 28.5% equity (43.5% after warrant conversion within 18 months). Management said INR5,652 crore (USD 592 million) has been received via equity and 25% warrant upfront, with about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due on warrant conversion. CRISIL (9 April), CARE (12 May) and ICRA (23 May) upgraded the company to AA+ across all three, with CRISIL and ICRA up one notch and CARE up two. The call centred on a multi-year plan (FY27 to FY30) with a 4.4% steady-state ROA, cost-to-income falling to about 26%, and a shift to a co-lending and asset-light model, alongside a legacy-book write-off/credit cost discussion. The call also included a correction of the FY30 ROA figure from 8-odd percent to 4.4%.

segments.name: Residential mortgages (prime and affordable)
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market home loans (8.5% to 10% yield) to be sourced for sale to banks; affordable portion (10% to 13%) to be held on balance sheet. Management says mortgages drive growth in FY27 and FY28.

segments.name: Business loans and micro-LAP
segments.commentary: Prime mass-market loans yield 9.5% to 11% and are to be sold; semi-urban and micro-LAP loans yield 11% to 13.5% and are to be held.

segments.name: CRE project loans
segments.commentary: Done only on a co-origination basis with credit funds, pari-passu with no credit guarantee, with the company taking roughly 10% to 15% of disbursements.

segments.name: Gold loans and loans against securities
segments.commentary: Planned as the next secured products; gold needs a separate branch network, with wider product launches from FY28. About 240 branches are already sized for other products.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursements of about INR30,000 crore; Q1 FY27 disbursements to be at least 50% to 60% above Q4 FY26, then a 30% to 40% step-up on that base.

Marginal cost of funds to fall about 160 bps; cost of funds to decline 150 bps over three years; 270 bps total reduction tied to AA to AAA migration (120 to 150 bps on AA to AA+, and the rest on AA+ to AAA).
Portfolio mix target: 60% secured and 20% unsecured or semi-secured, with 80% retail; about 30% of incremental disbursements through co-lending or direct assignment.
Gearing capped at about 3.5x to 4x; liquidity held at the higher of 6 months of repayments or 10% to 15% of borrowings.
Target AUM of INR2 lakh crore and high-teen ROE (about 18%), with the timeline described as 'in no hurry'; FY27 and FY28 growth to be mainly mortgages.
capex_capacity: Branch network to grow fivefold to about 1,600 branches; workforce to rise to 20,000 people, with about 8,000 by end of FY26 per management.
A gold loan branch costs about INR20 lakh to set up and takes about 3 years to become fully productive and profitable; investment is not described as running into tens or hundreds of crore.
Technology spend (CRM upgrade and Salesforce deployment about 6 months ago) is expensed through the P&L, not capitalised; 37 AI use cases identified.
Targets: agent productivity up 30%, mortgage turnaround from 5 to 7 days to 2 to 3 days, loans per person per month from 0.6 to 2-plus.
demand_pricing: Management says productivity rose 2x between March and April 2026 following the shift to an asset-light model.
Disbursals of about INR72,000 crore planned for FY29 versus INR50,000 crore in CY17 and CY18 (as cited by management).
Competition: management says there are few AAA-rated NBFCs and that the market has room for new entrants; it cites AAA players (and 3 to 4 other AA+ players) disbursing around INR50,000 crore a year.
Management says insurance cross-sell reaches over 90% of borrowers.
Management says about 90% of borrowings are onshore; domestic bonds have appreciated about 100 bps since the IHC announcement, with international bonds about 250 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Ahuja (BlackRock): Will offshore rating agencies follow the onshore upgrades, and is the slow cost-of-funds decline due to non-call fixed-maturity debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects international agencies to follow the domestic upgrades. Bonds cannot be renegotiated and have 3 to 4 year maturities, so the cost decline comes with a lag; incremental borrowing at lower cost and bank renegotiation are the levers.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI Bank): How will the company build non-mortgage portfolios, who will run them, and how will costs be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it has run secured and unsecured products at scale before, that tech and app-based lending help, and that people and tech investment will be made. Growth in FY27 and FY28 will be mainly mortgages, given no rush to hyper-grow.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): What share of growth comes from core versus new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 and FY28 disbursals are 80% existing products, falling over time; by FY30 the mix is targeted at 50% mortgage-backed and 50% other products.

qa_highlights.question: Avinash Singh (Emkay): How will competition from AAA NBFCs be handled, and is the FY30 ROA of about 8% correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the FY30 ROA figure was an error and corrected it to 4.4%, with FY27 at 1.8%, FY28 at 3.7% and FY29 at 4.4%. It says the market is large enough and that mortgage front-loading and co-lending support productivity.

qa_highlights.question: Naintara Ghosh (Deutsche Bank): How much investment is needed for the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is mainly branches and people rather than large capex; technology costs already incurred (CRM, Salesforce) run through the P&L, and product-level ROA can be shared on request.

qa_highlights.question: Vineet Sharma (Param Capital): What drives the NIM rise from 3.5% to 5.8% when cost of funds is not falling as fast?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the NIM gain comes from the spread on sold-down loans (AUM less loan book rising from about INR30,000 crore to INR45,000 crore in FY28), and that equity adds liquidity without a P&L cost. Cost of funds shown is for on-balance-sheet borrowings only.

qa_highlights.question: Arun Antony (JM Financial): Is the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction for FY27 still achievable given the West Asia conflict and rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 270 bps, with 120 to 150 bps coming from AA to AA+ and the rest from AA+ to AAA, and said the company is operationally, financially and promoter-ready for AAA.

qa_highlights.question: AS Raju (individual investor): What is the outstanding write-off as of 31 March, and will recoveries be included in projections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recoveries of about INR7,000 crore from amounts provided are built into the projections and described the provisions as credit costs, not write-offs. It said asset reconstruction company sales recover 70% to 80%.

risks_watch: Execution on FY27 disbursals (INR30,000 crore) and Q1 FY27 step-up; management's productivity claims rely on a 2x jump in one month.
Cost-of-funds path: 270 bps depends on AA to AAA migration; international agency ratings are still pending, and about 90% of borrowings are onshore.
Warrant balance of about INR3,200 crore (USD 335 million) due within 18 months, plus IHC's rise to 43.5%.
Credit-cost and recovery assumptions: the legacy book had provisions, with recoveries of about INR7,000 crore assumed; the call did not give a detailed write-off schedule.
Cost-to-income falling from ~50% to ~26% while hiring and building new products, with a risk of cost overrun during the transition.
A FY30 ROA projection error was corrected on the call; the revised presentation should be checked for other inconsistencies.

It was more cautious on timing, saying the 270 bps cost-of-funds reduction depends on the AA to AAA path. It was evasive on some specifics, such as the write-off quantum, and it corrected the FY30 ROA figure during Q&A.

AA+ is just the first stop. AAA is the destination.
I would refrain from calling this write-off. These are credit costs, which will enable management to focus on bandwidth.

535789|2026-06.headline: Sammaan Capital posted Q1 FY27 PAT of INR243 crores, with cost of funds falling from 10.5% to 10% and AUM at INR56,239 crores.
535789|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 as the first quarter under IHC ownership, with PAT of INR243 crores after last quarter's balance-sheet markdowns. Disbursements were about INR3,875-3,900 crores across five products to roughly 12,000 new customers, and net NPA is 0.15%. Cost of funds declined through the quarter, helped by rating upgrades (domestic AA to AA+, international B+ to BB-) and repricing of existing borrowings. Management reiterated a shift from portfolio management to growth, a build-out of branches, tech and senior hiring, and multi-year targets for cost of funds, cost-to-income, ROE and ROA.

Down about 50 bps during the quarter

guidance_outlook: Disbursements: INR10,000 crores in H1 FY27 (Q1 on target) and INR20,000 crores in H2, total INR30,000 crores for FY27; INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.

Branches: about 240 at end of H1 FY27, rising to 270, with 800 branches targeted by end of FY28.
Five-year targets cited on the call: ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%, as put out on May 20.
Inorganic growth to be considered from FY28; the bias for now is to build.
capex_capacity: Branch network to rise from about 240 at end-H1 FY27 to 270; 23 master service centres across 20 states; management targets 800 branches by end of FY28.
Digital-first app to go live in H2 FY27, integrating a new Salesforce-based CRM and a new loan management system, plus a data lake.
Digital personal loans to launch on the app in H2 FY27; gold loans, two-wheeler loans and BNPL-type e-commerce tie-ups targeted by end-FY28.
53 AI use cases under implementation, with about 60% to be implemented in FY27; about 66% of identified use cases reportedly in motion.

Securitisation and asset-light model: at least 30% of origination to be securitised or sold down, with 60-70% kept as a backup option; assets below 9.5% to be sold down via direct assignment, above 9.5% sliced between balance sheet and securitisation.
Asset yield universe cited from 8.5% (prime) to about 20% (unsecured); LAP 11-12% and affordable loans 12-13% also eligible for securitisation.
Fee income expected to rise, with direct assignment fee income kicking in around October 2026 with about a six-month lag.
97% of Q1 disbursements and 97% of AUM are secured.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Will lower cost of funds be passed on to customers for acquisition, or will spreads be retained?
qa_highlights.answer: Strategy rides on lower cost of funds plus asset-light model; sub-9.5% assets to be sold down via direct assignment and higher-yield assets kept or securitised, balancing fee and spread income.

qa_highlights.question: Bhanu Chauhan (Barclays): How much upfront opex and what is the cost-to-income path?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex will rise in absolute terms, offset by fee income with a lag of a quarter or two; cost-to-income around 50% this year, declining from H2 FY28, reaching 30-35% by FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Abhiram Iyer (Deutsche Bank): What is the asset-class breakup of the roughly INR3,000 crore per half target?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 mix about 75% mortgage-backed and 25% new products; disbursement breakdown to expand from 4-5 boxes to at least 8 by end-FY27 and 15 by end-FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Agarwal (Bajaj Alternates): What tangible benefits has IHC delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 90 bps saving on about INR50,000 crore borrowings (about INR450 crore annualised), targeting a further 70 bps; software procurement at 30-50% of earlier costs; and senior talent additions.

qa_highlights.question: Sanket (DAM Capital): What is IHC's larger vision beyond lending in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Dalia Khorshid (IHC) said the group is open to opportunities in India across fintech, digital, AI and financial services, with Sammaan seen as a platform; management said FY27 is for stabilisation and other fee businesses will be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: Niharika (CapGrow): Are the five-year ROE, ROA and NIM targets achievable?

qa_highlights.question: Nilesh Sharma (Monomer): What are disbursement targets for this and next financial year?
qa_highlights.answer: INR30,000 crores in FY27 (INR10,000 crores H1, INR20,000 crores H2) and INR40,000-50,000 crores in FY28.

Recoveries and asset quality: management said recoveries will exceed internal projections and that no P&L pain is expected, but the Q1 PAT of INR243 crores relies on net recoveries of INR240 crores; watch recovery run-rate and ARC sale outcomes.
Five-year targets (ROE 6.8% to 18.7%, ROA 1.8% to 8.1%, NIM 3.5% to 8%): management stated confidence but gave no interim milestones beyond FY27 targets; track progress against these.
Governance and inorganic plans: statutory auditor change and internal audit co-sourcing partner selection were said to be closing this quarter; inorganic growth deferred to FY28.

First quarter was bang on target, and that will increase to INR20,000 crores in the second half.
So we're obviously confident which is why we mustered the courage to put it on in public domain and hold ourselves accountable to that.
This year is a year of stabilization of NBFC, of putting the building blocks together.

It was more hedged on the five-year targets' feasibility, senior-hire timing and the Dalia Khorshid response on non-lending India plans, which management said is a year away from decisions.

The Ahmedabad plant is now operational and the company's credit rating was upgraded during FY26. qa_highlights.question: Why do new rides not drive repeat visits?

538268|2026-06.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
538268|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

segments.name: Chennai Park (new, first year)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.name: Resorts (THE ISLE, Terrea, Wonderla resort)
segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

segments.commentary: Overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, mainly investments to strengthen the organisation; about INR1.5 crore incremental digital transformation (new POS from July) and about INR5 crore higher marketing YoY.

demand_pricing: Footfall growth at existing parks was 7% in Q1, but management would not commit to sustaining it; May (highest-footfall month) had no unseasonal rain, and management said weaker monsoon was not a major factor.

Hyderabad growth attributed to marketing and brand investment; trailing-12-month footfall was about 895,000 vs 893,000 a year earlier per an analyst's calculation, which management did not dispute.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7% ex-Chennai footfall growth sustainable, and what margin path should Chennai follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the resort model be replicated and is timeshare planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

538446|2026-03.headline: Moneyboxx Q4 FY26 total income rose to INR63.23 crore (from INR52 crore), but Q4 PAT was only INR0.47 crore amid high credit costs and AUM at INR893 crore.
538446|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of transition, correction and strengthening, after MFI guardrails and stress in small-ticket secured lending hit collections and asset quality. Secured loans rose to about 68% of AUM (from 45% a year earlier), and collection efficiency was around 93.5% for the quarter. Gross NPA was 3.59% and net NPA 1.75%, both lower year on year, but Q4 profit was thin and AUM was down versus last year due to an ARC transaction. Management guided to AUM growth of 43-44% for FY27 and a sharp pickup in disbursements from May 2026, while acknowledging moderate growth so far.

financial_highlights.change: 6% growth as stated; management said YoY decline was due to ARC transaction
vs INR52 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Secured lending (MSME, branch-led)
segments.commentary: Secured share of AUM about 68% (5% of this is unsecured backed by first-loss fee guarantee), up from 45% last year. Secured disbursements were 67% versus 49% last year; target is nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027. Average secured ticket size is INR6 lakh, with run-rate INR8-9 lakh.

segments.name: Renewable energy (solar) loans
segments.commentary: Launched in FY26; disbursements were about INR50 lakh in April, ramping roughly 10x in May to a possible INR5 crore. Management targets about 10% of AUM by March 2027. Average ticket about INR4 lakh, tenure about 4 years, yield about 22-24% including fees, with a second-loss fee guarantee after 3% first loss.

segments.name: Unsecured / digital lending
segments.commentary: Unsecured lending to be restricted to one state; below INR5 lakh secured ticket discontinued in most branches from April. A small digital unsecured lending initiative is planned to start in the current quarter, enabled by the in-house LOS Moneyboxx One.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected, as communicated to lenders; management said it has historically met lender-committed numbers.

Direct OEM/partner-sourced business targeted at 20-25% of monthly business to lower opex; two more partnerships starting in June 2026.

No new geographies in FY26-27; branch network to decline on a net basis via consolidation of rural branches and openings in Tier 1 cities.
capex_capacity: Branch network across 12 states; management is not seeking to expand branch count, consolidating rural branches and opening a few in Tier 1 areas (2 in Bangalore periphery, 1 in Jaipur).
Many branches are in early vintage (under 24 months); productivity is expected to improve as they mature, supporting operating leverage without aggressive expansion.
Newly launched in-house LOS Moneyboxx One and Sikka app are expected to improve turnaround time and field productivity, with benefits in coming months.
Decentralised credit underwriting model deployed, replacing the earlier centralised credit model.
demand_pricing: Management attributed slower growth to tighter underwriting after MFI stress, a state-head team rebuild and the shift to higher-ticket secured loans; some decline in demand acknowledged, with lenders across the sector tightening norms.
Secured yields will be lower; partnership and FLDG-backed business is expected to offset through lower opex and credit cost, per management.
Resolution rates improved: bucket 1 above 70% and bucket 2 above 75%, versus about 30-35% earlier. Current-bucket efficiency rose to over 99.4% in March from about 99% in January.
Management sees collection stress concentrated in the INR3-4 lakh secured ticket segment; SARFAESI and Section 138 actions started from May 2026.
Management expects a seasonal April-June weakness to be offset by solar loans, which peak in those months.

qa_highlights.question: Why has AUM growth remained moderate despite better collections and disbursements, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-MFI-guardrail shift, a senior team overhaul, decentralised credit and removal of sub-INR5 lakh secured tickets. It said top leadership is now in place, and that disbursements and AUM should grow month-on-month from May-June 2026, with FY27 AUM growth of 43-44% projected.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost appears high relative to AUM; how will opex come down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged high cost, attributing it to low AUM and hiring experienced staff; said cost should fall as AUM grows and that 20-25% of monthly business will come through partnerships without a sales team.

qa_highlights.question: Will the shift to secured lending lower yields, and what are the ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted that yields will fall on secured and partnership business, but said lower opex and credit cost should offset this. It cited peers at 12-15% returns on assets as the benchmark, without giving specific ROA/ROE targets.

qa_highlights.question: Any new geographies or products planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No new states in FY27; the 12-state footprint is considered sufficient. Solar is the new product (about 10% of AUM targeted), with one or two more products and a cattle-loan FLDG partnership planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand slowing due to macro uncertainty and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said appetite exists, but lenders have tightened norms and some demand has declined. Lending to restaurants was paused due to LPG shortage. It pointed to green shoots in the MFI segment and government guarantee support for working-capital loans.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the QoQ rise in GNPA and what is the Q1 FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress was concentrated in INR3-4 lakh secured loans and an older stressed book. Management said GNPA is falling monthly since January, with SARFAESI from May; disbursements in Q1 FY27 should beat last year, and Q2 should be far better.

538446|2026-06.headline: Moneyboxx Q1 FY27 disbursements fell to INR77 crore from INR92 crore as AUM reached INR832 crore; management guides to normalised disbursements by January 2027.

Disbursements were INR77 crore versus INR92 crore a year earlier, and total income was INR52.12 crore. Net interest and fee income fell to INR31.02 crore from INR38.52 crore, NIM dropped to 12.3% from 14.36%, and PAT was INR0.21 crore versus INR0.24 crore. Management pointed to partnership channels, solar lending and a digital product as the next growth drivers, with secured AUM targeted at about 80% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the April 2026 stop on unsecured lending in MP, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and Rajasthan, the move to larger tickets, and team retraining. It said it expects normalised disbursements by January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is the unsecured lending stop permanent?

538562|2026-03.headline: Skipper Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY) and PAT rose 70% to INR75.6 crore; FY27 guided to 15% revenue and ~30% PAT growth.
538562|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter to date: revenue INR1,666 crore (+29.4% YoY), EBITDA INR173.4 crore (+40.2%, margin 10.4% vs 9.6%) and PAT INR75.6 crore (+70%, margin 4.5%). FY26 revenue reached INR5,552.8 crore (+20%) with PAT of INR207.3 crore (+42%) and EBITDA margin of 10.3%. Order book closed at a record INR8,501.9 crore on record FY26 inflows of INR5,678 crore, but management flagged a temporary slowdown in domestic bidding and export disruption from the Middle East conflict, and guided FY27 conservatively at 15% revenue growth. Trade receivables rose sharply to INR1,485 crore, which management attributed mainly to a INR260 crore collection slipping into April and higher domestic billing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR9,200 crore order book executes by FY27 and FY28?

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion, and is it sustainable?

538567|2026-03.headline: Gulf Oil Q4 FY26 posted record quarter: 45,000 KL lubricant volume (+14%), EBITDA INR 135 crore, FY26 revenue above INR 4,000 crore.
538567|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly volume, revenue and EBITDA for Q4 FY26, with lubricant volume up about 14% and revenue up about 14%. FY26 lubricant volume grew 10.5% to 1,68,000 KL, and consolidated revenue crossed INR 4,000 crore for the first time. Margin pressure is building from the Middle East crisis and rupee depreciation, with crude moving from about USD 65-70 in February to USD 90-120 in March onward. Management is prioritising supply security and per-litre price pass-through, and is holding its 12-14% EBITDA margin band as the target. The Board recommended a record FY26 dividend of INR 51 per share, including a INR 30 final.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing segment-wise focus under 'Unlock 2.0' (accelerate, premiumise, transform), with digital initiatives, mechanic outreach and EV fluids for more than 30 OEMs. It aims to grow margins through premium products.

qa_highlights.answer: Global R&D is funded by Gulf globally, so no direct P&L hit in India. Payout was lifted from 30-40% three to four years ago to c.72% for FY26, as cash builds and M&A and Tirex funding are still ahead.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Chennai and Silvassa expansions on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Chennai is expected by Q3 and Silvassa by Q4 FY27; civil work at Silvassa is progressing.

qa_highlights.question: Are base oil availability and price rises hitting margins in Q1-Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to hold the 12-14% margin band and has cost levers. Supply has held so far, but a prolonged crisis could squeeze refiner supply chains. Prices are being raised repeatedly.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 volume driven by channel stocking or sustainable demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said double-digit growth ran through the year, with March-end boosted by supply-security buying from OEMs and distributors. Demand remains good into April-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook and revenue timing for data-centre cooling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume will be low and timing depends on which data centres are targeted; no revenue timing given.

538635|2026-06.headline: Snowman guides 10-15% top-line growth for FY27 despite war-driven volume dip; Gateway ICD volumes stagnant, DFC-JNPT link now complete.
538635|2026-06.overview: Joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics call covering Q1 FY27. Management attributed the volume softness to the West Asia conflict (since April), which cut imports sharply in April-May, and to July weather disruptions at ports; market share is described as intact while the underlying market has de-grown. Snowman pricing rose 5-7% on average across warehousing customers, and management guided 10-15% top-line growth across all segments. Rail EBITDA was pressured by lower double-stacking (39% vs 40-42% earlier), higher underframe and empty running, and wage and fuel inflation, with relief expected from Q2. Management reported no specific Q1 financial figures in the call.

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pricing up 5-7% on average; about 24,000 additional pallets expected by end of FY27 (Pune first, then Patna).

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Service margin typically 5-6%; no new 5PL customer added in Q1, with new names possibly by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: CFS (Gateway)
segments.commentary: Volumes improved and a pricing increase taken to offset fuel and wage hikes; margin uplift possible in Q2. Management is not actively pursuing a sale.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said share is intact and the market itself has de-graded due to the war; double-digit growth for the year is still expected once the situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: How much MAT credit supports the low cash tax rate, and when does full tax apply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Kartik Aiyer said the company will pay at 18.88% for at least 7-8 years, using accumulated MAT credit; management noted cash tax rose only INR 1-2 crore YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why has rail EBITDA per TEU weakened, and what is the fix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower import share, lower double-stacking, higher underframe and empty running, port imbalance at Mundra and Pipavav, and steep wage hikes (Haryana up 35%); recovery expected as volumes return, with fuel impact visible in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JNPT exposure and the economics of shifting to it?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT is about 5% of rail volume; on current pricing it is more expensive for North-bound customers but yields higher revenue and slightly higher EBITDA per TEU for Gateway due to distance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the CFS business and its land?
qa_highlights.answer: A sale was explored about 1.5 years ago without a satisfactory valuation; no active process now, though management is open to a good offer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value of the land bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a formal valuation; cited Garhi (85-90 acres) at INR 25-30 crore per acre on outright purchase, with total land of about 475 acres.

538635|2026-09.headline: Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call: pallets stored up ~10% YoY, ~23,000 pallets being added, FY27 EBITDA seen crossing INR100 crore; PAT remains thin.
538635|2026-09.overview: This was a joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call, with Snowman questions covering warehousing, 5PL, capex and margins. Management said pallets stored rose close to 10% YoY, with warehousing revenue growing about 10-11%, while utilisation held at 85% against a targeted 88-89%. 5PL grew only 1-2% as one major customer declined and another grew, and no new 5PL customer was added this fiscal. Management said Snowman is on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year but gave no firm PAT trajectory, citing reinvestment-driven interest and depreciation. On the Gateway side, management guided to a 100,000 TEU-per-quarter rail-volume floor and double-digit growth for next year, with Western DFC and JNPT linkage still unproven for volume shifts.

Analyst-cited figures, not disputed by management

segments.commentary: Growth of 1-2% in Q2; no new customer added this fiscal, with a few deals near closure. Scope expanded for one major customer to pan-India; management is avoiding low or negative margin business.

segments.commentary: Rail volumes recovered about 11% QoQ; management targets at least 100,000 rail TEUs per quarter. Ankleshwar MMLP EXIM permissions are in place and volumes are minimal so far.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said reinvestment keeps interest and depreciation high, so PAT may grow modestly; focus is on operating cash flow and EBITDA, with Snowman on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are warehousing margins falling over the long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5PL mix, park-and-pay spot business at under 10% margin, build-to-suit at lower margin, and minimum wage, PF and gratuity changes not yet passed through. Utilisation at 85% versus a targeted 88-89% also cut margins by about 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: How much could DFC and JNPT linkage lift Gateway volumes and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to size; road-to-rail shift of about 10,000-15,000 TEU per month is possible, but shipping line routing decisions at JNPT are the main driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indian Railways likely to cut tariffs post-JNPT DFC linkage?
qa_highlights.answer: Representations have been made for tariff rationalisation to compete with Mundra and Pipavav, but management said it is too early to comment and expects incremental JNPT rail volume in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: What are Snowman's capex plans and how is expansion funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is through both build-to-suit and owned capacity, with about 23,000 pallets under construction and 20-odd thousand under discussion; no capex quantum was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jaipur ICD status?
qa_highlights.answer: All final arguments are complete and the order is reserved; if favourable, construction starts and operations take up to 18 months.

538666|2026-03.headline: Sharda Cropchem FY26 PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores on record revenue of INR 5,268 crores; FY27 revenue guided at 10-15%.
538666|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 13% YoY to INR 2,065 crores, with EBITDA up 75% to INR 513 crores and PAT up 57% to INR 319 crores. For FY26, revenue rose 22% to INR 5,268 crores, EBITDA rose 69% to INR 1,040 crores (19.7% margin), and PAT rose 124% to INR 681 crores. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 10-15%, gross margin around 35% plus or minus a few points, and EBITDA margin of 18-20%.

538666|2026-06.headline: Sharda Cropchem Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to Rs.1,074 crore and EBITDA 25% to Rs.178 crore, but reported PAT of Rs.88 crore was cushioned by lower forex gains.
538666|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs.1,074 crore, with volume down 1.6% and forex contributing 12.7 points. EBITDA margin expanded 220 bps to 16.6% and gross margin rose 120 bps to 36.7%, driven by mix in NAFTA, LATAM and rest of world. Europe revenue softened as distributors cut stock after an unusual heatwave, though Europe gross margin improved to 44.2%. Forex gain fell to Rs.7.5 crore from Rs.73.1 crore, so reported PBT and PAT looked weaker, while management said PBT before forex grew 16% to Rs.111 crore. segments.name: LATAM
segments.commentary: Among the strongest growth engines this quarter, but gross margin fell to 16.9% from 28.0% a year ago.

segments.name: Rest of world

538685|2026-06.headline: Shemaroo Q1 FY27 revenue fell 6% to about INR 132 crore, but EBITDA loss narrowed to about INR 2 crore from INR 56 crore.

Net loss reduced to about INR 8 crore. rows.why: Guidance is conservative on EBITDA-positive (described as a conservative aim), and the Q1 revenue fell 6% YoY, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Digital revenue fell 17% YoY to about INR 56 crore on lumpy B2B syndication deals, the traditional ad market is weak with a BARC ratings blackout, and quarterly fluctuations were flagged.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ten new ShemarooMe titles were released in Q1 and the OHO Gujarati catalogue (over 22 originals) was acquired in April 2026, so ongoing content launches are firmly under way, though no new brand or platform launch was named.

rows.label: New-initiative spend cut by over 50% in FY27
rows.why: New-initiative spend was about INR 20 crore in Q1 and management says it is on track to cut it by more than 50% versus FY26, which is the main driver of the EBITDA turn.

rows.label: Debt reduction plan for FY27
rows.why: Management confirmed a debt reduction plan for this year, but gave no amount, against total debt of INR 311 crore at quarter end.

rows.label: Inventory charge-off cycle normalised
rows.why: Management says no remaining write-down risk and a normal charge-off cycle now applies against INR 348 crore of inventory, which should stop the large write-downs that drove last year's losses.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost discipline, the EBITDA turn and content library strength, but evasive on debt targets, OTT subscriber data, profitability timing and a breakeven revenue threshold, and admitted margins are below its aspiration; analysts pressed on granularity and the path to profitab

538715|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, EBITDA up 45.6% to INR54.59 crores at a 20.6% margin, with the order book at a record INR174 crores.
538715|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 12.5% to INR264.48 crores, below management's earlier 20-25% target, because supplies on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR were deferred by buyers. Profitability improved sharply: EBITDA margin expanded 460 bps to 20.6%, PAT rose 67.2% to INR30.14 crores, and Q4 EBITDA margin crossed 21%. The company deployed about INR27 crores of capex in FY26 under a Board-approved INR100 crores programme spanning FY26-FY28, and entered aluminium windows and facade with INR56 crores of orders. Working capital rose as management paid suppliers early and stocked PVC resin and polymers ahead of West Asia-related price increases.

financial_highlights.change: Management says it will not reach 0.75
Record high; vs INR120-140 crores last year

segments.name: PVC/UPVC polymer products
segments.commentary: Management said about 84% of FY26 revenue (about INR220 crores) came from PVC and UPVC, of which about INR60 crores was UPVC windows and the rest PVC profiles. EBITDA margin in this segment was higher than modular; PBT margin was about 16.6%.

segments.name: Modular furniture (Dynasty)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR43 crores (about 16% of sales), with PBT margin around 9%, which management said was up about 80% YoY. Four new builder brands were added, including Godrej, M3M and Smart Homes, and exports to Europe are growing.

segments.name: Plastic profile core segment
segments.commentary: Revenue grew over 13% and segment profitability rose 63%, per management. PVC profile capacity rose by 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT per annum, with utilisation around 66% in FY26.

segments.name: Aluminium windows and facade (Bangalore/Jaipur)
segments.commentary: New vertical under Mr. Varghese with INR56 crores of orders and revenue starting in Q4 FY26. Management guides INR40-50 crores of FY27 revenue; it targets EBITDA margins of about 20%.

segments.name: WPC doors and WPC wall/ceiling panels
segments.commentary: WPC door line (about INR10 crores capex) has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27. Management expects about INR15 crores of FY27 revenue; WPC wall and ceiling profile lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Long-term target of about 30% revenue CAGR while sustaining EBITDA and PAT margins; management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is sustainable.
FY27 PVC profile extrusion volume growth of at least 20%; modular furniture growth of 20-25% expected.
FY27 new-capex revenue addition of INR55-60 crores, with aluminium facade INR40-50 crores and WPC doors about INR15 crores.
INR100 crores capex over FY26-FY28: about INR27 crores in FY26, INR35-40 crores in FY27 and INR20-30 crores in FY28.
Existing extrusion capacity can deliver more than INR450 crores of profile revenue at 85% utilisation; management did not give a year for reaching it.
Working capital expected to improve materially in FY27 as inventory is consumed and supplier payment cycles normalise.
capex_capacity: PVC profile extrusion capacity raised by 3,600 MT from 24,000 MT to 27,600 MT per annum in FY26; utilisation about 66%, with 80% cited as the practical benchmark.
WPC door line: machines commissioned and trials underway; commercial launch expected from Q2 FY27. WPC door capacity not yet finalised.
WPC wall and ceiling profile extrusion planned for Q3-Q4 FY27.
Aluminium windows and facade: Bangalore unit implemented; a new Jaipur factory site is under construction with capex planned in FY27. Custom fabrication, so no defined capacity.
Management expects ROE and ROCE of about 25-26% to be sustained on the new capex; it also said the new capex would earn similar returns across segments.
demand_pricing: Order book INR174 crores: UPVC windows and doors about INR84 crores, modular furniture about INR34 crores, aluminium windows and facade about INR56 crores; 100% expected to execute in 18-24 months.
Price hikes: three price revisions since the West Asia conflict began, up to 30 April. Management estimated 15-18% raw material cost inflation across its product lines.
Roughly 30% of revenue is fixed-price; B2B PVC profile distribution (over 60% of revenue) carries price revision clauses. Aluminium projects carry NALCO-linked base-price pass-through clauses.
Management said PVC resin fell from about INR115 in March to INR80-85 now; prices can move both ways.
Mobilisation advances of 10-20% of project value; net advances exceed INR7 crores versus about INR5 crores last year.
Management says WPC doors have no direct competition in India today; aluminium facade faces large international system brands and local fabricators.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the shortfall versus the 20-25% growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said buyers deferred supply on some large UPVC window and door projects in Maharashtra and one or two in Delhi NCR. Order book was healthy and the shortfall was described as timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is a 20%+ EBITDA margin sustainable amid raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing product mix, upgraded offerings for upper-middle and high-end customers, and pre-buying of raw materials in February-March. It expects price revisions to offset the 15-18% input cost rise.

qa_highlights.question: Why did payables fall to almost zero and inventory and receivables rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paid suppliers in full in the last two months of FY26 to secure supply during the Middle East disruption and bought PVC resin and polymers heavily in March. Receivables rose only in line with revenue, and it expects the cycle to normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to at least 20% volume growth in PVC profile extrusion, with new verticals adding on top. Price growth was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR100 crores capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly internal accruals (about INR50 crores of operating cash generation in FY26), with some borrowing. Debt-to-equity is currently 0.56 and is not expected to reach 0.75.

risks_watch: Revenue timing risk: deferred project deliveries by buyers caused the FY26 shortfall against the 20-25% target.
Raw material and aluminium price volatility tied to crude oil and LME aluminium; the aluminium contracts carry base-price clauses, but UPVC and modular contracts are largely fixed-price.
Working capital: inventory build, receivables growth and near-zero payables; management guided to normalisation in FY27.
Execution of the new WPC door launch in Q2 FY27 and the aluminium facade ramp-up, including the Jaipur factory build.
The 30% CAGR target rests on new verticals with no revenue history; management has not disclosed WPC capacity figures.
Margin sustainability: management says 20%+ EBITDA margin is durable, but competitive pricing and price-cut pressure are noted in the call.
538715|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins, capex and the 30% CAGR target, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss and the working capital build. Several answers were vague on volumes, pricing and WPC capacity, and some figures were corrected during the call.
key_quotes: Q4 was our strongest quarter ever, with EBITDA margin crossing 21% and PAT growth of nearly 55% year-on-year.
Importantly, this is a matter of timing, not a loss of business, as our underlying demand remains robust.
Based on our current visibility, we are targeting approximately 30% CAGR revenue growth over the long term while maintaining sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins.
It's a cost-plus pricing, definitely it's a cost-plus pricing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 460 bps to 20.6% in FY26 with Q4 above 21%, management calls 20%+ sustainable, and price revisions are expected to offset a 15-18% input cost rise; competitive price-cut pressure is a counterweight.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: PVC profile capacity rose 3,600 MT to 27,600 MT in FY26 (about 15%), WPC door line starts commercial launch in Q2 FY27, WPC wall/ceiling lines are planned for Q3-Q4 FY27, and the Jaipur aluminium factory is under construction with FY27 capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides a minimum 20% growth in PVC profile extrusion volume, with PVC utilisation at only 66%, a record INR174 crore order book, and modular growth guided at 20-25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: A Board-approved INR100 crore programme already covers FY26-FY28 (INR27 crore spent, INR35-40 crore in FY27), so new announcements depend on the WPC and Jaipur ramp; utilisation is only 66%, well below the 80% benchmark, which argues against an immediate new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Order book is a record INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, and FY27 new-capex revenue is guided at INR55-60 crore, but FY26 revenue grew only 12.5% against a 20-25% target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue missed the 20-25% target at 12.5% because buyers deferred UPVC projects in Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; the 30% CAGR is long-term with no year, and the WPC and aluminium ramps have no revenue history.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: WPC door line has finished trials and is due for commercial launch in Q2 FY27, with about INR15 crore of FY27 revenue expected; WPC wall and ceiling profiles follow in Q3-Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Record INR174 crore order book
rows.why: Order book is INR174 crore versus INR120-140 crore last year, with UPVC about INR84 crore, modular about INR34 crore and aluminium about INR56 crore, all expected to execute in 18-24 months.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation in FY27
rows.why: Payables fell to near zero after full supplier payments in the last two months of FY26, and inventory was built ahead of West Asia price rises; management expects the cycle to normalise in FY27, while net mobilisation advances rose to over INR7 crore from about INR5 crore.

rows.label: Raw material price revisions
rows.why: Three price revisions since the West Asia conflict, with 15-18% input inflation estimated; B2B PVC distribution (over 60% of revenue) has price revision clauses, but about 30% of revenue is fixed-price and PVC resin has fallen from about INR115 to INR80-85.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins above 20%, the INR100 crore capex and the 30% CAGR, but defensive on the FY26 revenue miss, the working capital build and vague WPC capacity figures; analysts pushed on volumes, pricing and the revenue shortfall.

538730|2026-03.headline: PDS FY26 revenue rose 4% to ₹13,110 crores, Q4 PAT nearly doubled QoQ to ₹72 crores, and the order book is up ~11% to ₹5,074 crores.
538730|2026-03.overview: PDS delivered FY26 GMV of about ₹19,666 crores (+5%) and revenue of ₹13,110 crores (+4%), with full-year PAT down to ₹178 crores from ₹241 crores. Q4 PAT rose about 95% QoQ to ₹72 crores on better operating leverage, cost control and lower finance costs. Net debt fell to about ₹105 crores from ₹374 crores despite the Knit Gallery acquisition. Management guided to mid-single-digit revenue growth and ~10% profit growth for FY27, with gross margin up 40-50 bps a year and opex growth below top-line growth; analysts pressed on the gap between order-book growth and the guidance.

financial_highlights.change: almost doubled YoY; includes ~₹19 crores MTM gains on venture investments
+16% YoY; ~3% like-for-like ex Knit Gallery; down ~5.4% QoQ
vs 10.1% in FY25; Q4 ETR ~7.9% after DTA on ₹14 crore impairment
vs ~17 days a year earlier; ex-New Lobster almost 0 or slightly negative

segments.name: Sourcing
segments.commentary: Revenue ~₹12,399 crores with EBIT of ₹266 crores in FY26, described as resilient.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 31% YoY to ~₹1,034 crores; EBIT rose to ₹57 crores (~5.5% margin), helped by factory utilisation and Knit Gallery integration.

segments.name: New Lobster (brands)
segments.commentary: Income from operations ~₹500 crores (vs ~₹480 crores), gross margin fell from ~30% to ~20% as the Ted Baker agency business dried up; PAT rose to ~₹38 crores from ~₹13 crores.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue flat YoY in USD (~+0.4%) and down ~4-5% QoQ; order book up ~30% YoY. Management said the US business was PBT positive in Q4.

segments.name: UK and Europe
segments.commentary: Order book growth low single digit (~3-4%).

segments.name: Asia
segments.commentary: Order book growth ~8-9%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 mid-single-digit revenue growth (~5-6%) and ~10% profit growth, with a cautious stance.
Gross margin to improve 40-50 bps a year over the next 1-2 years; EBITDA margin to improve 50-75 bps in FY27.
Employee and other expenses to grow more slowly than the top line in FY27; employee cost base ~₹1,310 crores.
New vertical investment to fall to ~₹80 crores in FY27, then ₹50-60 crores a year; no new verticals for the next 12 months.
Medium to long-term mid-teens growth targeted; management said the 5% PAT target is still behind.
Top-10 clients expected to grow ~7-8% in FY27; new verticals and North America to drive growth.
Net working capital to be held near current levels (~4 days).
capex_capacity: Capex in FY26 was reduced by more than half versus FY25.
Manufacturing footprint in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and India (Knit Gallery acquired).
Design-led sourcing draws on ~600 approved factories across Asia.
Project PULSE: AI-enabled digital backbone integrating sourcing, supplier governance, procurement, pricing and master data, building on BCG-led cost programme.
Restructuring: closed Design ARC branch and Lilly & Sid; consolidated Design ARC Asia and licensing into Poeticgem; exited Grupo and J-Craft.
demand_pricing: Order book as of early April 2026 ~₹5,074 crores, up ~11% YoY; North America up ~30%.
Secured a new sourcing-as-a-service mandate with a leading US value retailer, scalable beyond ~₹475 crores over time.
Customers remain cautious with shorter order cycles and selective deferments; no broad-based cancellations.
Management said some customers pushed back on shipments and held inventory in the past year.
Pipeline: large sourcing-as-a-service contracts (4-5 year terms) expected to be signed within 2-3 months; the company and Li & Fung are in RFQ stage for global sourcing contracts.
Design-led sourcing gross margin typically 15-18%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gross margin and EBITDA margin outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin to rise 40-50 bps average per year over 1-2 years; EBITDA margin to rise 50-75 bps this year, aided by lower one-off restructuring costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~16-17 day working capital sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not go back to 17 days and aims to hold current levels for the year, with quarterly fluctuations possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Poeticgem and Simple Approach margins erode?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to one-time redundancy costs from the BCG-led efficiency programme in H2; both verticals are expected to return to profit growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the order book growth (11%) not translate into higher revenue growth (5-6%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer caution on inventory and shipment pushbacks; UK and Europe order book is only ~3-4%, Asia ~8-9%, Americas ~30%.

qa_highlights.question: How does PDS keep winning share with retailers like Walmart?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of retailer sourcing goes through third-party vendors and that PDS offers four services: manufacturing, strategic vendor (design-led sourcing), sourcing-as-a-service, and brands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the Ted Baker (New Lobster) business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is negotiating with ABG for ~$2-2.5 million a year in financial support for 12 months, with a request to extend it for 24 more months; a conclusion is expected in 4-6 weeks.

risks_watch: Ted Baker franchise partner insolvencies; New Lobster support from ABG is only for 12 months (~$2-2.5 million).
Order book growth of 11% vs guided 5-6% revenue growth; Europe weakness after Matalan and Gerry Weber exits.
Brand business (wholesale) under review; further portfolio rationalisation and one-time costs possible.
Management did not reconcile the BCG-driven ~₹90-100 crore EBITDA uplift with only ~10% profit growth; analysts questioned this.
Other expenses rose ~16% (≈11% ex acquisitions), including royalty payments on curtailed brands and shutdown provisions.
Low Q4 effective tax rate (~7.9%) from DTA recognition; sustainability of the tax rate.
Concentration in top-10 clients (two faced challenges in FY26); top-10 growth guided at ~7-8%.
538730|2026-03.management_tone: Cautious but constructive: management repeatedly stressed "extreme caution" for FY27 and guided conservatively, while highlighting order-book growth, cost discipline and profit recovery. It was evasive on the US Q4 profit variance and on multi-year numeric targets, deferring follow-ups offline.
key_quotes: we are maintaining mid -single- digit growth outlook for the current year and then close to about 10% or so plus broad growth in the profits.
the growth in expenses should be slower than growth in the top line.
we are surely not going to allow it to go back to 17 days.
