rows.when: FY27 (EBITDA +50-75 bps); gross margin +40-50 bps a year ove
rows.why: Management guided EBITDA margin up 50-75 bps in FY27 and gross margin up 40-50 bps a year, aided by lower one-off restructuring costs; FY26 gross margin already rose 48 bps to 20.6%, but EBITDA fell to ₹385 crores from ₹457 crores.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capex was cut by more than half vs FY25 and the brief gives no new plant, line or capacity commissioning dates; the growth story is asset-light sourcing and order book conversion.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book ~₹5,074 crores (+~11% YoY, Americas +~30%) and guided revenue growth of ~5-6%, though UK/Europe order book is only ~3-4% and customers are pushing back on shipments.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was reduced by more than half in FY26 and no utilisation or capacity constraint is reported; new investment is limited to ~₹80 crores in FY27 for verticals, not plant capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was explicitly cautious ('extreme caution') and guided FY27 revenue to ~5-6% and profit to ~10%, with analysts questioning the gap to the 11% order-book growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order book growth of 11% is not converting into revenue (5-6% guided), UK/Europe order book only ~3-4%, customers holding inventory, and New Lobster support from ABG covers only 12 months (~$2-2.5 million).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Large 4-5 year sourcing-as-a-service contracts expected to be signed within 2-3 months, and a new US value-retailer mandate scalable beyond ~₹475 crores; but management said no new verticals for the next 12 months.

rows.label: Sourcing-as-a-service contracts in RFQ/pipeline
rows.why: Large 4-5 year sourcing-as-a-service contracts expected to be signed within 2-3 months, and a US value-retailer mandate scalable beyond ~₹475 crores, against an order book of ~₹5,074 crores (+~11%).

rows.label: Project PULSE and BCG cost programme
rows.why: BCG-led programme and AI backbone expected to support margin, with management guiding opex growth below top-line growth and new vertical investment falling to ~₹80 crores in FY27 from higher levels; analysts noted an unreconciled ~₹90-100 crore EBITDA uplift.

rows.label: Net debt near zero, dividend payout ~42%
rows.why: Net debt fell to ~₹105 crores (Mar-26) from ₹374 crores, ~0.27x net debt/EBITDA, with ₹781 crores operating cash flow and ₹3.3 per share dividend proposed.

tone.note: Management stressed 'extreme caution' for FY27 and guided conservatively, highlighting order book, cost discipline and profit recovery; analysts pressed on the gap between 11% order-book growth and 5-6% revenue guidance, and on the unreconciled BCG-driven EBITDA uplift.

538730|2026-06.headline: PDS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹3,444 crore, EBITDA up 90% to ₹96 crore, and net debt fell 73% to ₹29 crore.
538730|2026-06.overview: PDS reported Q1 FY27 revenue of ₹3,444 crore (+15% YoY), with gross margin up 63 bps to 20% and EBITDA of ₹96 crore (margin 2.8%, +111 bps). PAT rose 43% YoY to ₹29 crore, though other income fell to ₹9 crore from ₹40 crore that included a ₹22 crore FX gain last year. Order book grew 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crore, and management announced new mandates with annual potential of about US$330 million. Net working capital fell to 1 day and net debt to ₹29 crore, with management stating a commitment to low single-digit working capital days.

financial_highlights.change: +8% YoY in INR; -2.4% YoY and -6.2% QoQ in USD
vs ₹40 crore in Q1 FY26 (which included ~₹22 crore FX gain)
+11% YoY in INR; flat in USD
down 73% from ₹105 crore at Mar-26; net debt/equity 0.02x, net debt/EBITDA 0.07x

segments.name: Sourcing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹3,272 crore (+16% YoY), EBIT ₹58 crore, EBIT margin 1.8%; the key contributor to the quarter.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹227 crore (+4% YoY), EBIT ₹15 crore, EBIT margin 6.5%; management aims to upgrade customer mix toward fashion customers via the Busana partnership.

segments.name: New verticals investment
segments.commentary: Investment of ₹37 crore in Q1 vs ₹41 crore last year (-8%); brand management investment down 38%, design-led sourcing down 5%, North America investment up on GSCL scale-up.

segments.name: Americas / Europe
segments.commentary: Americas revenue grew 48% YoY; Europe revenue grew 21%.

guidance_outlook: Management asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating Q1 trend; will revisit guidance after mid-year.
Interest cost guided flat-to-down in USD terms, with early payment discounts (EPD) offsetting lower interest cost; more disclosure on EPD vs gross margin planned from Q2.
Working capital expected to stay at low single-digit days, possibly 0-1 days in some quarters.
Ted Baker losses for FY27 expected not to exceed US$2-3 million; Q1 loss approx US$2 million PBT.
Venture investment capped at under ₹10 crore a year (US$1-1.5 million).
Expect new sourcing-as-a-service contracts to ramp over 12-24 months; the French retailer contract has option value of US$300-400 million GMV within 2 years.
Management said the 555 target is still a long-term goal, with focus on sequential EBITDA margin and PAT improvement each quarter.
capex_capacity: Asset-light sourcing model used to add capacity; management said it could onboard 4-5 third-party factories within ~6 months for a large account, versus a US$50-60 million manufacturing investment otherwise.
Depreciation increase reflects Knit Gallery acquisition and capitalisation of UK office property.
Ongoing SAP upgrade to S/4HANA and AI/digital investment across sourcing, pricing, supply management and operations.
Sourcing-as-a-service GMV under execution in Q1 was ~₹1,700 crore; 600 partner factories cited across the platform.
Sourcing geography: >50% of sourcing from Bangladesh; expanding India (Knit Gallery) and exploring Egypt.
demand_pricing: New mandates from marquee customers with annual business potential ~US$330 million, with 3-4 year contract horizons.
Sourcing-as-a-service GMV of ~₹1,700 crore in Q1 generated ~₹42 crore revenue (~2.5% of GMV) and ~₹10 crore PBT (~25% of revenue).
US accounts reopened or added: Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS, American Eagle; management says 70-80% of key US accounts are now opened.
Europe: growth from Mango (Spain), CCC (Poland); Gerry Weber's bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.
Marks & Spencer reportedly exploring a 50/50 in-house vs third-party sourcing split; opportunity cited at US$100 million (not yet confirmed as a contract).

New Lobster (brand management) revenue ~₹100 crore in Q1; other licensed brands ~₹350 crore annually (~₹90 crore per quarter) and profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Order book up 23% and Q4 up 11% versus earlier mid-single-digit guidance; should growth be much higher this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the order book has shaped up well and management is positive, but asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating the Q1 trend and to revisit guidance after mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Are new-vertical investments on track for the ~₹80 crore annual scale-down, given Q1 at ₹37 crore, and how will US investment and PBT be factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects more profitability over coming quarters and said the full-year P&L impact of new initiatives would broadly be in line with prior expectations; no explicit ₹80 crore reconfirmation was given.

qa_highlights.question: Finance cost stayed flat despite lower net debt; will it keep rising with factoring as revenue grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said interest cost is not going up, with quarterly ups and downs possible. Sanjay Jain said USD interest cost is stagnant and directionally flat or lower, with early payment discounts (EPD) offsetting interest, and more EPD-vs-gross-margin disclosure from Q2. Average USD borrowing cost is about 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a cost-saving lever only or also a revenue driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said AI currently drives productivity, citing a China subsidiary with 60 staff whose turnover doubled to $120 million, with local software under $25,000 a year. Customer-facing AI design helped win the French retailer contract.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1-day working capital a cyclical mix effect or structural, and could it return to negative as in FY23?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said the 1 day reflects a higher share of factorable receivables; structurally management guides to low single-digit days, with 0 to 1 days possible in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Americas (+48%) and Europe (+21%) growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth said 70-80% of key US accounts are now open and volumes are scaling, with Coles, Walmart, Fashion Nova, T.J. Maxx, PBS and American Eagle cited. In Europe, growth came from Mango (Spain) and CCC (Poland), with new German accounts replacing Gerry Weber.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the 555 target today given macro and currency factors?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said 555 remains a long-term goal; the Gerry Weber and Matalan (about US$140 million to US$70 million) setbacks cost 12-18 months of stabilisation. Management now focuses on sequential EBITDA margin and PAT improvement each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the outsourced opportunity and how does PDS grow wallet share once inside a retailer? Is there a risk retailers bypass PDS to deal with factories directly?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth cited Marks & Spencer exploring a 50/50 in-house vs third-party split, with a US$100 million opportunity that PDS could serve asset-light with 4-5 third-party factories in about 6 months versus US$50-60 million of capex. He said standalone factories have little value and PDS's factories are the next tier, not the top 5-10.

qa_highlights.question: How much Ted Baker loss is in Q1 and for FY27, and what is the resolution path?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said Q1 Ted Baker PBT loss was about US$2 million and FY27 losses should not exceed US$2-3 million. Discussions with Authentic Brands Group are ongoing after franchisee administration in the UK and US.

538882|2026-03.headline: Emerald Finance Q4 FY26 net profit INR4.364 crore; management reiterates FY27 EPS target above INR7 versus INR4.36 in FY26.
538882|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR9.76 crore against INR6.49 crore in Q4 FY25, with net profit of INR4.364 crore. FY26 total income was INR31.2 crore and net profit INR15.15 crore, though the transcript cites EPS of INR4.36 for both the quarter and the year, which needs verification. CRISIL upgraded the rating from BB+ to BBB-. Management said EWA disbursements slowed in the quarter because of market volatility, with corporate rejection rates near 60%. Several figures given on the call were inconsistent or deferred to email, including EWA revenue share, NPA breakup and the SME loan book.

segments.commentary: About 180-185 corporates active; 214 corporates on books as of March 31, 2026, though the 185 figure was also cited. Around 30,000+ employees covered, with 15% using EWA monthly and monthly repeat rate about 90%. Average loan INR25,000, cap INR1 lakh per transaction, and the lower of 50% of salary or INR1 lakh applies.

segments.name: Cross-sell (personal, home, gold loans, LAP)
segments.commentary: Cross-sell disbursal was about INR12 crore in Q4, now larger than EWA disbursal of INR10 crore. Yields vary by product: about 4% on personal loans, about 1% on gold loans and 1-1.25% on home loans or LAP. Most cross-sell is 100% distributed; small-ticket loans of INR4-5 lakh are booked on balance sheet.

segments.name: SME / business loans
segments.commentary: Book is INR111 crore per management. Management guided to decent growth in FY27 without a number, and expects cross-selling to EWA corporates to contribute.

segments.name: Gold loan syndication
segments.commentary: INR375 crore disbursed in Q4 through banking and NBFC partners.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS target: management said if all goes well, EPS should cross INR7 in FY27, versus INR4.36 in FY26; repeated in Q&A. Earlier call guidance of FY27 profit of INR32-40 crore was raised by an analyst; management did not restate that range.

Corporate additions: 150-200 companies targeted for FY27 by Talin Aggarwal, versus a later answer of 120-150 corporates per year over the next two years; management said the bare minimum is about 30 per quarter and that systems could handle 400-500 corporates in the year.
EWA disbursement growth: management pointed to continued growth at the pace of the last eight quarters, and said it could increase; no numeric disbursal guidance given.
Cost of funds: management said offers from financial institutions are being received after the CRISIL upgrade and an update would follow shortly; no reduction achieved yet as of the call.

Revenue growth: Sanjay Aggarwal said Q4 top line was about 25% higher than the prior quarter. Talin Aggarwal said FY27 profit growth would be at roughly the same pace as FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.
SME book: management expects decent growth in FY27 without a number, with a large proposal pipeline and cross-sell to EWA corporates.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.

Platform: proprietary API-driven platform for onboarding, salary validation and disbursement; Emerald EWA mobile app rolled out; WhatsApp disbursement; cross-sell module added to app and portal, giving instant checks with partner banks.
Partners: more than 40 financial partners and 14 lenders, per management.
Targeted corporate additions for FY27 were given in the Q&A, not as capex or capacity.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 EWA disbursal was about INR10 crore against guidance of INR11.5-12 crore for the quarter-end run rate; cross-sell disbursal was INR12 crore, now larger than EWA.
Corporate rejection rate is about 60%, based on CIBIL or banking checks; management attributed the slowdown to market volatility over the past three to four months.

Cross-sell yields: about 4% on personal loans, about 1% on gold loans, 1-1.25% on home loan or LAP; management said the blended yield changes every quarter. Management gave 1.3% as the cross-sell average when asked.

EWA revenue: management said about 6% of Q4 income came from EWA alone, while the presentation cited 8% for the full year on an EWA-overall basis; an analyst's Q4 EWA revenue estimate of INR70-80 lakh was not confirmed.
Gold loan syndication: INR375 crore disbursed in Q4 through ICICI, HDFC, RBL and Muthoot Finance.

Employee profile: average salary of EWA users about INR55,000-60,000; average loan INR25,000; cap INR1 lakh; minimum as low as INR100. Share of covered employees using EWA monthly is 15%; monthly repeat rate about 90%.

SME book: INR111 crore, corrected from the analyst's INR120-130 crore figure.

qa_highlights.answer: Talin Aggarwal said Q4 EWA disbursal was INR10 crore because the market became highly volatile in the past three to four months, with corporate rejection near 60% on CIBIL or banking grounds.

538882|2026-06.headline: Emerald Finance Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit rose 52.72% YoY to Rs 4.88 Cr; gold loan distribution slowdown dented top line.
538882|2026-06.overview: Management reported consolidated total income up 39.97% YoY to Rs 9.44 Cr and net profit up 52.72% to Rs 4.88 Cr, with diluted EPS at 1.44 versus 0.92. Gold loan distribution fell sharply (Rs 290 Cr in Q1 vs Rs 375 Cr in Q4), which management said pushed distribution income down and made the quarter-on-quarter top line decline. EWA's share of consolidated revenue rose to about 10.5%, and the EWA monthly run rate was stated at Rs 26 Cr. Management reiterated FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 but gave no quarterly bridge, and analysts questioned the pace required.

financial_highlights.change: +52.72% YoY; ~12.5% QoQ per analyst question, not disputed
~Rs 16 Cr from banks incl. SBI; rest from NBFCs
Rs 12.5 Cr EWA, remainder MSME and personal loans

segments.name: EWA (Early Wage Access)
segments.commentary: Monthly run rate of Rs 26 Cr (Rs 12.5 Cr EWA disbursal + Rs 13.5 Cr cross-sell distribution) vs Rs 22 Cr in Q4 (Rs 10 Cr + Rs 12 Cr). Average ticket size Rs 26,000; 32 corporates onboarded in Q1, about 210 active companies at 30 June; ~40,000 registered employees.

segments.name: Gold loan distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution volume fell to Rs 290 Cr in Q1 from Rs 375 Cr in Q4 due to RBI restrictions on banks and NBFCs; distribution fees about 0.9-1% on average (HDFC ~1.25%, ICICI ~0.75%, RBL ~1%). Management expects recovery from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: MSME and personal loans / interest income
segments.commentary: Interest income is primarily MSME working capital loans. Management expects good MSME growth in FY27; home loan, LAP and business loan books described as steady.

segments.name: Education loans (Credila alliance)
segments.commentary: Started during the quarter; about Rs 1 Cr disbursed in the last month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 reiterated; management said growth momentum should pick up from Q2 and that Q1 is seasonally slow.
Analyst arithmetic: EPS 7 implies roughly 66% PAT growth YoY, assuming no equity dilution; management said no equity dilution is planned.
Management expects PAT growth of about 40-50% over the next 2-3 years, with PAT margin stabilising at 40-45%.
EWA revenue share expected to stabilise at 30-40% (management wording); a separate remark put it at 12-15%. Management said this was not a firm target.
Management declined to give a March 2027 EWA run-rate target, stating it has no internal number; guided to 10-12% QoQ growth in EWA.
capex_capacity: Borrowing headroom: management says Rs 63 Cr more debt could be raised, keeping debt-equity near 1:1; SBI enhancement proposal under process; ICICI line of Rs 10 Cr announced.
New products (digital gold/silver, small-ticket SIP, pocket insurance) expected to launch within a month via app, web portal and WhatsApp; still in vendor integration.
AU Small Finance Bank partnership for gold loans started this quarter; management is exploring at least one more bank partner.
Management said no capital raise or co-lending is planned for EWA.
demand_pricing: Gold loan distribution slowed sharply; management expects no rebound this quarter and a pick-up from Q3 or Q4 FY27 when banks relax norms.
A single new corporate (BSE-listed, ~11,000 employees) was onboarded; only ~1,000 employees from one plant are live, with six more plants pending.
Repeat usage: management cited ~90% repeat rate for EWA users; seasonal peaks in March and around Diwali (+100-200 bps).
Portfolio-level EWA yield or fee rate was not disclosed beyond ~10-13% range commentary; NPA-related cost remarks included in Q&A below.
Competition: MoneyView (owns Jify), Refyne and Fable named; management expects more fintech entrants and plans LSP/RE partnerships with startups.

qa_highlights.question: Are NPAs rising too fast, and is there a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPAs are about half of provisions, with provisions at about 0.3-0.35% of book. EWA 90+ provisions of about Rs 3 lakh were roughly matched by write-offs; business and personal loans had about Rs 8 lakh provisioned against Rs 6 lakh written off in the quarter, and Rs 4 lakh was recovered on earlier write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why was EWA onboarding limited to about 30 corporates a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 60-64 corporates were evaluated to onboard 32, with a rejection rate of about 50-55% due to macro stress, so onboarding is slow and risk-led. Growth expected at 10-12% QoQ, with large corporates as the expected source of a sharp jump.

qa_highlights.question: Will EWA co-lending or a capital raise be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no. Co-lending was described as unsuitable for EWA because it charges no interest and earns only a disbursement fee; debt-equity headroom is ample.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and depreciation costs fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to lower gold-loan incentives paid to employees and DSAs (about 40% of gold-loan business goes to staff or DSAs), with more direct EWA sourcing that carries no commission. Management said it would check the depreciation decline with auditors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fees and commission expenses drop?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is sourcing more direct business through employees, so it pays fewer outside DSA fees. Fee payments were described as one-time costs per referral.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AUM growth and credit cost target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No numeric AUM growth or credit cost target was given; management cited AUM of Rs 125 Cr at 30 June with headroom to grow EWA and MSME books.

risks_watch: Gold loan distribution recovery timing: management expects no rebound in Q2 and a pick-up only from Q3 or Q4 FY27 as banks relax RBI-driven norms; distribution is about half of the Rs 26 Cr EWA monthly run rate and is outside management's control.

FY27 EPS guidance of about 7 (implies ~66% PAT growth with no dilution) versus Q1 PAT growth of about 52.7% YoY and ~12.5% QoQ; the gap depends on large corporate onboarding that is not yet quantified.

EWA onboarding pace: 32 corporates added in Q1 after evaluating 60-64, with a rejection rate of about 50-55%; only ~1,000 of ~11,000 employees at the new BSE-listed client are live, with six plants pending.
Asset quality: management cites NPAs at about half of provisions, but NPA trend was questioned in Q&A; watch 90+ DPD, write-offs and standard-asset provisioning (~0.3% vs RBI 0.25% floor).
Competitive intensity from MoneyView (Jify), Refyne and Fable plus expected new entrants; management's LSP/RE partnership plan and MOUs are not yet disclosed to the exchange.

Revenue mix: management gave inconsistent EWA revenue-share targets (30-40% vs 12-15%) and declined a March 2027 run-rate target; borrowing headroom of Rs 63 Cr relies on SBI enhancement and new bank lines still in process.
key_quotes: We are pleased to begin FY'27 on a steady note, delivering healthy growth across all of our key financial parameters other than the goal loan business.
I think we should be able to achieve the guidance of 7, we should be able to match that.
Talin Aggarwal: Sir, honestly, we cannot comment on that. Because almost 50% of it is made of distribution income.
Sanjay Aggarwal: No. We don't want to. We're not short of funds.

538920|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 57.2% YoY to INR165.3 crore with EBITDA margin of 18.5%; capacity now 11,000 MT after brownfield expansion.
538920|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR165.3 crore, up 57.2% YoY and 9.8% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR30.6 crore (18.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crore (12.7% margin). For FY26 consolidated revenue rose 79.3% to INR553.1 crore, EBITDA rose 88.1% to INR99.6 crore, and PAT rose 79.8% to INR72.2 crore. Installed capacity rose from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT through an internally funded brownfield expansion, now fully operational from Q1 FY27. Management guided to about 95% utilisation (10,200–10,400 MT) in FY27 and a 5,500 MT freeze-dried coffee (FDC) plant by Q2 FY28, with a larger capex and debt plan outlined.

segments.name: Spray / agglomerated coffee (bulk and packed)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after expansion from 6,500 MT; packed-form share rose from about 35% to about 53% in FY26, and FY27 packed share expected to grow a further 5–10%. Packing capacity is 5,000 MT with one more line being added, targeting a 40:60 bulk-to-packed ratio.

segments.name: Freeze-dried coffee (FDC)
segments.commentary: 5,500 MT plant with capex of about INR550 crore, of which about INR150 crore is spent; commercial operations expected from July 2027 after a three-month trial, with about 70% utilisation and about 9 months of output in FY28. A phase 2 of another 5,500 MT is planned for FY29-30 at INR370–400 crore, with land and building already being planned for it.

segments.name: Sales mix by geography
segments.commentary: Africa about 31%, CIS and Russia about 22%, Southeast Asia about 22%, Americas and Europe about 18%, local sales about 5%. Top five to six of 19–20 customers contribute about 45–50% of business.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume: about 95% utilisation of 11,000 MT, implying production of about 10,200–10,400 MT; Q1 has annual maintenance of 15–20 days and about 70–75% of FY27 sales are projected to be covered; Q2 projected sales of 2,300–2,400 MT.
FY27 realisation expected slightly better than FY26 on product mix (consumer packs and agglomerated); management cited 2–3% improvement.
FY27 EBITDA margin shows slight improvement over FY26; management targets about 19% (current 18.5% plus about 0.5% from utilisation).
FY28 margin expected to improve further (about 20–21% with 8–9 months of FDC output); FY29 margin 22–24%.
FY27 operating cash flow expected positive overall, with Q1 seasonally negative and Q3–Q4 positive.

FY27 debt expected to rise by about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%. Peak debt for the FDC project of about INR400 crore (INR300 crore ECB at about 5–6% including hedging, plus INR100 crore working capital at about 8.3–8.4%).
capex_capacity: Brownfield expansion from 6,500 MT to 11,000 MT completed in FY26 using internal accruals; expanded capacity fully operational from Q1 FY27.

FDC plant of 5,500 MT: capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent, remaining about INR400 crore to be spent over roughly the next year; commissioning by March 2027, trial run for three months, commercial operations from July 2027, completion stated as Q2 FY28.
FDC phase 2 (5,500 MT) planned for FY29-30 at about INR370–400 crore; management said funding through internal accruals may be difficult and ECB may be required.
Packing capacity 5,000 MT, with one additional packing line being added.
demand_pricing: Management said geopolitical tensions have had no direct impact as the company does not focus on Middle East or Western Asia; focus is Central America, America, Europe, Africa, Southeast Asia and Russia.
Coffee prices described as stable and expected to continue at current levels; packaging input costs (metal tins, aluminium) rose slightly and were passed to customers, improving realisation slightly.
Realisation management said is driven by product mix, not coffee bean prices; company operates a cost-plus model.
Global instant coffee production (including freeze-dried) is about 1,000,000 MT, growing about 30,000 MT per year, per management.
Management said it has no plans to enter retail; focus is on e-commerce and local presence.
EBITDA per kg for Q4 was similar to Q3; Q4 volume was 1,924 MT versus 1,802 MT in Q3 (one answer cited 1,824 MT for Q4 before correcting to 1,924 MT).

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the expanded plant and expected run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant is at full capacity of 11,000 MT and expects about 95% utilisation for FY27, with 95% of production exported.

qa_highlights.question: FDC capex and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR550 crore, about INR150 crore spent; remaining about INR400 crore over roughly the next year. Commissioning by March 2027, commercial operations from July 2027 (not a six-month delay, per management).

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: additional about INR300 crore term debt plus INR100 crore working capital for FY28, so peak debt about INR400 crore additional. FY27 debt up about INR30–40 crore over FY26 at about 8.3–8.4%.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 based on 11,000 MT at about 95% utilisation with slightly better prices. FY28 includes about 9 months of FDC at 70% utilisation. Margins improve in FY28 and further in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Phase 2 capex and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 about INR370–400 crore with land and building already planned; funding through internal accruals may be difficult, so ECB is likely.

qa_highlights.question: Customer concentration and FDC go-to-market?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19–20 customers globally; top five to six contribute about 45–50%. FDC to be sold to existing customers and new markets.

risks_watch: Phase 2 FDC funding (about INR370–400 crore) is not yet secured; management said internal accruals may be insufficient and ECB may be needed.
Customer concentration: top five to six customers are about 45–50% of business.
Ramp-up risk: FY27 utilisation of 95% of 11,000 MT depends on customer visibility, and Q1 has a lean season and maintenance shutdown.
FDC commissioning and commercial start (July 2027) and ramp to 70% utilisation are untested.
Debt rises to about INR400 crore additional, with ECB hedging cost and interest rates in the 5–6% and 8.3–8.4% range.
Investor relations responsiveness: management said it would check and replace the investor email ID after an analyst reported unanswered emails.

key_quotes: Around 95% capacity utilization will be there this year out of the 11,000 metric tons, and 95% of whatever production we are doing, the entire thing will be exported because we see visibility for the orders and sales.
At this point in time, it is very difficult for me to comment on the second phase because funding it through internal accruals may be difficult. We may have to go for ECB only.
Ours is a cost-plus model, so it does not have an impact from coffee bean prices.

538920|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 58.4% YoY to INR161 crore and PAT 46.1% to INR20.8 crore, with 1,856 MT sold against 2,402 MT produced.
538920|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR161 crore (+58.4% YoY), EBITDA INR31.6 crore (+75.2%) and PAT INR20.8 crore (+46.1%), with a 12.9% PAT margin. The 4,500 MT capacity added at end-FY26 ran at about 90-95% utilisation, taking installed capacity to 11,000 MT. Management said the NCLT approved the merger of two wholly owned subsidiaries effective 21 July 2026, and freeze-dried coffee (FDC) capacity of 5,500 MT is under construction for start in Q2 FY28. Q1 was a seasonal lean quarter, with production exceeding sales and inventory building ahead of Q2 deliveries.

Management figure; analyst calculation of INR172 included chicory

segments.commentary: Installed capacity 11,000 MT after 4,500 MT added at end-FY26; packing capacity 5,000 MT; Q1 packing mix 45% bulk and 55% consumer packs. Management guided FY27 volume of about 10,500 MT at 95% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins keep rising, and what is the FDC start timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expected to rise 0.5-1% from Q1 levels. FDC trials by June 2027 with production from Q2 FY28; 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months, adding about 2,400 MT in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue potential and the chicory contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 revenue ballpark is INR850-900 crore on 10,500 MT. Chicory revenue is INR40-45 crore a year, and EBITDA from chicory in Q1 was about INR2.1 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the debt and capex plans for FDC?

qa_highlights.question: Why are working capital days high at 120-130 and when does cash flow improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth inventory is the main reason; CFO said FY27 operating cash flow will be positive, with working capital days around 125 and the FY27 cash-generation capacity estimated at about INR79 crore if growth inventory was not needed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any hedging or inventory loss risk given production above sales in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said beans are bought back-to-back, with 40-45 days of stock held; surplus Q1 production is expected to be picked up by customers in Q2.

risks_watch: FDC ramp-up: 5,500 MT line depends on June 2027 trials, with production from Q2 FY28 and FY28 volume of about 2,400 MT at 60-65% utilisation over 8-9 months; LOIs cover 70-80% of capacity but are subject to quality and price.

539056|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR178 crores and EBITDA 24% to INR90 crores (50.7% margin), with footfalls up 22%.
539056|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR178 crores, with footfalls up 22% to over 11.5 lakh visitors and parks revenue up 22% to INR161 crores. EBITDA rose 24% to INR90 crores and PAT rose 30% to INR58 crores. Management attributed the soft spots to an extended heat wave that kept Khopoli park non-operational for about two weeks and a shift in some CBSE school holiday calendars, and said it deliberately priced softer to build footfall. Management also announced the acquisition of a 50.002% stake in Mehsana Next Parks (Shanku's Water Park) for INR50 crores and the entry into indoor entertainment via a Hello Park franchise.

qa_highlights.question: Is like-for-like growth weak given Q1 FY25 revenue of about INR184 crores vs INR177 crores now, and is ARPU flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the heat wave, Khopoli closure and school calendar shifts; it chose softer pricing to push footfall and expects headroom to correct pricing over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Hello Park economics: margins after rent, royalty and year-one footfall/ARPU?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket price target INR800-900; ticketing about 65-70% of revenue; EBITDA margin 24-25% after mall rent; royalty 5% of revenue; capex about INR10 crores per 10,000 sq ft centre; payback 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Jai Malpani said the promoter group is positive and the conversion will happen before the due date.

qa_highlights.answer: Mix of internal accruals and moderate debt; average debt/EBITDA 2.5-3x, up to 3-3.5x for a limited period.

qa_highlights.question: Dave & Buster's integration timing?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm timeline; the model is still being stabilised; not expected in the next three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gujarat ARPU drop sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat price sensitivity; a deliberate price test; adjoining hotel and mall not yet operational; expected to recover over time.

539083|2026-03.headline: Inox Wind Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue flat YoY at INR1,306 crore; FY27 guidance of ~75% revenue growth and 20%+ EBITDA margin.
539083|2026-03.overview: Inox Wind reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR1,306 crore (flat YoY), EBITDA of INR333 crore, PBT of INR216 crore, PAT of INR106 crore and cash profit of INR268 crore, with FY26 revenue of about INR4,500 crore against an earlier INR5,000 crore target. Management attributed the shortfall to geopolitical disruption: delayed imported ECS components, shipping and commodity cost pressures, and a PSU contract with payment delays. The company is pivoting from turnkey EPC to equipment supply, with equipment supply now about 50% of the order book and a target of 75% to 80%. Inox Green (O&M) reported Q4 total income of INR120 crore (up 40% YoY) and EBITDA of INR57 crore, and it is guided to above INR600 crore EBITDA in FY27 after consolidating two pending acquisitions and a demerger.

financial_highlights.value: INR4,600 crore against INR5,000 crore guideline
financial_highlights.change: INR400 crore shortfall expected to be recovered in Q1-Q2 FY27
about INR40 crore from acquisition-linked debt, about INR10 crore value-added services, about INR10 crore treasury

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG/EPC)
segments.commentary: Consolidated Q4 revenue INR1,306 crore flat YoY with EBITDA INR333 crore; order book 3.1 GW, with about 600 MW added in FY26, and visibility of more than 24 months. Only about 500 MW of the order book is from group company Inox Clean.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 (approx. INR7,500 crore on a INR4,500 crore base), with EBITDA margin of about 20% (stated as '20% to 20%').

Group Inox Clean targets about 14 GW capacity by FY29, adding about 3 GW+ annually, of which 20-30% is expected to be wind, to drive recurring orders for Inox Wind.

capex_capacity: Inox Green's two acquisitions cover about 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M assets; entity one order expected within a couple of weeks, entity two expected within 60-90 days.

Evacuation infrastructure demerger from Inox Green into Inox Renewable Solutions approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; about INR1,000 crore gross block and INR50-55 crore annual depreciation removed. Completion expected in 1-2 months.
Cranes moving in-house (half in-house, a couple more due this year); power transformer manufacturing started last year and ramping up.
Management plans to expand into power electronics (transformers, inverters, power electronics, ECS) with details to follow in coming months.
Group Inox Clean has about 2 GW installed, 6 GW solar module and 3 GW cell capacity; targets 10 GW each of IPP, cell and module over about 15 months.
demand_pricing: Order book 3.1 GW, diversified; recent wins include Aditya Birla, Gentari/Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green. Multiple customer negotiations near closure.
Order mix is about 50:50 turnkey to equipment supply, targeted to move to 75% equipment supply (management also cited 75-80%).

Management says margins are guided at about 20% or higher on equipment supply; equipment supply is on LC terms, passing steel price changes through, reducing exposure to land/ROW cost and payment delays.
Revenue mix: about 10% O&M and 90% Inox Wind currently; O&M expected to rise to about 18-20% of consolidated revenue.
Management said it does not have FY27 order inflow targets and is 'sold out' for about 2.5 years on its stated ambitions.

qa_highlights.question: How will the two Inox Green acquisitions contribute to EBITDA and when will they be consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both acquisitions carry roughly 50% EBITDA margins, as they are former OEMs with substations and evacuation systems. Entity one's order is expected within a couple of weeks; entity two is 60-90 days away, and all revenues from 1 April 2026 are to be reflected in consolidated results.

qa_highlights.question: What was the FY26 working capital position against the INR5,000 crore guideline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it achieved INR4,600 crore against the INR5,000 crore guideline, with the INR400 crore balance expected in Q1-Q2 FY27 after supply-chain issues from delayed imported ECS components.

qa_highlights.question: What was actual MW execution in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give megawatt execution, saying the company guides on revenue only, and reiterated this stated policy.

qa_highlights.question: Will equipment supply shift raise margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins stay at about 20% or higher, with equipment supply carrying less risk and more upfront cash; O&M at about 50% margin would add a higher-margin bias.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of INR61 crore at Inox Green: how much is recurring and how much is treasury?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR40 crore relates to the two acquisitions (debt-linked, net of deferred tax, roughly INR25-26 crore at PAT level), INR10 crore is value-added services and INR10 crore is treasury income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Inox Green revenue fall QoQ from about INR78 crore to INR69 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the quarterly variation to value-added services timing (about INR8-9 crore) and said the annualised run-rate is the right measure.

539083|2026-06.headline: Inox Wind Q1 FY27 consol revenue INR872 crores, adjusted EBITDA INR237 crores (~27% margin), PAT INR64 crores; FY27 guidance of 75% revenue growth reaffirmed.
539083|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue was INR872 crores with adjusted EBITDA of INR237 crores, PBT of INR95 crores, PAT of INR64 crores and cash profit of INR153 crores. Management said the pivot toward equipment supply (about 59% of third-party order book as of July 2026) is disrupting near-term revenue, with benefits expected from Q2-end and mainly in H2. The order book is about 4.4 GW after a 200 MW NLC India LOA, and an MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean (500 MW firm). Analysts pressed hard on the H2-weighted guidance, flat year-on-year Wind revenue and the pending INR400 crore deferred revenue, and management largely refused to quantify quarterly numbers.

financial_highlights.change: No year-on-year growth cited; management said Q1 is at par with Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR57.9 crores, of which INR50+ crores operational

segments.name: Inox Wind (WTG and EPC)
segments.commentary: Order book about 4.4 GW as of July 2026, with equipment supply about 59% and turnkey 41% for third-party orders. Management says equipment-supply margin and revenue benefits show from Q2-end, predominantly H2.

segments.name: INOX Green (O&M)
segments.commentary: Q1 total income INR101 crores, EBITDA INR57 crores, PAT INR41 crores; machine availability ~96.3%. Own portfolio ~13.3 GW peak (10.5 GW wind operating, rest solar), with ~6.5 GW acquired wind O&M assets still not consolidated. Management guides ~50% O&M EBITDA margin.

segments.name: INOX Renewable Solutions (IRSL / RESCO, EPC)
segments.commentary: Demerger of power evacuation infrastructure business from INOX Green completed; record date August 1, 2026, listing expected in about 2-3 months pending regulatory approvals. Transformer expansion (4.9 MVA, then 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+), 4 cranes in operation, and USS launch planned in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 75% over FY26 maintained; management reiterated it as an annual, not quarterly, target.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 20% to 22% for full year FY27 maintained.
H2 heavy: 70% to 75% of annual business expected in H2; H1 about 25% of annual operations.
INR600 crores annual EBITDA guidance for INOX Green maintained, expected on annualised basis from Q3 FY27 once Wind World India (acquisition expected to complete in Q2 FY27) is consolidated.
Deferred revenue of about INR400 crores from Q4 FY26 to be recognised partly in Q1, fully within FY27.
Working capital guidance on annualised basis maintained; receivable days expected to fall over the next 3-4 quarters.
capex_capacity: 4X wind turbine: foundation complete, tower and main components ready; first prototype installation targeted August 2026, commercial launch about a month later.
Management said it is contemplating higher turbine models (5X/6X) if market demand exists.
ALMM and indigenisation: 80-90% of wind turbine components already indigenised; target near 100% indigenisation before end of calendar 2026 for 3X and 4X.
Transformer capacity expansion in IRSL (Jaipur): 4.9 MVA next, then 8-20 MVA and 100 MVA+ units; own crane fleet of 4 with more in FY27; USS and inverters/capacitor systems planned.
INOX Clean plans 3 GW+ annual IPP capacity; management expects ~25-30% of that to flow to Wind and the balance to Green (O&M) and RESCO (EPC).
demand_pricing: Order book ~4.4 GW as of July 2026, visibility of 24-36 months; 200 MW repeat LOA from NLC India in July via tender.
MOU for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean in June 2026; firm orders for 500 MW so far, balance 1 GW to be firmed later.
Indian wind additions of 1.4 GW in Q1 FY27; total installed wind 57.4 GW; management expects 8-10 GW annual additions over next few years.
Blended realisation for INOX Green's ~4 GW consolidated wind portfolio of INR9-10 lakh per MW (excl. GST); acquired portfolios expected to be substantially higher.
Wind World India: ~4.5 GW O&M portfolio, FY26 revenue ~INR580 crores, ~5% contracted annual price escalation; clients include Tata, ReNew, Greenko, Apraava, Hindustan Zinc.
Management said there is no preferential pricing for INOX Clean versus third-party customers.

qa_highlights.question: What was MW execution in Q1 and what is the FY27 estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give MW numbers; it now guides on revenue and margin rather than machine volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue growth of 30% and 20% EBITDA margin be confirmed for next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance; management reaffirmed 75% full-year growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin, with significant improvement expected in Q2 and H2 weighting.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue flat YoY and is the company no longer doing EPC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat revenue to the pivot to equipment supply causing disruption; it said Q1 is at par with prior-year Q1 and that EPC continues within IRSL with ~40% of third-party orders turnkey plus 1.5 GW INOX Clean MOU and NLC LOA.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables are high versus peers; how are EPC receivables accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are recognised under Ind AS 115 on risk-transfer basis and remain elevated until commissioning; management said receivable days fell in Q1 (figures not disclosed) and should drop substantially over the next 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR600 crore Green EBITDA guidance annual or quarterly?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual basis, expected from Q3-Q4 FY27 post consolidation of acquisitions; management would not guide on FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are INOX Clean terms arm's length versus other customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are arm's length, INOX Clean is treated as a customer, and there is no preferential pricing for it.

qa_highlights.question: Risks to meeting the 75% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO cited only force majeure events; said the equipment-supply pivot carries no seen risk to deliverables.

risks_watch: Full-year FY27 guidance (75% revenue growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin) is H2-weighted with 70-75% of business in H2; H1 tracking is roughly 5-10% short of the 25% share per management's own math, so Q2 delivery is the first test.
Recognition of the ~INR400 crore deferred revenue from Q4 FY26, partly in Q1 and the balance across FY27; management did not quantify how much was recognised in Q1.
Receivables remain elevated until commissioning under Ind AS 115; receivable days and working capital improvement over the next 3-4 quarters are unquantified.

Wind World India acquisition completion in Q2 FY27 and consolidation of the ~6.5 GW acquired O&M assets; INR600 crore INOX Green EBITDA is annualised from Q3 and excludes the acquisitions until consolidated.
Gap between INOX Green's ~50% O&M EBITDA margin guidance and reported margins; one-time and life-extension costs cited, with separate billing of value-added services expected from this year.

RESCO (IRSL) listing timing, expected in about 2-3 months pending regulatory approvals; 4X prototype installation in August 2026 and commercial launch about a month later; INOX Clean related-party order flow.
key_quotes: And we maintain that revenue guidance of 75% growth over the previous year and an EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% on a consol basis is what we maintain our guidance for the full year basis.
This is an annualized business. So on a quarterly basis, it will be pretty tough for us to say.
INR600 crores was an annual guidance, not the quarterly guidance. I can't achieve INR600 crores in a quarter.
So over the course of next 3, 4 quarters, you will see all these numbers falling out drastically and the balance sheet improving big time.

Flat YoY Wind revenue was acknowledged as disruption from the pivot rather than explained with figures.

539118|2026-03.headline: VRL Logistics Q4 FY26 total income rose 6% YoY to INR859 crore, with tonnage back to 3% YoY growth and EBITDA margin at 21.4%.
539118|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR859 crore, up about 6% YoY and 3% QoQ, helped by better realisation, new clients and return of previously lost accounts. Realisation per ton was about INR8,147, up roughly 3% YoY, and daily tonnage crossed 11,500 tons. EBITDA margin was about 21.4%, down about 190 bps YoY from an exceptional Q4 FY25 (23%+) but up about 48 bps QoQ. FY26 total income was about INR3,245 crore, profit INR237 crore (up about 29%), and EBITDA margin 20.8%. Management guided to FY27 tonnage growth of 6-7% and kept an EBITDA margin of around 20%+ despite fuel cost pressure, which it plans to pass on via selective rate hikes and fuel surcharges.

financial_highlights.change: down ~190 bps YoY; up ~48 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Return on capital employed / return on equity (FY26)

financial_highlights.change: INR101 crore vehicles; INR165 crore land and buildings

segments.name: Tonnage / volume
segments.commentary: Tonnage decline was 13% in Q1 FY26 and about 7% for full FY26; Q4 returned to about 3% YoY growth. April 2026 YoY volume growth was about 8% per management.

segments.name: Customer mix (Q4 YoY)
segments.commentary: New customers contributed about 17% of quantity, lost customers reduced volume by about 14%, and existing customers grew about 1%.

segments.name: Commodity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Textiles and cloth about 17-18%, agri (equipment, fertiliser, pesticides) about 10-11%, others (industrial, pharma, books, auto) about 5-6% each. Management says petrochemical-linked goods such as plastics are seeing lower demand.

segments.name: Booking mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: TO PAY and PAID spot bookings about 80%, ACCOUNT customers about 15-16%, FTL about 6-7%.

segments.name: Door-to-door
segments.commentary: Share rose to about 38-40% of commodities from about 33-34% earlier; realisation is about INR1-1.5 per kg higher for door delivery.

guidance_outlook: FY27 tonnage growth guided at 6-7% for the full year, with at least about 2% sequential growth each quarter.
New branches expected to add about 2-3% to FY27 tonnage; about 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings, fewer closures).
EBITDA margin to be maintained around 20%+ (near 21% in Q1 FY27 per management), with some basis-point impact from the withdrawal of bulk fuel purchase.
FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore: about INR100-150 crore for vehicles and INR200+ crore for land and buildings.
Depreciation not expected to rise materially because most new investment is in land (non-depreciable).
Fuel price pass-through via selective route rate hikes, chargeable-weight change (1 cubic feet from 8 kg to 9 kg on certain routes) and fuel surcharge in contracts.
capex_capacity: Fleet: about 6,000 owned vehicles per management; vehicle count fell from about 6,100+ to about 5,900 YoY, with about 500 additions planned in FY26 (100+ done, about 400 more by December 2026) and no scrappage planned.
Network: about 1,293 branches and 50 trans-shipment hubs across 24 states and 4 UTs as of March 2026; about 110 branches opened in FY26 with about 55-60 closed, net about 40-50.
Vehicle life: normal replacement at up to 15 years; earlier only for outdated or accident-damaged vehicles.
About 77% of fleet debt-free and 14% fully depreciated.
Hubs in pipeline: 2-3 locations including Nagpur and Raipur.
demand_pricing: Q4 volume growth came from new customers and return of lost accounts after contract restructuring; management says lost customers are returning due to service levels.

Fuel: diesel prices rose about INR3 recently; management said it has passed through on selected routes but not across the network, and that a 2x increase in rates within a week means pricing will be reviewed over 1-2 months.
Fuel procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as direct refinery purchase fell from 41% to 36% of volume (bulk purchase withdrawn).
Competition: most of the industry is unorganised; VRL says it is at a premium to unorganised operators but comparable to organised players and express cargo on corporate accounts.
Demand headwind: petrochemical and crude-linked goods such as plastics are seeing weaker demand, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume growth outlook and what efforts drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 6-7% full-year tonnage growth and about 2% sequential growth per quarter, driven by completed rate rationalisation, marketing, new branches and new customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel-driven price hikes hurt volumes, and how is fuel cost passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume pressure is from weak petrochemical-linked demand, not fuel prices. Hikes were applied on selected routes, with fuel surcharges in contracts; April 2026 YoY volume grew about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of lower bulk fuel purchase?
qa_highlights.answer: Some basis points of margin impact; management said it is flexible to hold EBITDA around 20% and the bulk purchase facility has already been lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did lorry hire charges rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Fleet fell from about 6,100 to 5,900 vehicles while tonnage grew, so outside hired vehicles were used to carry the extra volume, plus higher lorry hire rates.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new branch contribution and depreciation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches contributed about 1-1.5% of Q4 growth; FY27 branches expected to add 2-3%. Depreciation is not expected to rise much, as land is a large share of new investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business mix and competitive positioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is about 80% spot (TO PAY/PAID), 15-16% account, 6-7% FTL; door-to-door about 38-40%. Rates are at a premium to unorganised players and comparable to organised players.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility and geopolitical risk; the pass-through lag could compress margins in the near term, per management's own caveat.
Weak demand in petrochemical-linked commodities (plastics etc.) could offset recovery.
Reliance on hired vehicles (lorry hire cost rose) while owned fleet shrinks.
Achievement of 6-7% FY27 volume growth depends on net new branches (about 100) ramping up.
Management did not disclose kilometre-based metrics; lead distance is about 270-280 km and capacity 15-18 tons.
539118|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volume recovery and pricing pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins, with management stating some temporary disconnect is possible. Answers on fuel pricing and competition were direct, while the company declined to disclose the bus-business question (not in business) and kilometre data.
key_quotes: And ultimately, the cost, whatever additional costs will come, that needs to be pass it on to the customers.
So, on a full year basis, we are expecting around INR300 crores to INR350 crores capital expenditure.
But definitely, on a full quarter basis, we are planning to maintain similar EBITDA numbers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 100 net new branches planned in FY27 (100+ gross openings) adding 2-3% to tonnage, plus 2-3 hubs in pipeline including Nagpur and Raipur, while the owned fleet shrank from about 6,100 to 5,900 and about 400 more vehicles are due by December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: FY27 (at least 2% sequential growth each quarter)
rows.why: Management guides 6-7% FY27 tonnage growth, with April 2026 up about 8% YoY, Q4 at about 3%, and new customers contributing about 17% of quantity against about 14% lost volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex guided at INR300-350 crore (INR200+ crore for land and buildings) and utilisation read is not disclosed, so a land and branch capex plan is guided but not new.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Tonnage returned to about 3% YoY growth in Q4 and April 2026 grew about 8%, so the 6-7% FY27 guide could be exceeded if new customers and returning accounts keep coming, but petrochemical demand is weak.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged a near-term margin risk from fuel: diesel up about INR3, procurement cost per litre rose from INR84.52 to INR85.54 as refinery share fell from 41% to 36%, and pass-through is only on selected routes, with pricing reviewed over 1-2 months.

rows.label: Return of lost customer accounts
rows.why: Lost customers cut Q4 volume by about 14%, and management says they are returning on service levels, which supports the 6-7% FY27 tonnage guide.

rows.label: Fuel pass-through via rate hikes and surcharges
rows.why: Diesel rose about INR3; hikes applied on selected routes, pricing review over 1-2 months, and contracts carry a fuel surcharge, though the network-wide pass-through is not yet complete.

rows.label: Weak petrochemical-linked demand (plastics)
rows.why: Management says plastics and crude-linked goods are seeing lower demand, a headwind that could offset the recovery in volume.

tone.note: Management was confident on the volume recovery (April 2026 up about 8%) and fuel pass-through, but cautious on near-term margins given bulk fuel purchase withdrawal; analysts pushed on fuel pricing, competition and kilometre data, which management did not disclose.

539118|2026-06.headline: VRL Logistics Q1 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 81 crore (9% margin) on freight realisation up 9% to Rs 8,546/tonne and volumes up 9%.
539118|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 18% YoY to Rs 885 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to Rs 193 crore, with margin up 71 bps to 21.8%, despite a sharp fuel cost spike (procurement cost Rs 83 to Rs 94/litre). Management passed through the cost increase via rate hikes of roughly 5% in the quarter, and volumes grew about 9% YoY to 10.19 lakh tonnes. Net debt fell to Rs 391 crore from Rs 440 crore, and the board approved a Rs 280 crore buyback at Rs 320/share, subject to shareholder approval. Full-year guidance is raised to about 8% volume growth.

financial_highlights.change: up ~18% YoY from Rs 751 crore; up from Rs 859 crore QoQ
up ~22% YoY from Rs 158 crore (21.1%); margin up 36 bps QoQ from 21.4%
up from Rs 50 crore (6.7%) YoY; described as highest-ever quarterly profit
up 9% YoY from Rs 7,852; up ~5% QoQ from Rs 8,147
up ~9% YoY from 9.35 lakh MT; down ~1.7% QoQ
Rs 18 crore vehicles; Rs 49 crore land and buildings

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 volume growth now expected around 8% (earlier guidance 6-7%); July volumes grew about 10%, and Q2 about 9% is expected.
Freight rates expected to improve further from 8,546/tonne if fuel prices do not fall; if fuel falls, rates may be cut by about 2-3% (a Rs 4 fuel cut implies about 2% price impact).
EBITDA margin of about 20-21% considered maintainable for the next 3-4 years.
Volume growth of 7-8% a year expected over the next 3-4 years.
Free cash flow of Rs 120-130 crore per quarter; Rs 480-500 crore for the full year.
Capex of Rs 200-240 crore a year (vehicles Rs 120-140 crore; property balance); debt expected to stay at current levels after buyback.
capex_capacity: Fleet of about 6,000 owned vehicles; about 79% debt-free and 13% fully depreciated; old vehicles being scrapped.
Network of about 1,300 branches, up about 108 YoY and 16 added in Q1; about 40-50 branches are owned premises, with the rest leased (Ind AS 116 lease liability).
Existing truck capacity is fully utilised; growth beyond it needs new vehicles or outside hired vehicles (lorry hire rose).
Full-year property capex planned at Rs 150-160 crore for sorting centres (about 12-13 of 50 transshipment hubs already owned; 3-4 more identified).
Vehicle capex of about Rs 100 crore for the rest of FY27.
demand_pricing: Blended freight realisation up 9% YoY; management says about 5% was a price increase taken in Q1 (April-May fuel-driven rate hikes plus later increase after government fuel price revision), described as sustainable.
Volume growth of about 9% = about 6% from existing customers and about 3% net from new customers; about 16-17% of tonnage lost from low-margin customers, partly recovered.
About 85% of LTL business is on PAID and TO PAY terms; receivable days about 10-12.
Bulk fuel purchase stopped as bulk price was about Rs 15/litre above retail when crude spiked.
About 70% of the industry is unorganised; VRL estimates it is about 30% organised.
Agriculture is about 10-11% of volumes; lower monsoon may slightly weigh on coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken and will it sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 5% was taken in Q1 across fuel-driven hikes, and it is sustainable; if fuel falls, rates would be cut 2-3%. Freight realisation of Rs 8,546/tonne would hold absent fuel changes and may improve further, as mid-quarter hikes are not fully in the Q1 average.

qa_highlights.question: Is 9% volume growth the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year volume growth now expected at about 8%, up from 6-7% guidance, supported by branch expansion and recovery of lost customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and how does it fund the buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual FCF of Rs 480-500 crore funds capex of Rs 220-240 crore and the buyback; debt will stay at about the current level (about 0.3x debt-to-equity).

qa_highlights.question: Why buyback rather than debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Buyback replaces dividend, as about Rs 175 crore was paid as dividend last year; debt is already nominal at about 0.3x debt-equity.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of DFC and rail on the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Company is in talks with the Ministry of Railways on hub-to-hub rail use; collaboration is minimal today and management says it would not hurt the customer-facing business.

qa_highlights.question: Karnataka minimum wage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Rule not yet in force (challenged in court); impact expected to be small as salaries are already above minimum wage, with only statutory contribution changes.

risks_watch: Fuel price path (Gulf/crude volatility): fuel cost pass-through works both ways, with rate cuts of 2-3% if fuel falls.
Sustainability of ~9% volume growth after the recovery of lost low-margin customers; full-year guidance raised to 8%.
Buyback of Rs 280 crore at Rs 320/share is subject to shareholder approval; promoters are not participating.
Lower monsoon could weigh on agriculture (10-11% of volumes) in coming quarters.
Karnataka minimum wage rule is pending in court; statutory cost impact is possible.
Shift in lead distances from East/Northeast expansion: management says the NTKM impact is only 2-3%.

539141|2026-06.headline: UFO Moviez Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,118 mn (vs ₹1,090 mn YoY) and advertisement revenue grew 33% YoY, helped by Dhurandhar spillover.

Management credited a 33% YoY jump in advertisement revenue to the spillover from "Dhurandhar" and to annual advertisers onboarded around it. Product sales declined YoY, driven by roughly ₹7 crore lower international sales because Dubai imports were delayed by the regional war; management says these orders remain in hand. Releases fell to 399 titles in the quarter from 456 in Q1 FY26.

539150|2026-03.headline: PNC Infratech FY26 standalone revenue fell to INR 4,633 crore; management guides ~30% growth to INR 6,000 crore in FY27 with ~12% EBITDA margin.
539150|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was INR 1,458 crore with 12.02% EBITDA margin and PAT of INR 100 crore, while FY26 standalone revenue of INR 4,633 crore was below earlier expectations due to delayed appointed dates on four projects worth over INR 4,400 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR 6,000 crore (~30% growth), FY28 about 25% higher, and EBITDA near 12% in FY27, citing bitumen and crude-driven cost pressure partly offset by new escalation mechanisms. The company has an unexecuted order book above INR 22,000 crore, and it is diversifying into solar, BESS, coal mining and water. Net surplus on a standalone basis was INR 327 crore, while consolidated net debt to equity was 0.76 times.
