tone.note: Management was confident on the INR 22,000 crore order book and the ~30% FY27 revenue and ~12% EBITDA guidance, but cautious on margins from bitumen and crude costs and on appointed-date timing; analysts pressed on the FY26 revenue shortfall, the FY27 order target, and the rise in interest cost.

539150|2026-06.headline: PNC Infratech Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore and PAT to Rs 271 crore, while management kept FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 6,000 crore.
539150|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 34% YoY to Rs 1,518 crore, with EBITDA of Rs 375 crore (24.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 271 crore (17.8% margin). Consolidated revenue was Rs 1,688 crore (+19% YoY) and consolidated EBITDA Rs 524 crore (31% margin). Management kept FY27 and FY28 revenue guidance and new-business targets unchanged. The call was dominated by the Kanpur-Lucknow expressway issue, where NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the SPV and management declined to discuss the possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome.

financial_highlights.value: Net worth Rs 6,084 crore; bank debt Rs 428 crore (D/E 0.07x excl. ICD); cash and investments Rs 1,046 crore; net cash surplus Rs 133 crore
Net worth Rs 7,147 crore; total debt Rs 5,448 crore (D/E 0.76x); cash and bank Rs 2,870 crore
About Rs 20 crore in Q1, guided run-rate about Rs 20 crore/quarter
financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 30 crore in Q4

segments.name: Highways (EPC/HAM/BOT)
segments.commentary: Highway contracts are 64% of the Rs 19,100 crore unexecuted order book. Management says the road unexecuted order book is slightly above 60%. Fund-based portfolio is 17 projects: 1 BOT-Toll, 2 BOT-Annuity, 14 HAM.

segments.name: Water (Jal Jeevan Mission and irrigation)
segments.commentary: Opening water order book was Rs 2,310 crore; Rs 136 crore executed in Q1, leaving about Rs 2,180 crore. About Rs 741 crore (ex-GST) is due from government. Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 416 crore invoiced, Rs 263 crore received, Rs 153 crore receivable.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Mining EPC targeted at about Rs 500 crore revenue in FY27 and similar in FY28; Q1 execution was low due to land-access problems, and two new surface miners were deployed.

segments.name: Pune Ring Road
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about Rs 75 crore. Billing is milestone-linked to precasting and erection, so it is lumpy; management did not give FY27/FY28 revenue numbers.

segments.name: Solar (MP, NHPC PSA route)
segments.commentary: EPC component about Rs 2,000 crore on more than 300 acres leased in Madhya Pradesh. Work to start in Q4 FY27; more than Rs 1,000 crore revenue targeted in FY28, balance in FY29. Equity requirement about Rs 400 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 6,000 crore and FY28 of Rs 7,500 crore, with about 12% margin, maintained unchanged.
New business target of Rs 12,000-15,000 crore for FY27 maintained; management said about Rs 5,900 crore has been secured so far.
JJM revenue targeted at Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28; project to complete by December 2028.
Andhra Pradesh irrigation: Rs 150 crore targeted in FY27, balance about Rs 600 crore in FY28, subject to timely payment.
Effective tax rate guided at 25-27% for FY27. Capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for standalone FY27 and FY28 (Q1 spend about Rs 70 crore), plus about Rs 350 crore on the mining project.
Equity: Rs 436 crore remaining for existing HAMs over two years (about Rs 226 crore in FY27); about Rs 400 crore for the two new HAMs, mainly in FY28-29.
Pantnagar airport expected before end-September 2026; Bhopal bypass AD pushed to Q3 CY26 due to scope change.
capex_capacity: Standalone capex guided at about Rs 150 crore for FY27 and about Rs 150 crore for FY28; Rs 70 crore spent on machinery in Q1.
Coal mining project total capex about Rs 350 crore (management corrected from Rs 150 crore), front-loaded in the initial years.

Two new HAM SPVs (Barabanki-Mustafabad and Mustafabad-Biswariya) signed concession agreements with NHAI on 16 July 2026; 150 days allowed for financial closure, and appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land.
HAM portfolio: 6 projects at COD/PCOD, 5 under construction, 1 (MPRDC) with financial closure documents submitted, 2 new projects in financial closure.
Rs 1,187 crore of HAM equity infused to June 2026 out of Rs 1,623 crore requirement (excluding the two new HAMs).
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs 19,100 crore (mgmt said Rs 19,600 crore earlier in call, then Rs 19,100 crore per prepared remarks). It is 64% highways, about 21% water/canal/railway/airport, about 15% coal mining.

Bids submitted: 24 projects worth about Rs 32,000 crore (16 EPC, 8 HAM), including 10 HAM, 8 railway, 2 coalfield. A further about 78 projects (about Rs 1.7 lakh crore) are to be bid in the next 2-3 months.
NHAI's Q1 FY27 awards were 107 km and execution about 640 km; NHAI plans to bid out 54 projects worth about Rs 1.8 lakh crore over 2-3 months.
Management targets a non-road share of about 40-45% over time, versus about 60% road order book today.
Management did not comment on pricing or competition.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for Kanpur-Lucknow issue (non-performer or bidding ban), possible duration, UP-level bidding impact, repair cost and standalone vs subsidiary impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment beyond exchange filings. NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the concessionaire SPV; reply is being submitted and the decision rests with NHAI, so no timeline or ban duration was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 and FY28 guidance changing, given about Rs 5,900 crore of new business secured versus Rs 12,000-15,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: No change. FY27 revenue Rs 6,000 crore, FY28 Rs 7,500 crore, about 12% margin and FY27 new business target Rs 12,000-15,000 crore all maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Barabanki-Mustafabad appointed date and equity quantum for the two new HAMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Concession agreements signed 16 July 2026 with 150 days for financial closure. Appointed date follows NHAI handing over 90% of land. Equity expected around Rs 400 crore, not Rs 490 crore as the analyst suggested.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital details: inventory, debtors, payables, mobilisation advance, retention, unbilled and HAM/water debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory Rs 847 crore, debtors Rs 1,900 crore, trade payables Rs 680 crore, mobilisation advance Rs 178 crore, retention Rs 295 crore, unbilled Rs 462 crore, HAM debtors Rs 479 crore, water debtors Rs 925 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise in Q1 and what is the ICD and interest outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose due to a term loan for machinery financing, repayable over 4-5 years. ICD is Rs 485 crore. Quarterly interest run-rate about Rs 20 crore, and debt is expected to decline.

qa_highlights.question: Water (JJM and AP irrigation) revenue targets and receivables?
qa_highlights.answer: JJM revenue Rs 700-800 crore in FY27 and about Rs 1,000 crore in FY28, project completion by December 2028. Rs 741 crore excluding GST is due from government. AP irrigation Rs 150 crore in FY27 and about Rs 600 crore in FY28, with Rs 153 crore receivable and Rs 94 crore release expected within 7-10 days.

qa_highlights.question: Coal mining and solar revenue and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal mining revenue about Rs 500 crore each in FY27 and FY28; total mining capex about Rs 350 crore, front-loaded. Solar EPC about Rs 2,000 crore with equity about Rs 400 crore; solar revenue minimal in FY27, more than Rs 1,000 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Order book reconciliation versus last quarter's Rs 22,000 crore figure?
qa_highlights.answer: The earlier Rs 22,000 crore included the two new HAMs; the current unexecuted order book is about Rs 19,100 crore, including the two HAMs, Pantnagar airport, Ganga bridge and LDA flyover.

risks_watch: Kanpur-Lucknow expressway: NHAI show cause notice to SPV, possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome, toll loss and repair cost still unquantified; management gave no timeline.
Receivables: JJM Rs 741 crore excluding GST pending from government and AP irrigation receivable; working capital at 110 days depends on these collections.
NHAI award slowdown (107 km awarded in Q1) and unclear timing of the Rs 1.8 lakh crore bid pipeline; Rs 32,000 crore bids under evaluation with financial bids not yet opened.
Execution timing risks: Pune Ring Road billing is lumpy and FY27/FY28 revenue not given; coal mining Q1 execution hit by land-access issues; solar work only from Q4 FY27 pending PSA/PPA.
Two new HAMs need financial closure within 150 days and appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land; Pantnagar airport target end-September 2026 and Bhopal bypass moved to Q3 CY26.

Balance sheet: debt rose to about Rs 900 crore including Rs 485 crore ICD despite Rs 1,100 crore cash, with a new machinery term loan; management did not fully explain the rationale beyond liquidity strategy.
Order book reconciliation was confusing (Rs 22,000 crore vs Rs 19,600 crore vs Rs 19,100 crore), and some figures were corrected during the call (mining capex, equity for new HAMs).
key_quotes: So, we are maintaining the same guidance.
we don't want to share anything beyond what we informed to the exchanges.
Testing is going on, so this month everything will be clear.
So, we expect this funds will be realized in the coming months, because the state government is actively pursuing release of 50% subsidy from the Government of India.
539150|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on guidance, order pipeline and margins, but guarded and evasive on the Kanpur-Lucknow NHAI matter, refusing to discuss non-performer, bidding-ban or toll-loss outcomes. Several figures were given loosely or corrected mid-call, and some answers were deferred to after the call.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin was 24.7% in Q1 (up from Rs 141 crore to Rs 375 crore YoY) and management guides about 12% margin for FY27-28 with interest cost falling from about Rs 30 crore in Q4 to about Rs 20 crore a quarter; the 12% guide sits well below the Q1 run-rate, so margin guidance looks conservative, though the brief gives no explicit margin-expansion call and the quarterly margin is likely

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Solar EPC of about Rs 2,000 crore starts Q4 FY27 with more than Rs 1,000 crore revenue targeted in FY28, two new HAM SPVs signed 16 July 2026 with 150 days for financial closure, and coal mining EPC targeted at about Rs 500 crore revenue in FY27, though the appointed date depends on NHAI handing over 90% of land.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management holds FY27 revenue at about Rs 6,000 crore (Q1 standalone Rs 1,518 crore, up 34% YoY) and FY28 at Rs 7,500 crore, but the Rs 5,900 crore secured against a Rs 12,000-15,000 crore new business target and NHAI awards of only 107 km in Q1 leave the back-half ramp unproven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Standalone capex is guided at about Rs 150 crore a year with only Rs 70 crore spent in Q1 and no utilisation figure disclosed, so a new capex announcement depends on the bid pipeline (about Rs 1.7 lakh crore to be bid in 2-3 months) converting into awards.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 6,000 crore was held unchanged and new business secured is only about Rs 5,900 crore against a Rs 12,000-15,000 crore target, with NHAI awards subdued at 107 km in Q1, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The Kanpur-Lucknow expressway SPV faces an NHAI show cause notice with possible non-performer or bidding-ban outcome (toll loss and repair cost unquantified), receivables of Rs 741 crore excluding GST from JJM are pending, and coal mining Q1 execution was hit by land-access issues.

rows.label: Kanpur-Lucknow NHAI show cause notice and possible bidding ban
rows.why: NHAI has issued a show cause notice to the SPV, management gave no timeline and the non-performer or bidding-ban outcome is unquantified, so a ban could cut the Rs 32,000 crore of bids under evaluation and the Rs 1.7 lakh crore pipeline.

rows.label: Receivables collection from government (JJM and AP irrigation)
rows.why: Rs 741 crore ex-GST is due from government for JJM and Rs 153 crore is receivable in AP irrigation, with Rs 94 crore release expected within 7-10 days, while NWC stands at 110 days.

rows.label: Non-road mix shift to 40-45% from about 60% road order book
rows.why: Water is about 21% and coal mining about 15% of the Rs 19,100 crore order book, and management targets non-road share of 40-45% over time, though no timeline was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on guidance, the order pipeline and margins but evasive on the Kanpur-Lucknow NHAI matter, and analysts pushed on the new business gap (Rs 5,900 crore secured vs Rs 12,000-15,000 crore target), the order book reconciliation and the debt rise.

539150|2026-09.headline: PNC Infratech Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% to ₹1,146 crore; FY27 guidance of ₹6,000 crore revenue and 12% margin reiterated.
539150|2026-09.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,146 crore (up 17% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹138 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹73 crore. H1 FY27 standalone revenue was ₹2,664 crore (up 26%), including a ₹217 crore arbitration award booked on realisation. Management kept FY27 revenue (₹6,000 crore), 12% EBITDA margin and ₹12,000–15,000 crore order inflow guidance unchanged, while the NHPC BESS project was exited after the LOA lapsed. The High Court stay on NHAI debarment (granted October 12, 2026) allows bidding to resume, with the next hearing on November 26, 2026.

financial_highlights.value: 0.21x (0.10x net of cash and current investments of ₹1,252 crore)
Over ₹18,000 crore (incl. two new NHAI HAM projects)

segments.name: Highways (core)
segments.commentary: Highways are 63% of the ₹18,000 crore unexecuted order book; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above ₹17,200 crore, of which 6 are at PCOD/COD and 5 under construction.

segments.name: Water, canal, railway and airport
segments.commentary: These contracts are about 21% of the order book. Water receivables fell after ₹267 crore was released in the quarter; the Pantnagar airport EPC (₹302 crore, 24 months) was awarded in July 2026.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Coal mining is 16% of the order book. FY27 coal revenue guidance was cut to ₹350–400 crore from ₹500 crore, with about ₹160 crore executed through September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹6,000 crore unchanged, including the ₹217 crore arbitration award; H2 implied revenue of about ₹3,336 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 12% maintained on ₹5,800 crore excluding the arbitration award; management said bitumen cost pressure is already factored in.
FY27 order inflow guidance of ₹12,000–15,000 crore maintained; ₹4,260 crore secured so far, with ₹8,000–11,000 crore targeted before March 31, 2027.
FY28 revenue guidance of ₹7,500 crore (about 25% growth) and 12% margin retained; management cites ₹15,000 crore opening FY28 order book.
Water revenue FY27 revised to about ₹650 crore (from ₹750 crore); FY28 water about ₹1,000 crore. Coal FY28 about ₹500 crore.
Capex guidance: about ₹200 crore for FY27 (₹155 crore spent in H1) and about ₹150 crore for FY28. Equity for HAM projects: ₹913 crore outstanding, ₹460 crore targeted in FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of ₹155 crore spent in H1 FY27; about ₹200 crore expected for FY27, implying roughly ₹50 crore in H2.
Equity infused in HAM projects: ₹1,212 crore to date against ₹2,125 crore requirement; ₹913 crore balance over two to three years, funded by internal accruals.

NHAI HAM projects (two, concession signed July 16, 2026): financial closure within 150 days; appointed date expected in Q4 FY27; 730-day build period with 35–40% progress in FY28 and about 60% in FY29.
MPRDC Bhopal bypass HAM: appointed date expected before December 31, 2026, with some progress in FY27.

Canal project paused until mid-November due to water release; about ₹60–70 crore work in FY27 and about ₹400 crore in FY28; ₹495 crore executed to date, about ₹790 crore left; extension to December 31, 2028.
NHPC BESS project exited: PPA/PSA not signed in time, LOA cancelled, bid security refunded; excluded from order book.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 vs 107 km in Q1; 19 of 54 identified projects approved and 17 appraised for the remainder of FY27.
17 bids submitted worth ₹16,600 crore (13 EPC, 3 HAM, 1 TBCB); price bids not yet opened. Pipeline of about 80 projects worth ₹180,000 crore to be bid through January 2027.
Management says competition is intense in small EPC jobs but less so in large, fund-based HAM and TBCB projects.
Input costs rose from West Asia conflict (diesel, bitumen); MoRTH/NHAI/AAI extended monthly price-adjustment escalation through December 31, 2026, with limited mitigation.
Management reports ₹267 crore water receipts and ₹183 crore Andhra Pradesh irrigation receipts in the quarter; irrigation revenue of about ₹500 crore booked.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹244 crore arbitration award included in Q2 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is recognised only on realisation; ₹217 crore of the arbitration was recognised in H1 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the arbitration award be included in the ₹6,000 crore guidance and the 12% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the ₹6,000 crore includes it. The 12% margin applies to the ₹5,800 crore remaining revenue excluding the award.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone debt has doubled while cash is high; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is equipment finance (about ₹400 crore+, five-year terms) and short-term working capital; ₹494 crore is inter-corporate deposits from operational SPVs. Management denied the position is arbitrage-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares at current prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is thinking along those lines (buyback), without giving details.

qa_highlights.question: Are the NHAI HAM appointed dates on track?
qa_highlights.answer: MPRDC appointed date expected before December 31; NHAI HAM projects expected in Q4 FY27, with 90% ROW achieved on the NHAI projects and financial closure within 150 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹8,000–11,000 crore H2 order inflow come if the NHAI ban persists after November?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes the relief continues and expects over 50–60% of new orders from NHAI, MoRTH and NHIDCL, with 30–40% from non-NHAI.

risks_watch: Stay on NHAI debarment order: next hearing November 26, 2026; bidding eligibility depends on outcome.
Standalone debt rising while cash is held; management attributes this to working capital and equipment finance, with inter-corporate deposits from SPVs.
Input cost inflation (bitumen, diesel, batteries, logistics) with only partial escalation coverage through December 31, 2026.
Order inflow of ₹8,000–11,000 crore needed in H2 to meet the ₹12,000–15,000 crore guidance, with no visibility beyond the 17 bids pending price opening.
Overseas expansion (Kazakhstan subsidiary, Georgia bid) and the lack of a clear growth driver after BESS exit; management flagged aggressive bidding in roads.
Coal mining execution affected by local resistance on land vacation, though October execution improved; water receivables pending.
539150|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on guidance and order pipeline, but defensive when challenged on the BESS exit, the rising standalone debt and the NHAI order inflow dependence. Management reiterated all FY27/FY28 targets without changes despite several analyst questions on feasibility.
key_quotes: We don't see any major challenge achieving the 30% growth what we've given the guidance.
So, highways will continue to be our focus sector to expand our business.
We are giving the guidance of 12% EBITDA on the INR5,800 crores, excluding the arbitration claim.
Yeah. We are thinking in the same line to buy back.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin is guided at 12% on Rs 5,800 cr, versus H1 standalone margin of 19.2% inflated by the arbitration award, and management says bitumen cost pressure is already factored in with escalation only through Dec 31, 2026.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two NHAI HAM projects (concession signed July 16, 2026) expected to reach appointed date in Q4 FY27 and MPRDC Bhopal HAM before Dec 31, 2026, but capacity is not quantified and HAM projects add equity rather than plant capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY28 revenue guided at Rs 7,500 cr (about 25% over FY27) backed by a Rs 15,000 cr opening order book and NHAI awards of about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 versus 107 km in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is guided modestly at about Rs 200 cr for FY27 (Rs 155 cr spent in H1) and Rs 150 cr for FY28, with HAM equity of Rs 460 cr targeted in FY28; management is also thinking about a buyback, but no utilisation figure is disclosed to justify a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue at Rs 6,000 cr (H1 Rs 2,664 cr), and the Rs 217 cr arbitration award is already included, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coal FY27 revenue was already cut to Rs 350-400 cr from Rs 500 cr and water to about Rs 650 cr from Rs 750 cr, and H2 needs about Rs 3,336 cr revenue plus Rs 8,000-11,000 cr order inflow amid NHAI debarment risk with a hearing on Nov 26, 2026.

rows.label: H2 order inflow of Rs 8,000-11,000 cr
rows.why: Rs 4,260 cr secured so far against a Rs 12,000-15,000 cr FY27 target, with 17 bids worth Rs 16,600 cr pending price opening and dependence on NHAI debarment being lifted after the Nov 26, 2026 hearing.

rows.label: Share buyback under consideration
rows.why: Management said it is thinking along buyback lines without details, while standalone net cash is Rs 1,252 cr against standalone debt that has doubled.

rows.label: Standalone debt rising despite cash
rows.why: Standalone net debt/equity is 0.21x gross and 0.10x net of Rs 1,252 cr cash, but debt has doubled on equipment finance and Rs 494 cr inter-corporate deposits, so a reduction is not guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27/FY28 revenue guidance, order pipeline and 12% margin but defensive on the BESS exit, the rising standalone debt and dependence on NHAI order inflow; analysts pushed on feasibility of the Rs 8,000-11,000 cr H2 inflow and the arbitration-driven margin.

539199|2026-03.headline: SG Finserve FY26 PAT rose 58% to INR 128 crore on a INR 3,936 crore loan book (up 75%), with management guiding AUM growth of 25-30% medium term and 35-40% for FY27.
539199|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating income of INR 334 crore (up 96% YoY), closing loan book of INR 3,936 crore (up 75%, stated as an all-time high) and PAT of INR 128 crore (up 58%). Q4 PAT was INR 42 crore, up 30% QoQ, and Q4 fee income was about INR 6.2 crore against about INR 1.5-1.9 crore in earlier periods. Management reiterated nil NPA as its guidance and said it is comfortable with leverage of about 1.9x, aiming for 3x over two to three years without fresh equity. Q&A covered NPA philosophy, TReDS entry, related-party exposure and the sharp rise in fee income, and several answers were framed as conservative guidance.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / anchor financing)
segments.commentary: More than three-fourths of the business per management. Construction is the largest sector at about 35% of AUM, followed by automotive; average ticket about INR 5 crore per borrower.

segments.name: Factoring
segments.commentary: Bilateral factoring commercialised in March 2026 with INR 175 crore outstanding at 31 March. TReDS participation expected to go live in Q1 FY27 through RXIL and M1xchange.

segments.name: Cross-sell (LAP, working capital, business loans)
segments.commentary: Opportunistic cross-sell within the anchor/dealer ecosystem at near-zero acquisition cost; management said it is not a core focus. Mobile is about 2% of AUM.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance of 25-30% CAGR medium to long term; FY27 aspiration of 35-40% AUM growth.
Profit guidance of 30-35% CAGR, measured on full-year PAT of the previous financial year, not Q4 exit run rate.
Profitability range: ROA 4.5-5%, ROE 14-16%, cost to income 13-17%.
Leverage to rise from about 2x to 3x over two to three years, in phases; comfortable range 2x-3x.
Internal AUM target of INR 10,000 crore in three to four years without fresh equity, with bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore.
NPA guidance remains nil; management said the aim is no losses, while acknowledging that lending involves losses.
capex_capacity: Operates from 30 hub locations pan-India, each covering about a 100 km radius; business is 100% domestic with no import-export financing.
Bank lines of more than INR 3,000 crore, with INR 3,000-3,500 crore estimated, not fully utilised.
Gross disbursements for FY26 crossed INR 25,000 crore; Q4 disbursements about INR 7,700 crore against a book of about INR 3,900 crore (average churn about 45 days).
New businesses (unspecified) are under groundwork, subject to regulatory approvals; timing of FY27 or FY28 uncertain.
demand_pricing: Management said fewer than 100 of the top 500 corporates are active in supply chain finance, and only 25-30% of anchors' sales are covered by organised programmes, so headroom is large.

Management estimated the wider supply chain market, including PSU banks, at upward of INR 1 lakh crore; five to six private banks and a few NBFCs each run AUM of INR 10,000-15,000 crore in dealer finance.
Fee income is being pursued as a strategy; fees on disbursements range from 10 paise to 50 paise, with some cases at 1%.
Management said no stress is visible in top sectors but is monitoring geopolitical and fuel/gas supply risks; steel import effects are yet to be assessed.

qa_highlights.question: How does the business model support nil NPAs, and is there a buffer in NPA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exposure is short-term (about 45-day churn), invoice-backed and end-use monitored, with anchors paid directly and early-warning tracking of dealer cycles. It said Ind AS ECL and RBI rules limit conservative provisioning, with about INR 18 crore provision already held; the guidance is nil NPA by design.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leverage target and how will growth be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Leverage is about 1.9x; management sees 3x as acceptable and aims to reach it in two to three years in phases. Bank lines of INR 3,000-3,500 crore are available, so growth to INR 10,000 crore AUM is possible in three to four years without fresh equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income jump in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee income is now a strategic focus and that Q3 fees were under-captured; it expects Q4-level fees (about INR 6 crore) to become the norm.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% growth guidance conservative, and is FY27 guidance different?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is deliberately conservative and aims for 35-40% AUM growth in FY27, with 25-30% as the medium-term average. Earlier conservatism was attributed to a management change.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the loan book goes to group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: Related-party exposure is less than INR 100 crore; channel financing to group companies is around 30% of the overall book.

qa_highlights.question: Did steel prices drive the AUM increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the steel price rise did not drive the 31 March AUM; growth came from volume and FY26 average AUM doubled to INR 2,640 crore.

risks_watch: Fee income reliance: Q4 fee income of about INR 6.2 crore is far above prior quarters; sustainability is unproven.
Geopolitical and fuel/gas supply disruption could stress steel, auto and construction borrowers (top sectors), though no stress was reported.
Earlier guidance inconsistency across quarters, which an investor raised; conservative framing may need to be tracked against actuals.
Leverage increase from 1.9x to 3x and the timing of TReDS go-live in Q1 FY27 and of new business approvals.
Concentration in the construction sector (about 35% of AUM).
539199|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and asset quality, with repeated emphasis on conservatism in guidance; more hedged on new businesses, timing of TReDS, and geopolitical impact, which management said is still evolving.
key_quotes: Our closing Loan Book of INR 3,936 crores is at all-time high, which is backed by our core business - supply chain finance
But under-committing, over-delivering is something which suits us best.
By design, by target, we are not going to lose money. So that's why our guidance is NIL NPA.
We don't plan to have TReDS platform. We will only participate on existing TReDS regulated entities licensed by RBI.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.5 crore in Q3 and INR 1.89 crore in Q4 FY25 as cited by analyst

539199|2026-06.headline: SG Finserve posts record Q1 FY27 PBT of INR72 crore (+27% QoQ) and loan book of INR4,552 crore (+82% YoY) with nil NPAs.
539199|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly PBT of INR72 crore, up 27% QoQ, with the loan book rising 16% QoQ to INR4,552 crore. Net worth reached INR1,539 crore, leverage moved to 2.2x from 1.9x at March 2026, and CRAR stood at 32%. Annualised ROA was 5.1% and ROE 14%, with nil NPAs reported. Management reiterated FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY), with AUM guidance of INR5,500 crore for FY27 and a 25-30% AUM CAGR over three to four years.

segments.name: Supply chain finance and working capital
segments.commentary: Management said about two-thirds of business financing sits in working capital, supply chain and factoring; about one-third of AUM is from the APL Apollo ecosystem, down from a higher share, and 52 anchor mandates are running (5 added in Q1).

segments.name: Factoring (TReDS and bilateral)
segments.commentary: Factoring outstanding was INR225 crore in June versus INR175 crore in March; commercialised in March-April 2026, with yields at par with channel finance for TReDS and at or slightly above for bilateral deals.

segments.name: Beyond supply chain (cross-sell LAP, opportunistic)
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of business financing; management named digital lending and loan against property as products under consideration, with no retail or consumer lending.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT visibility of about INR300 crore (about 75% YoY); PAT about INR225 crore; FY27 closing equity about INR1,700 crore; FY27 AUM about INR5,500 crore (management called INR6,000 crore aspirational).
Targeted AUM CAGR of 25-30% over three to four years, with profitability CAGR of 30-35%; INR10,000 crore AUM now targeted for FY30 (earlier guidance was INR7,500 crore for FY30) and possibly FY29.
Quarter-on-quarter growth normalised to about 8-10% for PAT, with AUM growth of about 15-16% QoQ, after adjusting for INR337 crore equity received at end-March and early April.
Cost-to-income to be kept below 15%; opex maintained at about 1% of average book.
Leverage to move from 2x towards 3x over about two years, taking ROE from 14% towards 16% with ROA held at around 4.5-5%. No equity raise planned through the growth phase up to INR10,000 crore AUM.
Insurance broking subsidiary (SG Insurance Brokers) incorporated; IRDAI licence pending, commercialisation at least two to three quarters away, and not expected before Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: No capex or physical capacity discussed; the business is asset-light, with about 30 locations for sales coverage.
ESOP pool of 20 lakh approved by shareholders; about 10.32 lakh granted in April and about 50,000 granted in July to new joiners, leaving about 9 lakh unallocated with no timing decided.
GIFT City entity approval received from the board, subject to dual RBI and IFSCA approvals; long-term plan.
Board has approved AIF and ARC business; no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Average portfolio yield held at about 12.5% in Q3, Q4 and Q1, with factoring added without diluting or enhancing the overall yield.
Management said geopolitical uncertainty is hitting the MSME and trader business through lower incremental working capital needs, but has not yet translated into credit pressure.

Management said it does not compete with large banks and NBFCs, and fills the gap left when a dealer's bank working capital limit falls short of its requirement; for example, INR2 crore gap on a INR10 crore need.
Management estimated the addressable market as receivables of about INR25 lakh crore on the balance sheets of the top 1,000 corporates.
Management said the MoU-based anchor pipeline (52 anchors, INR7,700 crore MoU value) is a dummy limit and should not be read as book visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will equity be raised this year, given net worth near INR1,510 crore and projected FY27 book growth?

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 AUM guidance only 25-30% CAGR when growth is far higher currently?

qa_highlights.question: Is NPA-free status sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nil NPA is the stated aim, but acknowledged that losses can occur in lending; a larger net worth and profitability would be the buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q1 run rate persist, given that H2 is usually stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR4,000 crore average book sustains the base, with incremental growth on top; QoQ PAT growth of 8-10% is targeted after normalising the equity infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost-to-income only 7% against a 14% guide?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified the right metric is opex at about 1% of average book, and the company guides to cost-to-income below 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is SG Insurance Brokers and when will it start?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a wholly owned subsidiary for B2B fee-based cross-sell to the existing anchor and borrower ecosystem, not underwriting; subject to IRDAI approval and at least two to three quarters away.

539199|2026-09.headline: SG Finserve posted an all-time high quarterly PAT of INR59 crore in Q2 FY27, with loan book at ~INR5,700 crore and H1 PBT of INR150 crore.
539199|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR59 crore and a loan book of about INR5,700 crore, up roughly 25% QoQ on period-end basis (average AUM up 17% QoQ). Asset-to-equity rose from 2.8x to 3.7x over the last year, and quarterly ROE reached about 15%. Management revised its mid-term debt-to-equity ceiling from 3x to 4x, which it said would take AUM to about INR11,000 crore, and it expects no equity raise this year. New initiatives during the quarter included factoring/TReDS, digital lending, loan against property (LAP), and a stake in an AI/digital subsidiary, plus a GIFT City subsidiary and an AIF pending SEBI approval.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / deep-tier)
segments.commentary: Supply chain is ~70% of AUM. Group ecosystem share of book has fallen to 25%; the company powers ~60 brands. Steel and building products ~35% of AUM and auto ~20%.

segments.name: Factoring / TReDS
segments.commentary: Factoring licence received in March 2026; now ~15% of book after starting in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Digital lending (BharatPe merchant LSP model)
segments.commentary: ~10,000 loans disbursed; book only INR121 crore at 30 Sep 2026. Management expects ~10% of AUM in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP) / business loans
segments.commentary: Just started in Delhi NCR with four disbursals and INR17 crore outstanding; tickets above INR25 lakh.

segments.name: Project finance
segments.commentary: 12 accounts disbursed recently, none commercially operational; management expects starts in 6-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Debt-to-equity mid-term ceiling revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing in the call's board meeting.
AUM growth guidance of 30-35% CAGR on a one-year-forward basis; profitability CAGR guidance of 35-40%.
Management targets INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years, implying ~100% growth from current book; equity dilution or higher leverage mandate expected only after that.
Full-year PAT guidance of INR225 crore reiterated; management said it may do slightly better.
Expects around 7,000 crore AUM by year end on current run rate (per management comment); Q2/Q4 seasonality of 2-3% on the higher side.
Target of adding 2 anchor corporates per month for the next 12-18 months.
GIFT City finance subsidiary (~INR48 crore investment approved) expected operational in about a year, subject to RBI and IFSCA approvals.
Planning to keep ROA above 4.5% and cost-to-income below 15%; yield maintained at ~13% on AUM.
capex_capacity: Headcount ~100 (roughly doubled in one year); per-employee annualised PAT above INR2 crore; presence in 34 locations.
Digital lending built on LSP framework; in-house AI/digital stack being built via a 15% stake in a subsidiary rather than external SaaS.
New subsidiaries: AIF (Cat III equity AIF, SEBI approval awaited), AMC subsidiary, GIFT City finance company (~INR48 crore), shared services company (cost amount undecided), AI/technology subsidiary.
Project finance: 12 accounts, none yet operational.
LAP: specialist team hired; scaling to be gradual, starting in Delhi NCR.
demand_pricing: Wallet share across the ~60 anchor brands is under 5%; management targets doubling to 10%, plus 20-25 new brands in the next year.
~800 active customers, average ticket ~INR7 crore; per-borrower appetite limited.
Yield on AUM maintained at ~13% (ROI ~12.5% plus 50-70 bps fee income); range 11-15% by risk category.
Lending rates are benchmarked to the SGFL benchmark rate; management said any repo-linked cost increase would be passed on, though benchmark not yet raised.
Management positions the company as filling the INR10-20 'untied' portion of borrowers' funding need after banks/NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity this financial year, given borrowings near 3x net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Debt-to-equity mandate raised to 4x, with incremental borrowing approved by the board; equity dilution or higher leverage considered 2-3 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow ~18% QoQ while AUM grew 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Income accrues on daily outstanding; average AUM grew 17% QoQ, so period-end growth overstates income growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost as a percentage of income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x); management said this lifts ROE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the collection efficiency and DPD profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly collection efficiency 99.5%; 60+ DPD is zero overall and 30+ DPD is zero in non-supply-chain book; 0.5% slips to 1+ DPD and is mostly collected within 30 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: How does the RBI draft on revolving credit affect the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the product is term-based with no rollover or extension, so it is aligned; only documentation and reporting systems need tweaks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds and funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Single source is banks and NBFCs (19 lenders), plus opportunistic commercial paper; cost of borrowing about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 credit cost increase a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is an ECL/IRAC regulatory requirement, not cash credit cost; ~INR25 crore accumulated on ~INR5,700 crore book, and nil NPA is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why would borrowers choose SG over banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowers often get INR80-90 of a INR100 requirement from banks; SG funds the remaining untied portion, under a coexistence model across PSU banks, private banks, large NBFCs and mid-layer NBFCs.

risks_watch: Leverage rising toward the 4x D/E ceiling; equity dilution likely around INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM given the ~3x price-to-book; watch the CCD/OCD option.
Finance cost ratio rising (44.5% of interest income); repo hike and benchmark pass-through timing unclear.
Draft RBI norms on revolving credit could require documentation and system changes for supply-chain products (about two-thirds of AUM).
BharatPe digital-lending book: management acknowledged gross NPAs are possible, relying on FLDG and LSP cushions.
New businesses (AIF, GIFT City, LAP, project finance) carry execution and gestation risk; project finance accounts not yet operational.
Management said the Q2 front-loading of growth may normalise; the 30-35% growth guide must be tested in H2.
Opex discipline as headcount and locations expand; the cost-to-income target is below 15%.
539199|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and leverage, with repeated emphasis on conservatism. Management was evasive on digital-lending ROA ('will not be able to divulge the commercials') and on the cost and timing of the shared-services company and the AIF, and it was cautious on the RBI draft, calling it a documentation tweak.
key_quotes: Our mid-term target was to not leverage ourselves beyond debt-to-equity of 3x. But now considering the growth which has front-loaded, we are revising our leverage to debt-to-equity of 4x.
Our collection efficiency, Mayank, is 99.5% on a month-on-month basis.
The objective is to not increase the cost; our objective is to bring synergy and reduce the cost or worst, maintain the cost.
So the problem is not the TAM; the problem is, what we want to do and what we don't want to do, because as I said, we are a very conservative lender.

539221|2026-03.headline: Sportking expects top line up 7-10% and margins to expand 15-20% QoQ over next three quarters on higher yarn prices and a long sales book.
539221|2026-03.overview: Management described a resilient Q4 FY26 with revenue broadly stable and profitability improved, driven by better yarn realisation and stronger cotton yarn demand. Demand was attributed to China's resurgence as a cotton yarn importer, Bangladesh recovery, and a stronger rupee-driven competitiveness shift for Indian spinning. Management said spreads are at roughly three-year highs and expects margins to expand over the next two to three quarters, with the 150,000-spindle greenfield project slated for commercial operations in Q3 FY27. Acquisitions of a majority stake in Marvel Dyers and Processors and the Sobhagia Sales manufacturing facilities were approved, with closure targeted within the calendar year.

financial_highlights.value: Broadly stable (no figure stated on call)

financial_highlights.change: Expected to reverse in Q1 if rupee does not depreciate further
Management estimate for current/coming financial year

qa_highlights.question: How will new capacity ramp, and why are spreads rising and sustainable for 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads supported by a 90-day export book already largely sold for the current quarter and cotton covered for 3-6 months. New greenfield capacity is on timeline, with 97-98% utilisation about 6 months after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Is China a durable demand source given historical volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged volatility but said Chinese domestic demand has turned after 4-5 years of weakness and that China now needs to import cotton given peaking domestic production and high cotton duties.

qa_highlights.question: What happens to margins once new-crop cotton prices fall or rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current spreads are among the best of the last 3 years even at today's cotton prices; April-September is seasonally weak and October-March is seasonally stronger. No crystal ball on pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for H1 FY27 and quarter-on-quarter trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects QoQ margin expansion of at least 15-20% over the next 2-3 quarters, citing higher yarn prices (USD3.30 vs USD2.70-2.80) and the long sales book. It declined to give formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the acquisitions and synergies on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired entities are about 7-8% of turnover (about INR200 crores). Immediate margin impact is small; they serve as labs for downstream expansion. Closure expected this calendar year at the latest.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin and the forex hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Better spreads and robust demand drove margin; some small provisions held it back. The forex loss was a notional mark-to-market on unshipped and unreceived items at the all-time-high dollar on 31 March, expected to reverse if the rupee does not weaken further. Management said it books sales the same day and holds no open risk.

Management said the margin is elevated, expects the next two quarters to stay around these levels, and expects longer-term margins near 15% after the Odisha plant. The solar project started commercial operations late in the prior quarter (about 10 days of contribution) and is guided to save about INR15 crore a year, with the full 90 days flowing from the current month.

Solar project commissioned and operating; expected to cut annual power cost by 12-15%.
demand_pricing: Management said demand from all markets remains healthy and expects festive-season support domestically.

Order book kept at 70-90 days, similar to end of last quarter.
Cotton prices rose about 10-11% over the last quarter; management says most purchases were made about 3 months earlier and that Q2 should be similar to or better than Q1.
India-UK FTA signed last month, but no orders yet; management expects 6-9 months for orders to reflect in the order book.

539300|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 120.64% YoY to INR276.33 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 8.18% on raw-material and crude-linked cost pressure.
539300|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR276.33 crores, up 120.64% YoY and 39.85% QoQ, with PAT of INR15.04 crores (up 130.67% YoY). EBITDA rose 94.41% YoY to INR22.59 crores, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 8.18% from 9.28% a year earlier and 10.19% in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the margin squeeze to dyes, chemicals, boiler fuel, LABSA and PP packaging costs linked to geopolitical crude volatility, which hit the textile business hardest. 539301|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.
539301|2026-03.overview: Arvind SmartSpaces reported record FY26 bookings of INR1,550 crore, up 22% YoY, with Q4 bookings crossing INR600 crore for the first time. Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

Forest Trails (Bengaluru row houses/villas) site experience and show villa expected ready in 3-4 months; sales activation to restart in FY27.
HDFC platform of INR600 crore, of which INR350 crore used; the balance is being backfilled as available-on-call lines for any product type.
Three HDFC-linked Bengaluru projects use OCD structures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity investment behind FY26 BD and the FY27 BD guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 BD was about INR3,200 crore with investing outflow of about INR600 crore; FY27 BD lock-in target is INR4,000-5,000 crore. Project-wise capital breakup not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the OCF as a percentage of collections stay at 36-37%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to converge to the 22-25% EBITDA margin profile over time; for the next few years it could be 25-30%, helped by plotted projects and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% conservative given launch timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch pipeline is weighted to H2, with the Ahmedabad project possibly in H1; approval slippage is a risk, but management is reasonably sure of timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be held given rising costs from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 22-25% margins on new sales; a short commodity spike of a quarter or so can be absorbed within budgeted contingency.

qa_highlights.answer: JV with Oxford Sigma on a MHADA redevelopment; Arvind has a 44% profit share, and the partner handles site management and approvals, with Arvind leading development, sales and construction.

539301|2026-06.headline: Arvind SmartSpaces Q1 FY27 presales rose 147% YoY to INR432 crores; PAT jumped to INR97 crores on Orchards Phase 1 BU receipt.
539301|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR432 crores grew 147% YoY, with management attributing it to both Aqua City demand and broader core-market strength. Revenue rose to INR318 crores from INR102 crores and adjusted EBITDA to INR150 crores from INR25 crores, mainly from Orchards Phase 1 in Bengaluru receiving BU. Collections grew 76% to INR336 crores and net operating cash flow was INR81 crores. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 35-40% bookings growth, INR4,000-5,000 crores BD and 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales, and India Ratings upgraded the company to AA- (stable).

segments.name: Ahmedabad (Aqua City, horizontal)
segments.commentary: Aqua City named as standout booking performer in Q1; new Vastrapur project planned for launch this year. Management cites leadership in horizontal development in Ahmedabad.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Orchards Phase 1 BU received, driving the quarter's revenue and profit step-up; Bengaluru stock close to INR3,000 crores. Three launches planned this year, including Sarjapur, which has approvals.

segments.name: Mumbai / MMR
segments.commentary: Mumbai stock of INR4,000 crores-plus GDV; two Goregaon redevelopment-related and BD additions. Goregaon saleable carpet area about 6.7 lakh sq ft, 35-floor-plus, about 4 years to complete; 2 Mumbai launches planned this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% over FY26, implying about INR2,100-2,200 crores (per Q&A).
FY27 business development of INR4,000-5,000 crores GDV; INR2,600 crores already added in Q1; management leaning to upper band.
EBITDA margin on new sales of 22-25%; management says portfolio average about 25%, JD projects at lower end and outright at higher end.
FY27 operating cash flow target of INR400-500 crores (FY26 about INR400 crores).
Launch pipeline of about INR3,000-3,500 crores booking value across 6 projects (Ahmedabad 1, Bengaluru 3, Mumbai 2) this year.
Land outflow for FY27 of about INR600-900 crores (Q&A), with 4-5 year realisation of INR5,100 crores operating cash flow from existing portfolio.
Management did not give revenue guidance; expects strong YoY growth in FY27 revenue but timing depends on OC receipts, some lined up in Q4.
Medium-term 25-30% CAGR target over 4-5 years; comfort debt-to-equity at 1:1.
capex_capacity: Unrecognised revenue of INR3,825 crores to be recognised over about 4 years: plotted projects 2-3 years, high-rise OC in about 4 years.
Existing portfolio operating cash flow of over INR5,100 crores expected over next 4-5 years.
Construction spend ramped up in Q1; management says larger incremental outflow is construction cost.
Goregaon redevelopment: 200-plus units to be handed to existing members; area for members not yet disclosed.
Pen Khopoli project in Mumbai awaiting approvals; company hopes to launch at least 2 of 3 Mumbai projects this year.
demand_pricing: Management says underlying demand is strong; Aqua City plus broader core-market strength drove bookings.
Sustenance sales improved through sales team build-out across 3 cities, channel partner and marketing reach; sustenance may exceed plan.
Price increases expected to moderate after 3-4 years of strong appreciation; company does not underwrite large price hikes.
Bengaluru price uplift giving better margins on some older projects.
Management sees Mumbai, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad each delivering 22-25% EBITDA; no Tier 2 plans for now.
Management sees annual residential absorption of INR3-4 lakh crores across the three focus markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aqua City-driven booking strength project-specific or indicative of underlying demand in Gujarat and Bengaluru?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination of both; the market is strong and stable and responding well to most projects, and underlying demand remains quite strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the unrecognised revenue conversion and normalised margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 margin was boosted by Orchards BU; the 25% portfolio average is the base case. Revenue recognition is OC-linked and lumpy, so no annual revenue guidance is given.

qa_highlights.question: How is OCF flattening and what is FY27 OCF guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 OCF was about INR400 crores; FY27 target INR400-500 crores. Q1 OCF of INR81 crores reflects higher construction outflow, which management views as positive catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and leverage comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity at 0.29x; management comfortable up to 1:1 and expects gradual debt increase, funded by OCF and debt lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will BD of INR600-1,000 crores be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR400 crores from operating cash flow plus debt headroom; BD cash deployment guided at INR600-1,000 crores in the year (land outflow INR600-900 crores per earlier answer).

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for an annuity or commercial portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Not today; management is considering it after a few years, starting with for-sale assets to test development before holding assets.

risks_watch: Revenue and margin are lumpy and dependent on OC timing, with some OCs lined up in Q4; the Q1 margin of about 48-49% is well above the 25% portfolio average.
Net debt to equity rising from prior level to 0.29x as BD accelerates; management's comfort threshold is 1:1.
Launch execution: 6 launches worth INR3,000-3,500 crores this year depend on approvals, including Pen Khopoli.
Labour and construction cost inflation is gradual per management but may pressure margins.
Guidance inconsistency: BD cash deployment quoted as INR600-900 crores in one answer and INR600-1,000 crores in another.

539302|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR 2,121 crore, while FY26 order inflow of ~INR 7,210 crore missed the INR 10,000 crore target by about 28%.
539302|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total revenue was INR 2,121 crore (+13% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 237 crore (+2% YoY, margin 11.17%) and PAT of INR 153 crore (+18%). FY26 revenue was INR 6,107 crore (+16%), EBITDA INR 750 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT INR 412 crore (+18%). Order inflow missed guidance after cancellation of a INR 1,563 crore BESS order by the West Bengal electricity department, and the water division faced certification delays. Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, order inflow of about INR 12,000 crore and EBITDA margin of about 12.5%.

segments.name: Power vs non-power mix
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 57% power and 43% non-power; FY26 was 64% power and 36% non-power. Backlog is about 70% power and 30% non-power.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue was 94% domestic and 6% international; FY26 was 95% domestic and 5% international. International work is mainly O&M and manpower supply (Middle East, Nigeria), with international revenue of INR 327 crore in FY26 versus INR 292 crore in FY25.

segments.name: MDO (mining, KBP and SAIL/Tasra)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 MDO revenue was INR 226 crore, including INR 117 crore in March. Management targets INR 500 crore in FY27 and INR 1,250 crore in FY28, with EBITDA margin of about 15% now rising toward 20% at peak rated capacity (FY29-30).

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: O&M is the highest-margin business at about 15-16% EBITDA. Management cites O&M order growth of about 8% and about 4,100 MW of O&M orders in FY26, including a INR 279 crore Mumbai Monorail/metro O&M contract.

segments.name: EPC / civil
segments.commentary: Construction margins are below 8-10%. The BOP EPC order for the 800 MW Singareni project from BHEL is about INR 2,550 crore. Electrical transmission work has ended and was moved into civil.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 21%, which management says it is confident of achieving.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR 12,000 crore, mainly BOP EPC and O&M; FY28 target INR 12,000-15,000 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% including other income, up 0.25-0.3 percentage points.
MDO revenue targets: about INR 500 crore in FY27 (KBP INR 350 crore, Tasra/SAIL INR 150 crore), INR 1,250 crore in FY28, and about INR 2,100-2,200 crore at full capacity in FY29-30.
Blended EBITDA is guided to rise about 0.5% a year to 14% by FY30 and about 14.25% in FY31.
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore at Power Mech level (washery) and about INR 400 crore at the Tasra SPV, without debt.
capex_capacity: KBP mine (Kurmitar area) began production in November 2025; the client is lifting above contract capacity, and FY26 offtake was about 1.6 million tonnes.
Tasra washery construction should finish by December 2026, with washed coal from Q4 FY27 and Tasra production from mid Q4 FY27. Management says the Tasra ramp-up reaches peak rated capacity in FY29.
Target full capacity: KBP about 5 million tonnes by FY30; SAIL/Tasra about 4 million tonnes by FY29.
Current metro O&M covers about 1,095 operational km in India, expected to reach 2,000 km; Mumbai light rail O&M covers 15 stations.
Annual power commissioning is expected to reach about 8,000 MW a year, which management sees as driving installation, civil and O&M demand.
demand_pricing: Management identified about INR 70,000 crore of opportunities for FY27 across power, non-power, metro O&M and EPC. Its past bidding is about INR 40,000-50,000 crore at a hit ratio of about 15%.
BOP opportunities worth about INR 15,000 crore are being bid for 2-3 projects, with a target of one more BOP win in FY27.
Pricing is the main constraint on BHEL packages; management says BHEL is changing its packaging approach.
Named opportunities: BALCO O&M about INR 1,500 crore, Butibori O&M about INR 700 crore, and NMDC EPC tenders worth about INR 8,000-10,000 crore with Thyssenkrupp as partner.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value remains, with about INR 128 crore of work awaiting certification and INR 90 crore receivable. Management has stopped new water bids.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 10,000 crore order target missed, and is FY27 better?
qa_highlights.answer: The miss was mainly the INR 1,563 crore West Bengal BESS cancellation. Management expects West Bengal to re-tender, and says Bangalore Metro and Monorail (L1 in April) support about INR 10,000 crore; FY27 target is INR 12,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook given water division delays and labour code?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 EBITDA of about 12.5%, up 0.25-0.3 points, helped by more O&M and EPC mix. The Labour Code gratuity provision in Q4 was about INR 4.5 crore for the full-year impact.

qa_highlights.question: Do escalation clauses protect margins against commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic contracts carry PVC/escalation clauses that are billed to clients. International business is mainly O&M manpower, so impact is limited; the 1.2-1.5% of international order book is largely O&M.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MDO FY28 cut from INR 1,800-1,900 crore to INR 1,250 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The KBP washery is not ready on the CCL side, so offtake is conservatively put at INR 350 crore in FY27. The SAIL/Tasra ramp from zero to 4 million tonnes in one year is treated as a challenge, so FY28 is INR 750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MDO margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is about 15% at present, and management expects about 1 percentage point a year, reaching 20%-21% at peak rated capacity around FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Are there labour shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is above 40,000, with 70-75% in labour roles and about 18,000 in O&M. Management says construction and installation labour is the constraint, but schedules have been met so far.

risks_watch: Order inflow execution: FY26 missed by about 28%, and the FY27 target of INR 12,000 crore depends on BOP wins against BHEL's changed packaging approach and pricing.
Water division: about INR 900 crore of contract value is stalled pending central and state fund release, and certification delays weigh on margins.
MDO ramp-up: KBP and Tasra volumes depend on client offtake, the CCL washery, and the rainy season. The FY27 MDO target (INR 500 crore) is well above the Q4 monthly run-rate once March is excluded.
Commodity and labour inflation: steel, cement and diesel prices have risen. Recovery relies on PVC clauses, and labour availability is a constraint.
Management's 1-point-a-year margin expansion in MDO and blended EBITDA targets rest on O&M and EPC mix shifts.
539302|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and bullish on long-term power and O&M demand, but cautious on near-term order inflow and the water division. Management was explicit about the BESS cancellation and the MDO timing shortfall, and gave specific numbers on most questions. Some answers on segment figures and MDO revenue were revised during the call, which weakens the precision of the guidance.
key_quotes: Otherwise, our numbers would have been much better in order backlog.
Of course, on the BOP side, we are going to bid for two- three projects, that's worth INR 15000 crores.
We are confident of achieving that, and even the MDO business ramp -up of production is happening, and we are more focused on the high -margin O&M business.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin of about 12.5% incl. other income, up 0.25-0.3 pts from 12.3% in FY26, helped by O&M and EPC mix, with MDO margin (about 15%) expected to rise about 1 pt a year toward 20-21% at peak capacity.
